e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.title: Clipboard copy on Linux appends fix-it hint when only OSC 52 worked
e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.summary: In `copyTextToClipboard` within `cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts`, when a local Linux session falls back to OSC 52 after no platform clipboard tool succeeds, Freebuff now appends the new `LINUX_OSC52_ONLY_HINT` to the plain 'Copied' message and holds the toast for 6000ms. OSC 52 is fire-and-forget, so a bare 'Copied' on Linux (where a Chromebook terminal ships with neither `wl-copy` nor `xclip`) can falsely claim success; the hint tells users to install `wl-clipboard` or `xclip` if the paste is empty. Native-tool copies on Linux still show the unchanged plain message, per the added tests.
e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.evidence: The diff in `cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts` adds the exported constant `LINUX_OSC52_ONLY_HINT` and appends it to the success message inside `copyTextToClipboard` when `process.platform === 'linux'` and no native clipboard tool succeeded, extending the displayed duration to 6000ms. New tests assert the behavior for 'a copy that only reached the terminal says so and how to fix it' and 'a native tool copy keeps the plain message'.
e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.migration: No migration required; this changes only the on-screen clipboard confirmation message on Linux when no native clipboard tool is available.

e27f00b1a1bc6baa8deb5600bf98fd70d627d1d1.text: When you tell the assistant to copy some text on Linux and your computer doesn't have the usual copy tools installed, you used to just see a generic 'Copied' message even though the text may not have actually been copied. Now you see that message plus a note explaining that the copy went through the terminal instead, and suggesting you install the missing tool if pasting doesn't work. The note also stays visible a little longer so you have time to read it. This only affects Linux users copying text without the standard clipboard utilities, and nothing changes for everyone else.

baffcb89339ea373a63aa77202bec34e76f80444.text: This release widens access to two premium AI models, lets sponsored assistant runs play safely with your terminal without touching risky commands or your own Linux environment, and makes the in-place sponsored run behave like a one-job task instead of resuming your half-finished work, with a few small fixes along the way. First, GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now open to everyone, dropping to plan-only lockout only for users still on the limited free tier. Second, when an advertiser-sponsored run needs to run shell commands, the assistant now refuses to execute WSL launches, destructive database commands like drop or reset, and container lifecycle commands that could affect your live services, answering with a plain sentence instead of running them. Third, the prompt shown during these in-place sponsored runs now states that following the approved procedure is the only goal of the turn and treats your recent messages as read-only background, preventing the run from getting pulled back into your last incomplete request. Fourth, a small fix for Linux users: when copying text to the clipboard falls back to the OSC 52 method because no native clipboard tool is available, the success message now adds a hint telling you to install wl-clipboard or xclip if your paste comes up empty. Upgrading means safer, more predictable sponsored runs on your project, the ability to pick GPT-6 Luna or MiMo 2.6 Pro without a waitlist if you are past the limited free tier, and a clearer clipboard success message on Linux setups that lack a native clipboard tool.

9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.title: Partner placement format added to freebuff placements
9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.summary: The 'partner' format is now an explicit entry in PLACEMENT_FORMATS, and SPONSOR_BREAK_FORMATS is a named list excluding 'partner' so adding a new format cannot silently make it a sponsor break. Two partner slots, Desktop-Partner-Skill-Picker and Desktop-Partner-Composer-PR, are added to PLACEMENT_SLOTS with available set to false, marking them as single-advertiser chrome that the campaign-builder picker cannot target. New exports isPartnerFormat, isPartnerPlacement, and PARTNER_PLACEMENT_IDS support partner-specific serving, and PLACEMENT_FORMAT_LABELS adds surface-based labels for the partner slots.
9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.evidence: In common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts, PLACEMENT_FORMATS now lists 'partner' explicitly; SPONSOR_BREAK_FORMATS is rewritten as a named array of 'showcase', 'spotlight', 'intermission' instead of deriving from PLACEMENT_FORMATS, so adding 'partner' no longer makes it a sponsor break by default. New exports isPartnerFormat, isPartnerPlacement, and PARTNER_PLACEMENT_IDS are added, and two slots (Desktop-Partner-Skill-Picker, Desktop-Partner-Composer-PR) are added to PLACEMENT_SLOTS with available: false and format 'partner'. PLACEMENT_FORMAT_LABELS gains labels for the two partner slots instead of relying on the hyphen-splitter.
9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.migration: If you relied on the prior behavior of a placement inheriting sponsor-break rules when its format was added to PLACEMENT_FORMATS, you must now classify partner formats explicitly using isPartnerFormat.
9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.unknowns: The consumer of the new isPartnerFormat and PARTNER_PLACEMENT_IDS symbols outside this file is not shown in the diff.

9e3fdf7603a276e2559d229d347fcaa976740d7a.text: Freebuff added a new 'partner' ad slot type to its advertising system, explicitly separate from sponsor breaks, so it won't accidentally inherit break-style rules. Two new desktop partner slots (in the skill picker and composer PR area) are marked as exclusive single-advertiser slots and cannot be targeted through the self-serve console. This change is internal to Freebuff's ad placement configuration and is in place but does nothing visible yet, since advertisers are not targeting these slots and no consumer behavior depends on them. You, as a Freebuff user, will not see any change in how the assistant works or what ads appear.

a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.title: Resume legacy pre-multi-session hour on cross-protocol restart
a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.summary: The CLI now records an optional `tokenKey` alongside the local `freebuff-instance-owner.json` record and exposes `deadLegacyFreebuffOwner` to detect a stale pre-multi-session hour left by a dead earlier binary. `useFreebuffSession` probes that legacy instance on the first tick, resumes it on the same expiry when this account still holds it active, and otherwise falls back to an ordinary `cli:` claim. The `restart` closure and fetch-error path both drop the legacy probe on any end, switch, rejoin, or unanswered adoption so no second hour is bought.
a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.evidence: `cli/src/utils/freebuff-instance-owner.ts` adds the `deadLegacyFreebuffOwner` and `forgetFreebuffInstanceOwner` exports, plus an optional `tokenKey` field written via a `token` parameter on `recordFreebuffInstanceOwner`; `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` imports both and wires a `legacyProbe`/`legacyHour` flow through `tick`, the startup-takeover branch, the `restart` closure, and the fetch-error handler
a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

a78f5290258b53013a16fefea0715f6d74f445f0.text: When an older Freebuff install quietly left a billing-hour open before the app was replaced by a newer build, this update recognizes that prior session so Freebuff picks it up rather than paying again. It applies to Freebuff's free ad-funded CLI and apps, not paid Codebuff subscriptions. For you it just means you no longer get prompted for a new session or charged again when restarting the app after this specific cross-version upgrade. No setup is required.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.201
f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package version advances from 0.0.200 to 0.0.201 in freebuff/cli/release/package.json. This is a routine release-bump commit with a +1/-1 diff against the packaging artifact for the free tier CLI distribution.
f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.evidence: In freebuff/cli/release/package.json, the "version" field changes from "0.0.200" to "0.0.201".
f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.unknowns: The diff does not show what functional or model changes are included in this release, so the consumer-facing impact of 0.0.201 is not visible.

f783139ae5607e7b53e6dd5608186d133930d7bd.text: Freebuff 0.0.201 adds a new ad slot type for partners and fixes session resuming after restarting the CLI. The partner ad format is now a recognized option in the ad system, with two reserved slots that advertisers can use, and the code that decides which ads are sponsor breaks is now safer so adding new formats won't accidentally promote an ad into the wrong place. When you close and reopen Freebuff, it now correctly picks up your previous session hour instead of starting over, as long as your account still has that hour active, and if that old session is gone it cleanly starts a fresh one without leaving a stale session running in the background. Upgrading gives you uninterrupted sessions when restarting the assistant and lays the groundwork for partner-sponsored features without changing your daily workflow.

06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.title: Codebuff own-credits 402 no longer treated as a Freebuff provider
06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.summary: isFreebuffProviderUsageError now short-circuits to false when the error message matches CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN (/codebuff\.com\/usage/i), so Codebuff's own out-of-credits 402 reaches the ordinary out-of-credits flow instead of being misreported as a Freebuff provider problem. This fixes a regression in CLI lite mode where a paying user running out of Codebuff balance was told the failure was "on us, not your account". The change touches only error-classification plumbing in the CLI and the shared constant it depends on.
06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.evidence: cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts adds CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN to the import and uses it inside isFreebuffProviderUsageError; common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts defines CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN as /codebuff\.com\/usage/i with a doc comment explaining it targets Codebuff's own 402 out-of-credits message.
06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.unknowns: The change is wired into isFreebuffProviderUsageError but no reader of CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN beyond that single short-circuit is shown in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: isFreebuffProviderUsageError now returns false when the parsed error message matches CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN before checking provider usage patterns.
Adds the export CODEBUFF_OWN_CREDITS_ERROR_PATTERN (/codebuff\.com\/usage/i) to distinguish Codebuff's own 402 out-of-credits messages from real provider billing failures.

06bf5c3390a40a61f96676cd94fdedbb04552956.text: The assistant now correctly tells paying users when their own Codebuff balance (not the free service's provider credits) has run out. This affects users running Codebuff in CLI lite mode, especially paying users who hit a 402 error. Previously, these users saw a message saying the problem was on Freebuff's side and were pointed to Freebuff's credit-purchase flow instead of Codebuff's; now they are sent to the correct out-of-credits flow for their paid account.

dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.202 published
dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.summary: The Freebuff CLI package.json version was bumped from 0.0.201 to 0.0.202 as a release-bump commit. The diff touches only the version string in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, with no code, manifest, or dependency changes accompanying it. This packages the 0.0.202 release line of the freebuff (0.0.x) CLI alongside the codebuff (1.0.x) line.
dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.evidence: The diff for `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes only the `version` field from `"0.0.201"` to `"0.0.202"`; analysis notes confirm Freebuff CLI release 0.0.202 was published.
dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.unknowns: The diff does not show what user-facing changes, if any, ship in 0.0.202 beyond the version bump.

dbc6a776fc0f8005806d797c00fe2c6caf1781c6.text: This Freebuff CLI release fixes a misleading error message that was shown to paying Codebuff users. When a paying user runs out of Codebuff credits, the CLI was incorrectly reporting the issue as a Freebuff provider problem, which confused users into thinking the failure was on Freebuff's side rather than their own account balance. The update corrects this error classification so that Codebuff's own out-of-credits situation is properly routed through the standard out-of-credits flow, ensuring paying users receive accurate messaging about their account status instead of being told the problem is with the service provider. Upgrading to this version means you will see the correct error message when your Codebuff credits run out, without any misleading attribution of the failure to Freebuff's infrastructure.

24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.title: SDK truncates history by USER PROMPT turns and elides large base64
24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.summary: The SDK's truncateRunStateAtUserTurn now counts only USER_PROMPT-tagged messages and can place the rewind boundary from the end via the new totalUserTurns parameter, fixing edits that over-trimmed compacted or stopped threads. In agent-runtime, compactWithModel serializes tool results with elideBinaryStrings, which names data URLs and long base64 runs as omitted text instead of feeding them to the summarizer
24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts adds elideBinaryStrings and omittedBinary and changes the message content mapping to name base64 media payloads instead of serializing them, and sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts adds totalUserTurns to truncateRunStateAtUserTurn and restricts the user-turn count to USER_PROMPT-tagged messages
24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.unknowns: The diff does not show which host consumer drives the totalUserTurns call or the rollout timing of the Desktop fix referenced in comments. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: compaction now names large base64 and data URL payloads instead of serializing them into the summarizer request
truncateRunStateAtUserTurn matches USER_PROMPT tags and supports counting the rewind boundary from the end via totalUserTurns

24636b016b85a8983dd35c208e1cd569e6eb2fca.text: The assistant now remembers which parts of your conversation were actually your questions to it rather than its own notes to itself, so edits no longer wipe out the wrong stretch of chat. It also strips out giant hidden image and base64 data that a single screenshot-heavy session could otherwise balloon into, preventing timeouts on long conversations. This is a reliability fix that ships in the current build, so you can keep editing mid-thread without watching your history disappear or the app stall on large attachments.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.203 published
a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.summary: The packaging manifest at freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumps the version field from 0.0.202 to 0.0.203, publishing the next 0.0.x release of the free-tier coding agent. This is a packaging-only version bump with no source code changes, updating the bin entry, file list, engine constraints, and OS/CPU targets for the published CLI artifact. The change marks Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 as the latest release in the 0.0.x line.
a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.evidence: In freebuff/cli/release/package.json, the version field of the freebuff package manifest is incremented from 0.0.202 to 0.0.203 in the published release artifact.

a23f0ae16d9c7d69458dce20ca74178bc530ffb8.text: Freebuff CLI version 0.0.203 is now available as a packaging release that bundles recent updates into one installable version. The SDK now truncates conversation history more accurately, counting only your actual prompts instead of every internal message, so long sessions stay trimmed without cutting off important context. When the assistant summarizes earlier parts of a conversation to save space, tool results that contain large chunks of encoded text or data are now labeled as omitted rather than being fed through the summarizer, keeping those summaries focused and readable. Upgrading gives you a more predictable experience when working on large or multi-step tasks, since the assistant will now handle very long conversations and messy tool outputs without them interfering with its summaries.

cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.title: Fatal crash reports ship to analytics on next launch
cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.summary: A fatal exit (uncaught exception or unhandled rejection) now writes a bounded crash report synchronously to disk before the process ends, and the next launch reads it back and ships it as the `cli.fatal_crash` analytics event. The report is capped at the error name, the first 300 characters of the message, the first 20 stack frames, plus version, platform, architecture and uptime, and reports older than seven days are dropped as stale evidence. Telemetry shipping is wrapped in a try block so a logging failure can never block a launch.
cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts` defines constants like `REPORT_FILE`, `MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS`, `MAX_STACK_FRAMES`, and exports `recordFatalCrashSync`, `takePreviousFatalCrash`, `buildFatalCrashReport`, and `FatalCrashReport`; `cli/src/index.tsx` calls `takePreviousFatalCrash()` at launch and tracks the result as `AnalyticsEvent.CLI_FATAL_CRASH`; `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` calls `recordFatalCrashSync` during `exitCliWithFatalError`.

changes.what: Added a new module that builds, records, and reads back a bounded fatal crash report for the next launch to ship.
Calls `takePreviousFatalCrash()` at startup and tracks the result as `AnalyticsEvent.CLI_FATAL_CRASH`.
Calls `recordFatalCrashSync` inside `exitCliWithFatalError` so a crash leaves a report before teardown.
Added the `CLI_FATAL_CRASH` analytics event constant.
Added `CLI_FATAL_CRASH` to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` so crash counts per version stay whole.

cb1dc4f15b6aec59f80dfac74c06d1427e76ec4e.text: When the coding assistant crashes unexpectedly (for example from an uncaught error or a rejected promise that was not handled), it now saves a small crash report to disk before shutting down and sends that report to analytics the next time it starts up, as a fatal_crash event. This affects end users of the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app or SDK, since the crash is still recorded best-effort and never blocks the next launch. In daily use, you should not notice anything different except that crashes now produce a single, deduplicated report instead of leaving no trace, so the team can see when and why the app exited unexpectedly.

38cd1ed44428f573c4754d8e0cee868f2875b54e.text: The Freebuff engineering team released version 0.0.204 of the Freebuff CLI, which is an internal maintenance update that keeps the terminal coding assistant current. This release includes several behind-the-scenes improvements: the CLI now better handles copying text to the clipboard on Linux systems, sponsored project runs (where advertisers fund real coding tasks) now refuse to run in WSL or execute destructive commands, and the CLI can resume a previous paid coding session after restarting. The main user-facing benefit is that sponsored coding runs can now declare and use their own temporary credentials for each task, making those funded projects more secure.

2abe8724f6320e633a07d1cb04090f2c0fd58a41.title: CLI partner ad rows above input and under /review
2abe8724f6320e633a07d1cb04090f2c0fd58a41.summary: Adds first-party partner ad rows to the Freebuff CLI: one branded line above the composer input when the draft mentions pull requests, and one under /review in the slash menu. Partner auctions are gated by resolveAdPolicy, held per account for PARTNER_AD_TTL_MS (30 minutes), deduped via an in-flight map, and rendered by PartnerAdLine using layout from common/src/ads/inline-ad-layout.ts; ads are dropped entirely when the policy names nothing or fetch fails. The change touches CLI rendering in chat.tsx, chat-input-bar.tsx, suggestion-menu.tsx, and use-dock-panel.ts, the inline-ad-layout and freebuff-placements registry in common, plus four new modules across cli/src/ads, cli/src/components, and common/src/ads.

2abe8724f6320e633a07d1cb04090f2c0fd58a41.text: A new kind of small, single-line ad now appears in the Freebuff command-line tool: one branded line shows just above where you type a message when your draft mentions a pull request, and another appears directly under the /review command in the slash menu. Nothing is added to your message or your work; the line simply sits next to the feature it relates to and disappears when you start typing again.

Edited instructionsPrompt to note that web research per message is capped and the user should answer from existing results when a researcher reports the limit was reached.
Documented a flake case where a polling assertion sampled the middle of backgrounded work before its async rm resolved, recommending awaiting the work itself via EngineRegistry backgroundSettled().

No setup is needed on your end; the limit is in place and active today.

e4a960f781aeb3023a406e4990b741212d0cafce.title: Freebuff 0.1.0 release raises database snapshot threshold tenfold
e4a960f781aeb3023a406e4990b741212d0cafce.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.1.0 is published, advancing the version in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` from 0.0.204 to 0.1.0. e4a960f781aeb3023a406e4990b741212d0cafce.text: Freebuff has published version 0.1.0 of its command line tool, which adjusts an internal database monitoring rule that the Freebuff team itself manages. The team raised the rule's trigger point from one million to ten million so routine scheduled work no longer sets off false alarms while still catching the kind of prolonged lockup that caused a previous incident. This only affects whoever runs Freebuff's service; everyday users of the public assistant do not need to do anything.

a99e5b771f53b678fcaf6ac889cc57487dd22a62.title: Docs/testing.md clarifies flake-hunt desktop Bun pinning

3e7db03d51d7fadf954a6daaee87949e67782596.title: Testing docs document Vite port 0 fallback and cache Dir sharing
3e7db03d51d7fadf954a6daaee87949e67782596.summary: docs/testing.md adds guidance that Vite's server.listen() reads `port: 0` as unset and binds 5173, and that `strictPort` makes it exit before listening if another process holds the port, so terminal.test.ts now calls `server.httpServer.listen(0)` itself and passes Vite a per-run `cacheDir` since the deps optimizer otherwise writes into the package's shared `node_modules/.vite`. A test reporting a child's death should carry its stderr and exit status, since the failing run read Vite exited before listening: with nothing after the colon because the child's stderr was piped and never read.

0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.title: Validate time zone before formatting in window label helpers
0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.summary: Added `isSupportedTimeZone` and rewrote `resolveWindowTimeZone` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` so the resolved zone is validated via `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` before use, falling back to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') when the runtime cannot format in it. The module comment cites 25 Cloud page crashes through 2026-09-26 caused by `Intl.DateTimeFormat` throwing a RangeError on a browser-reported zone the runtime then rejected, including from a PlayStation 5 browser and a Windows Chrome. `resolveWindowTimeZone` now returns the explicit or runtime-reported zone only when `isSupportedTimeZone` confirms it, otherwise UTC.
0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.evidence: Added `isSupportedTimeZone` and rewrote `resolveWindowTimeZone` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts`; the new function tests a zone by constructing `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone })` and resolving falls back to `FALLBACK_WINDOW_TIME_ZONE` ('UTC') when `isSupportedTimeZone` returns false. The module comment cites 25 Cloud page crashes through 2026-09-26 caused by `Intl.DateTimeFormat` throwing a RangeError on a browser-reported zone the runtime then rejected.

0fce93281ac8d26b2e7a391bbcd5c36cffa5ade0.text: Time zone handling has been made more robust so that invalid or unrecognized time zone names no longer cause the assistant's interface to crash, but instead quietly fall back to showing times in UTC. This affects you if you're using the assistant's command-line tools, web app, or desktop app, especially in situations where your device reports a time zone your system doesn't fully understand (such as certain consoles or older browsers). You will not notice any deliberate difference in behavior, but instead of encountering a broken or frozen clock-related display, the times you see will simply default to UTC rather than crashing the interface. This fix is live today and prevents rare crashes that previously occurred when the assistant tried to display time-zone-sensitive information.

9aff81261042e68a800732cc467a8d94fd394ae3.title: Log data serializer now converts Error objects to structured JSON
9aff81261042e68a800732cc467a8d94fd394ae3.summary: `serializeLogData` in `common/src/util/log-data.ts` now detects Error instances during JSON stringification and replaces them with the output of `errorToJson`, which preserves `name`, `message`, `cause`, and a `stack` truncated to `MAX_ERROR_STACK_CHARS = 2_000`. The replacer previously returned Error objects unchanged, so `JSON.stringify(error)` produced `{}` and error rows reached Axiom with no reason attached. Enumerable library fields such as `code` and `status` are still kept, and the same circular-reference guard applies.
9aff81261042e68a800732cc467a8d94fd394ae3.evidence: In `common/src/util/log-data.ts`, a new constant `MAX_ERROR_STACK_CHARS = 2_000` is defined, the function `errorToJson(error: Error)` is added to serialize Error `name`, `message`, truncated `stack`, and `cause`, and the `serializeLogData` replacer now calls if (v instanceof Error) return errorToJson(v).
9aff81261042e68a800732cc467a8d94fd394ae3.unknowns: The change adds a new serialization path and constant but the diff does not show which consumer introduced the failing error rows or why those rows were being logged at that volume.

9aff81261042e68a800732cc467a8d94fd394ae3.text: When something goes wrong inside the Freebuff service, the internal error details were being lost, leaving the team with empty records that showed failures happened but gave no clue why. The logging system now converts full error information, including the error message and relevant technical fields, into a readable format that preserves the useful parts while trimming overly long technical trace details. This is strictly internal work for the engineering team that operates Freebuff, so it does not change anything you see, tap, or pay for when using the assistant. No action is needed from you, and you will notice no difference in your sessions today.

1fa434c88f960a6c095e497aed6b93d9ca9f8197.title: Docs: update testing.md on idle tab marker ordering
1fa434c88f960a6c095e497aed6b93d9ca9f8197.summary: This commit updates `docs/testing.md` to correct the tense and add clarification around the ordering of the idle tab's `node_modules` marker removal. The text now reads that the strip removed the marker after its async `rm` resolved rather than removes, and notes that the marker currently goes first to fix a crash window. This is documentation only and describes test-harness flakiness around polling timing.

71741fc79de88ca49a02602fe2b124a35d6a7361.title: Show Discord invite banner after Freebuff sign-in
71741fc79de88ca49a02602fe2b124a35d6a7361.summary: Following a fresh Freebuff sign-in in `handleLoginSuccess` (`cli/src/hooks/use-auth-state.ts`), the CLI now activates a new `discord` top banner, which renders `DISCORD_AFTER_LOGIN_TEXT` and a clickable `FREEBUFF_DISCORD_INVITE_URL` link via `TOP_BANNER_REGISTRY` in `cli/src/components/top-banner.tsx`. The text and URL live in new shared constants `DISCORD_AFTER_LOGIN_TEXT`, `FREEBUFF_DISCORD_INVITE_URL`, and `FREEBUFF_DISCORD_MEMBERS_LABEL` (in `cli/src/login/discord-invite.ts` and `common/src/constants/freebuff-community.ts`), and the same line is printed by freebuff login --plain in `cli/src/login/plain-login.ts` so every post-login surface shows one headline. Restored sessions do not trigger the banner because only `handleLoginSuccess` sets it, after `resetChatStore()` clears prior banners. Raising the member count is a manual, in-whole-thousands edit to `FREEBUFF_DISCORD_MEMBERS_LABEL` rather than a live query.

71741fc79de88ca49a02602fe2b124a35d6a7361.text: Right after you sign in to the Freebuff CLI, you now see a friendly banner at the top of your terminal inviting you to join the Freebuff Discord community, with a clickable link that opens Discord for you. This only appears on a fresh sign-in (not when your session is restored from a previous one), and the same invitation message also prints in the plain-text login flow used for remote or SSH environments. It affects Freebuff users on the free tier, and the everyday impact is a new community invitation showing up once at the top of your chat after you log in.

c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.title: Fix OpenRouter to Anthropic model ID mapping for dotted version ids
c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.summary: The `OPENROUTER_TO_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP` in `common/src/constants/anthropic.ts` now includes explicit entries for `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` (`claude-sonnet-5`). The `toAnthropicModelId` fallback for unmapped ids rewrites OpenRouter's dotted versions to Anthropic's hyphenated form, so `claude-opus-5.5` no longer 404s at Anthropic's token-count endpoint because Anthropic does not accept dot-separated version numbers.
c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.evidence: In `common/src/constants/anthropic.ts`, `OPENROUTER_TO_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP` gains `'anthropic/claude-opus-5.5': 'claude-opus-5-5'` and `'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5': 'claude-sonnet-5'`, and the unmapped-id fallback in `toAnthropicModelId` changed from `openrouterModel.replace('anthropic/', '')` to `openrouterModel.replace('anthropic/', '').replaceAll('.', '-')` so OpenRouter's dotted versions are rewritten to Anthropic's hyphenated form.
c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.migration: No migration is required; existing callers of `toAnthropicModelId` automatically receive correctly hyphenated ids.

d86b11dbab81b4862d036cde60d4c2cfb523567e.title: CPU detail probing skips si.cpu() when os.cpus() throws
d86b11dbab81b4862d036cde60d4c2cfb523567e.summary: On the fingerprint path in `cli/src/utils/fingerprint.ts`, `canReadCpuDetails` now probes `cpus()[0]?.model` synchronously and, when that throws (for example Bun's lazy `os.cpus()` on Linux when /proc/stat and /proc/cpuinfo disagree, per CodebuffAI/freebuff#1374), `getSystemInfo` skips `systeminformation.cpu()` and resolves a CPU block with `cores: safeCpuCount(cpus)` and `physicalCores: 0`, logging the `cpu_info_unavailable` fingerprint type. `safeCpuCount` reads `cpus().length` and, on throw, falls back to `availableParallelism()`, returning `0` only when both throw, and `calculateFingerprint`'s runtime block now calls `safeCpuCount(cpus)` instead of `cpus().length`.
d86b11dbab81b4862d036cde60d4c2cfb523567e.evidence: The diff to `cli/src/utils/fingerprint.ts` adds the exported functions `canReadCpuDetails` and `getSystemInfo` (with the latter now accepting `{ load?, readCpus? }` options), introduces `safeCpuCount`, and replaces the previous `systeminformationModule.cpu()` call with a guarded branch that skips `si.cpu()` when `canReadCpuDetails(readCpus)` is false, falling back to `{ cores: safeCpuCount(readCpus), physicalCores: 0 }`. The JSDoc on `canReadCpuDetails` states Bun's `os.cpus()` is lazy and throws on Linux when /proc/stat and /proc/cpuinfo disagree (citing CodebuffAI/freebuff#1374), and the inline `logger.warn` uses the `fingerprintType: 'cpu_info_unavailable'` tag.
d86b11dbab81b4862d036cde60d4c2cfb523567e.unknowns: The rollout or user-facing frequency of the cpu_info_unavailable fingerprint type is not shown in the diff.

47605f76991c9d72442841160cd01722be08df3c.text: The Freebuff team trimmed overly long internal comments and documentation inside their shared codebase that tracks which prompts the free assistant is allowed to use. This is purely housekeeping for Freebuff's own engineers and has no effect on how the product behaves for anyone today.

6752415171bd7cfe97a2da2feb4418380357d4ee.text: Freebuff’s internal session code now has labels that can identify whether a session request comes from the Desktop app or the command-line app. This is for the Freebuff engineering team, and the labels are currently only prepared for future use. You will not notice any change in daily use, and no action is needed.

58699f0e07179ec3da47ddc01f58272ff7c6f565.title: House ad copy reframes usage as hours with tier name and total daily
58699f0e07179ec3da47ddc01f58272ff7c6f565.summary: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts`, three constants are introduced: `TIER_NAME` (the paid tier display name, defaulting to `Starter`), `FREE_PER_DAY` (from `FREEBUFF_FREE_TIER_ALLOWANCE.dailySessions`), and `TOTAL_PER_DAY` (the sum of `SESSIONS_PER_DAY` and `FREE_PER_DAY`). The inline creatives for `cli_chat`, `waiting_room`, `freebuff_web_chat`, and `chat_assistant` now lead with the plain title `Freebuff` and describe usage in hours a day instead of more sessions a day, and the `HOUSE_AD_DISPLAY_VARIATIONS` now compose titles like `Freebuff ${TIER_NAME}` and ad copy that combines the per-hour increment with the combined free plus paid allowance that `${TOTAL_PER_DAY}` already renders. The `chat_assistant_sr` and the `Desktop-Showcase` break creatives, which still read `Freebuff Pro`, are untouched, leaving the legacy wording in place for that surface.
58699f0e07179ec3da47ddc01f58272ff7c6f565.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts`, new constants `TIER_NAME = ENTRY_TIER?.displayName ??
