439c9e6c52fc1e267d29777147ff4f306f8c8077.text: The assistant no longer guesses how much conversation your model can hold at once. When you bring your own connection, the assistant now asks your model provider what its real size limit is, instead of assuming a small default that caused it to squeeze and re-summarize the whole conversation every few turns. If your provider doesn't report a size, the assistant uses a smarter 128k-token default (or 400k at most), so most coding conversations run without stopping to compress history. If your connection reports a window that's correct, the assistant trusts it and leaves it alone. This is live today for anyone running the assistant with a bring-your-own-connection setup.

d86b11dbab81b4862d036cde60d4c2cfb523567e.text: Released on September 27, 2026, Freebuff can complete its device identification for sign-in even when a computer refuses to provide detailed processor information. It affects Freebuff CLI users on those affected computers, while other users continue as before. You should not need to do anything, and the CLI should avoid failing during sign-in, although it may use less processor detail when identifying the device.

c71604de74656272d8721f0f33e0cfe031eb23cb.text: Freebuff now translates the names of newer Anthropic models into the spelling Anthropic accepts, including a fallback for model names that were not listed explicitly. This is an internal production change for the Freebuff engineering team that maintains model support. You do not need to change anything or expect a visible interface change, but token counting for these models no longer fails because of the name format.

538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.title: CLI restores arrow-key editing with open suggestion menus
538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.summary: The CLI now lets bare left, right, Up, and Down keys edit a non-empty draft while preserving Up/Down navigation for open slash and mention menus. The ordering in `resolveChatKeyboardAction` fixes menu scrolling after typing `/` or `@`, and `shouldInterceptChatInputKey` applies the same distinction at the input interception layer. `Ctrl+Q` remains ahead of the ctrl-c rules, so the queue editor works with a half-typed message when queued items exist.
538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.evidence: `cli/src/utils/chat-input-key-intercept.ts` removes the non-empty-draft arrow interception and lets open suggestion menus retain Up/Down handling. In `resolveChatKeyboardAction` in `cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts`, the bare-arrow `none` action now runs below slash and mention menu handling, while the queue editor remains at Priority 2.5.

48ad7f372029c76ef633a3fcb148a1601d110352.text: A maintainer added a new section to an internal project guide that explains how knowledge and best practices are collected and shared across the team. This is an internal documentation update that changes no behavior of the application. You will not see anything different in the terminal or in your chats. The change also adds a to-do noting they want to try a better way of comparing and applying changes in the future.

fb3e26bdf23087b7bb3f017afb39134eca8d6233.text: The monthly fee for Pro subscribers using more than their 10,000 credits just went up: overage now costs 90 cents per 100 extra credits, up from 50 cents. If you're on the Pro plan and you run past your monthly allowance, your next bill will reflect the higher rate. Nothing else about your service changes, you just pay more for the same extra usage.

24c16b3a2476eacf23a71b3a290d0a4305387027.text: The update process that upgrades Manicode now correctly displays the package manager it found before starting the upgrade, instead of showing a broken or missing installer name. This affects only people running the Manicode upgrade command from their terminal. If you already started the update today, you will now see an accurate installer name in the log and a slightly different sign-off message at the end of the process.

b59a8ab8c6bdd0625e2088c8ccc199a7b541dcd5.text: The referral page on the website was tidied up to make it easier to read. The link for referring more people was moved out of the main heading and placed next to where it shows how many people you’ve already referred, and some wording was adjusted to be friendlier - "Share this link with them" instead of "Send this link to them," and "people" instead of "friends," with the extra link now phrased as “(Wanna refer more?”). This is a small, live update to the referrals page, so anyone checking their referral status will just notice the layout and wording look slightly different; no action is needed and there’s no change to how many credits you earn or your referral limit.

42c28d63b9490ba5f63f5b1f616e7b8fd090d50d.text: The service now sends a record to the billing system every time you use it, so your usage gets counted up for the month, but only if you are signed in and have an active paid plan. This runs quietly in the background after your conversation is saved, so it does not slow things down or change how the assistant works. You won't see anything new or different; it just makes sure your usage is tracked correctly for billing.

ca0c95cf0318ef95b381c1d8b11ae04d7628e905.text: When you ask the coding assistant a question, you can now choose how much it spends to answer, with three settings: a budget option that uses a faster, cheaper model and gathers fewer reference files, a standard option using the default model, and a premium option using the highest-quality model and scanning more files. The budget setting also skips some extra steps where the assistant looks for example code and test files, so it works a little differently than the others. Anyone who can run the assistant on their computer can pick a setting by typing a command flag when starting it.

b2172514822c8405c13432c4393f6620ff737fe8.text: The assistant no longer automatically commits and pushes your changes after each message. Instead, when you run it with the new staging option, it quietly places the files from that message into your version-control queue so you can review and confirm them yourself before anything is saved. This affects people who use the assistant from the command line and rely on it to track their work through version control. In daily use, you will still get your code written, but you have to take one extra step if you want those changes recorded, giving you a chance to look over what is being committed.

c9b8dfc97959583230cdce6950a22860304cb6d3.text: The program now recognizes a specific shell error message that previously slipped through its detection, adding 'syntax error near unexpected token' to the list of phrases it treats as a failed command attempt. This affects only the internal command-handling logic and is not something you would need to do anything differently to use. You do not experience any visible change in daily use; the assistant simply handles one more edge case the same way it already handles others, keeping its behavior consistent.

71ac99f1290e565ed508f14b950cde4939967dae.text: The software's version number was updated to 1.0.161, which is an internal bookkeeping step tied to releasing the latest build to people who install the assistant from the official package registry. This is routine maintenance work that only affects how the published package is labeled and distributed, not any feature you use. You do not need to do anything, and you will not see any difference in how the assistant behaves.

0cbf99e28ed75d9c0eecb31c6319d33ff19870d3.text: The assistant now saves your progress to a separate worker so saving a checkpoint no longer freezes the screen you are working in. This is an internal change for people running the tool locally, so you will not see a new button or option appear. In daily use, the difference is that taking a checkpoint feels smoother because the heavy saving work happens in the background instead of on the main thread.

a3c2420addf103825f58187ff477c7aaf415b899.text: The filter that catches risky typing in the assistant now checks the first word of multi-word phrases instead of treating every command as a single word. This was changed in an internal check that decides which typed commands are allowed to run. You will not notice anything different; the assistant still works the same, and no action is needed from you.

54f4d6eee4331aafc0f7a5b5f02c850d16a40be7.text: The system replaced three separate, nearly identical test-running steps in its automated checkup routine with one step that loops over all three packages automatically, cutting out the duplication. This is internal-only tooling, so it does not change what you see in the app or how the assistant behaves for you. You will simply experience the usual flow of the app just as before, with no action or visible difference on your end.

984f285ad3bdb5661cf12436fc43830a7fe510d3.text: When you type a message to the assistant, the system behind the scenes now calls that action 'user input' instead of 'prompt sent' so it is easier to tell apart from the assistant's own thinking steps. This is an internal labeling change in the analytics that logs your messages, and the logging now only happens after the system has confirmed your identity. It does not change how the assistant responds or how fast it works. You will not notice anything different while using it today.

fd549691e1225ea3bc1950707b849b0660aef58a.text: Templates that describe an assistant's output format must now state plainly whether that output should be structured JSON. Previously, the system assumed JSON whenever a format was supplied; now it requires an explicit label, and rejects the template if the two settings conflict. This only affects people who build or edit these templates, so most users will not notice anything different.

2a564ae89f287d49c1639bf3038f84292f1028d3.text: The list of helper assistants that a main assistant is allowed to call in has been renamed from 'subagents' to 'spawnableAgents' in the project's configuration files. This affects people who write or edit agent configuration files by hand, such as custom assistant definitions. You will not see this change while using the software normally, but configuration files you create or modify must use the new name from now on.

0ed7999b5a74286322fb3a42554d848752671a0a.text: The assistant has been told to keep working on a task in one continuous stretch rather than stopping early to ask if you want more. This guidance only applies to how the assistant behaves during coding tasks that are run through the new GPT-5 setup, and it is already in effect for those sessions. In everyday use, you should notice the assistant trying to complete a whole task (such as writing or fixing code) before pausing to check in with you, instead of stopping after every small step.

68bf922740c07889ebec41c5baf8b20276eb4a45.text: A new helper called Lewis & Clark has been added to the master assistant so it can be dispatched to quickly look up facts in the codebase or on the web. The main editor helper now also has the ability to call on a dedicated web-research helper while working, and that research helper has been narrowed to only searching the web and reading documentation instead of poking around in code files. The master assistant and editor have also been given clearer instructions describing these new abilities. This is internal work that helps shape how the assistant coordinates its helpers, so you won't notice anything different the next time you ask it to do something.

5ec7760aec07feedd81c1296a32f2760a13e21ee.text: The way the assistant decides which files matter most when running low on memory got a small internal cleanup: the list of inputs it uses to pick the most important files is now passed in as a single grouped setting instead of several separate ones. This is purely behind-the-scenes work for the people who build and maintain the assistant, so it does not change how you use the assistant or what it can do for you today.

9651f9341bde3c4401207497630d7a0d75829e11.text: Debug log files now get saved inside a separate folder called 'debug' instead of being mixed in with other files, which keeps them organized and prevents them from cluttering the main directory. This only affects internal development and testing work. If you're a developer working on Freebuff, your debug logs will appear in a dedicated subfolder; otherwise, there is no visible effect or action needed for regular use.

9e226827a42b370975fde54a1ecf394e5e93c85c.text: The team that checks how well the coding assistant works added a new, faster version of its test helper that skips the final checking step and keeps its closing remarks very short. This change only affects the internal nightly checks the team runs to measure accuracy, not the assistant you talk to. Nothing you do in a normal session feels different today.

ed8123417d0efdc798db9c0b825982936b241ea0.text: After the assistant gives you a step-by-step plan, two buttons now appear: one labeled 'Build Fast' and one labeled 'Build Max'. Clicking either one switches the assistant to that speed setting and immediately starts the build using that plan. This only shows up for you when you are in Plan mode and only after the plan has fully finished loading.

146adf8a068a1ce7195e80c2e4bfb3c0c3ca2a3c.text: The terminal interface now builds its message-formatting settings once and reuses that same set of settings for every message, instead of rebuilding a fresh copy each time a message appears. This is purely an internal housekeeping change for the CLI application, so it does not affect any account, plan, region, or pricing tier. You will not notice anything different in daily use, and there is no action required from you. The change is live today.

d6111d5d918a09727fdc1734bf302be69d88d531.text: The base2-fast mode now resolves to z-ai/glm-4.6:nitro. This is an internal configuration change affecting which AI model is used during agent orchestration. There is no visible change for end users.

e30ce4b158dcceef309360bc44e4634770a375b6.text: This was a behind-the-scenes publishing step that repackaged the same AI assistant into a fresh download labeled with a new release number. The update bundles features already built, such as the assistant routing its step-by-step thinking into its live response stream and letting people bring their own model provider API key. If you already installed the earlier version, you probably noticed no missing pieces, and this bump just keeps your install current.

341069192c57970279896134d88fa7b986589a11.text: The referral banner in the app now shows a fixed website address instead of fetching your personal referral link from a server. This affects the terminal app you use to interact with the assistant. You will see a simple message with a link to the referrals page; there is no loading delay or error message if a personal link cannot be retrieved. The change is live today and requires no action from you.

dfbdff0eec8fc81b0022b0b2f771d7fb7ab39b97.text: The assistant now treats a missing or empty message as blank instead of crashing when starting a side helper. Only the internal team that manages the agent engine sees any effect. Nothing changes for you in daily use.

037d104121c2ba0c45dc28b536d99a27cf27aaf0.text: The command-line tool's version number was bumped from 1.0.544 to 1.0.545, which is a routine packaging label change that does not modify how the application behaves for users. If you install or update the CLI today, you receive no new features or bug fixes beyond this version bump; nothing visible changes in daily use.

9f05d5e37cd1d2cb1f08fcb363cd8757202763a5.text: The team merged two help articles into one place in the documentation, deleting the separate pages about keyboard shortcuts and extra use cases, and combined their content into a single guide. This is an internal documentation update, so it does not change how the assistant works or what you can do today, but future readers will find all the tips and example commands in one spot instead of scattered across multiple pages. No action is needed from anyone, and nothing visible changes in the assistant.

a995965967df8fdbc1506425313f7cad072c0489.text: When you open the project picker in the Freebuff CLI, the list of folders now sorts names alphabetically and visually calls out which folders are tied to a Git repository. The highlighted row uses a softer background that stays readable in both light and dark terminal themes, and the helper text was simplified to 'Navigate to your project folder and press Open' with your current folder path shown in the footer. You will notice the folder list looks tidier, Git projects stand out, and the highlighted entry is easier to read, no setup or action needed on your part.

382195146821bd80e40fed2ffba7ba5efcdbe4f4.text: The project picker, the screen that lets you browse and choose which folder is your current project, has been rebuilt so it no longer breaks when your terminal window is very short. Instead of relying on fixed minimum-height rules, it now calculates which parts are essential (the file list, the text input, and the bottom status bar) and squeezes or hides optional parts (the logo, help text, and recent-project shortcuts) as space runs low. You, the person running Freebuff in a cramped or maximized-split terminal, will see the full file browser render correctly instead of being cut off or misaligned, and the text hint inside the input now reads 'Select project directory...' for clarity.

43ea122eac6e68bea05bff686c4d6099e2af8072.text: The terminal tool now turns on the optional text ads by default when someone first starts it, instead of making them ask for permission each time. The built-in shortcut menu entries for turning those ads on and off no longer show a small beta label beside their names. Anyone using the terminal tool as a new user is affected, because their first session will already have the ads feature active unless they manually disable it, and the only visible impact is that the commands for managing that feature look a little cleaner.

4a88477aab83e69caeceb7e109b377707d815e1d.text: The Freebuff CLI's question-and-answer popup was reorganized so the typing area, the list of choices, and the question title each live in their own tidy section, and the catch-all "Other" option was relabeled "Custom" to make its purpose clearer. No new features or visual overhauls are introduced, so daily use looks and feels the same. This is internal housekeeping that makes the popup easier for the development team to maintain and extend.

e70fc1ca89bf5cd55b9d363c6e664f22f2d77c8b.text: The written guide for people using the command-line tool was simplified by removing a section that listed extra command-line flags. The audience affected is internal, meaning only people who work on the project itself. In your daily use, nothing changes and no action is needed.

2f5d2bb93997374602839e7dbfff2de2b8719926.text: The text shown next to the slash command for starting over was rewritten to say it clears the conversation history and begins a new chat. You is seeing this only if you use the terminal app and open the command list or hover for help. Nothing is changing how clearing works or when you can use it.

9982f5a561976355256ecea412861e4c9d7db730.text: The large headline on the landing page was rewritten to say 'Better agents. Better code.' and the small text below it now claims the service finishes coding tasks more than 100 seconds faster than a well-known competitor, with better results. This only changes what visitors read on the public website, so existing users are not affected. No action is required from you, and the app behaves exactly as before.

4397bbce21cfa5d71613b14afd999451151da269.text: Searching the help docs and the web now costs nothing to look up, so you can read articles or browse the web for answers without it counting against your monthly usage. This is a temporary change for the documentation and searching tools used inside Freebuff. You do not need to do anything different, and what you see on your bill or account balance does not change because of it. It is in effect today for anyone using those two search features.

bf9eddaba35d2a608d7600e78e602ed432fcff3f.text: When you open the assistant in your terminal inside a project that keeps secret keys and settings in a hidden file called.envrc, the program will now automatically read those settings before it starts, instead of leaving them unloaded. This only happens on Mac and Linux where the helper tool called direnv is installed, and only when the.envrc file has been approved by running 'direnv allow'. You get to keep your project-specific environment variables loaded the same way they are in your other terminal windows, with no extra step required. If direnv is not installed or the file is blocked, the assistant starts normally and leaves everything as it was.

62fd54667bd81aadcaace15ff17372b51b3869ff.text: The buy credits panel on the website has been simplified so you now choose from fixed dollar amounts instead of typing in a custom amount. When you turn on automatic credit top-up, it defaults to a standard refill amount rather than the smallest option. You will see buttons for \$10, \$25, \$50, and \$100 (or higher amounts for organizations) instead of a free-text field where you could enter any value. No action is required from you, and the change is live today.

789820e7ef5e012252ad895bb9b25c3ad481ddfc.text: The website removed a separate navigation bar component that appeared at the top of every page, and instead built the navigation directly into the home page as a floating overlay that slides in with animation. This affects visitors to the Freebuff homepage who will now see the logo and GitHub link fade down from the top of the hero section rather than sitting in a permanent header bar above the content. There is no action needed from you. The change is live today, and aside from the navigation appearing as an animated overlay on the home page, you should notice nothing different in how the site works.

881686fe8d94809b7f42b6b88a2ab055f0d19928.text: Freebuff premium sessions reset at Pacific midnight: The Freebuff team changed how the daily quota of five premium AI coding sessions resets, moving from a rolling 20-hour window to a fixed daily reset at midnight Pacific Time (America/Los_Angeles). This affects you, a Freebuff user running premium models like DeepSeek, Kimi, or GLM, who previously had your session usage tracked over a sliding two-thresh window. In daily use, your five free premium sessions per day now replenish at a fixed time each day, so plan your work around this new daily reset schedule rather than expecting older sessions to gradually roll off your limit.

8ac94a54affac0eea3470c33444b18393683fa02.text: New Freebuff accounts now get a one-time 500-credit signup bonus instead of receiving 500 free credits every month. Existing users who were already getting monthly free credits keep them under the same grandfathered schedule. When you sign up today, you get your 500 credits once at registration rather than on a recurring monthly basis, and your usage screen now shows remaining credits with a simple "Free" label and a "Cycle" renewal date instead of "Monthly Free". No action is needed from current users whose accounts already had the old monthly grant, as they continue on their existing schedule.

30c51ac38ce89001a9a39a00416a2d56ad446fce.text: The team that creates the Windows download of the program now uses a compatibility-friendly version of its build tool to package it, which lets the packaged program run on a wider range of Windows PCs. The people who notice this are anyone who downloads and runs the official Windows installer, plus the automated setup that builds release copies for testing. For daily use there is nothing new to click or change, the program simply installs and starts up the same as before, only the behind-the-scenes packaging is more broadly compatible.

293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.text: The assistant's status display now shows how many units you've already used instead of how many you have left, so the numbers line up the same way in the model picker and other session screens. It applies to you: anyone checking their current session summary in the terminal. Nothing about what you can actually do changes, but the summary reads the same everywhere, so you won't see one screen say 'left' and another say 'used' for the same quota.

4b03dcbd2a7791366306ab976dba52fd9659b6d6.text: Freebuff now records, through its advertising partner Gravity, the moment you send your very first message in a session, but only the details that Gravity already shared with Freebuff through the browser. That first-message signal is sent along with a stable event identifier based on your user ID, the surface you are using (such as web, cloud, desktop, or the AI chat), and a strict 3-second timeout, so the record either completes quickly or fails in a way that Freebuff can retry. The feature is live today for Freebuff service surfaces, and it does not change what you see or do when you start a conversation, it only improves attribution behind the scenes, so users notice nothing different in daily use.

92ff02610686d5d9fc79060254e0ba759de87c76.text: The Freebuff welcome screen in your terminal now hides the streak bonus message when your window is too small (below 52 rows tall or not wide enough for the text to fit on one line), so the model picker stays easy to scroll without crowding. The streak indicator itself still appears whenever the feature is enabled, but the explanatory note only shows on roomier terminals. Additionally, the Kimi K2.7 Code model's tagline was updated to include ' & Slow', clarifying that it trades extra speed for cost efficiency. Live today for Freebuff CLI users.

ff555dfc23f4037715103ed7983c5e934eae5555.text: Freebuff moved its streak counter (the line showing how many days in a row you've used it) so the same code powers both the terminal app and the desktop app. The logic now lives in a shared library, while the terminal still adds its own layout rules on top. For you, this just means the streak display and its reward note behave consistently across surfaces and now also tease how many days are left to unlock your perk as you climb toward a full week. No action needed on your part, it's live today.

f5526661a4291076b5784de328a4ddb405831935.text: Starting July 29, 2026, the bonus model sessions you earn by referring friends now refresh every day (Pacific time) instead of once a week. If you keep using the tool every day, your referral rewards and a streak bonus (up to 4 extra sessions) also reset daily rather than weekly. The on-screen messages and countdown timers now say "today" and show a daily reset instead of "this week". Users on the free daily plan see no change; this only affects people who unlock the bonus model through referrals and full access.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.text: When you pick a model in the terminal model picker, the listed reasoning level now matches what the server actually uses to run that model, because the picker and the server now read from the same shared setting. This affects anyone who selects a model from the terminal list, so the displayed reasoning label can no longer disagree with the real behavior. You will notice the correct reasoning level shown next to supported models (like DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash, MiniMax M3 shows none, and OpenRouter-hosted GPT-5.6 Luna), so the label you see is the level actually applied.

c8ad1e274f4ab909d17fd050698c542d99ec3b63.text: The recommended default model has switched to GPT-5.6 Luna on all surfaces, so new users and default selections now land on Luna instead of DeepSeek V4 Pro, which was paused for free mode on August 18, 2026 and removed from the picker; Pro remains listed in the catalog so older clients can still request it and the server silently substitutes it at admission rather than rejecting it. A saved DeepSeek V4 Pro preference now migrates to Flash on every launch, and the catalog order, premium/unlimited buckets, and desktop concurrency split (1 premium to 3 unlimited sessions) were updated to match Flash becoming a premium, one-session-a-day model.

695d4d15676d9937d172ccf87909013085942be1.text: The assistant now treats weekends as always off-peak for DeepSeek, so the most expensive rates only apply on weekdays during the Beijing-time morning and evening rush. This affects paying subscribers whose plan excludes peak-hour charges from their allowance. You may see lower-cost usage or more available capacity on Saturdays and Sundays, since weekend requests no longer count against any peak-hour limits.

f396f4ef37618acc07c9b6c7e461695e3d357e72.text: The daily limit on free compute credits was raised, so accounts using free credits can now use about four times the value of their credits per day instead of the previous three times. This affects users who rely on free credits granted by the service. If you use these free credits, you will not notice anything different unless you were regularly hitting the old daily cap, in which case you may now be able to do a bit more before reaching the limit.

58699f0e07179ec3da47ddc01f58272ff7c6f565.text: Freebuff changed the promotional text you see when you run low on usage (in the CLI, web chat, and waiting areas), replacing session counts with hourly language and naming the paid plan where previously it said 'Freebuff Pro'. This affects only the in-app messaging shown to end-users of the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, and SDK, not any underlying usage limits or quotas. You might now see ads phrased like '+3 hours a day' or 'Total: 8 a day' instead of '+3 more sessions,' with the plan name 'Starter' (or whatever tier you'd see on /plans) called out in the message body. The update shipped live in the codebase on 2026-09-27, and surfaces like the screen-reader chat and Desktop-Showcase ads keep their old wording unchanged.

538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.title: Arrow keys let slash and mention menus own Up Down in non-empty drafts
538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.summary: The early arrow guard in resolveChatKeyboardAction that short-circuited Up/Down in a non-empty draft was removed from cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts and re-added as a Priority 7.5 step below the slash and mention menu handling, so typing '/' or '@' no longer swallows menu navigation. shouldInterceptChatInputKey in cli/src/utils/chat-input-key-intercept.ts drops its matching early guard and now lets an open menu own Up/Down via the hasSuggestions branch, while plain left/right at non-empty positions still fall through to the composer cursor. New tests assert Down/Up after typing '/' move the highlight and scroll the menu, an open menu owns Up/Down in the draft that opened it, and left/right remain ordinary input with an open menu.
538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.evidence: Removed the early non-empty-draft arrow guard that returned { type: 'none' } in resolveChatKeyboardAction (cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts) and replaced it with a lower-priority Priority 7.5 guard placed below the slash and mention menu handling, and removed the parallel early guard in shouldInterceptChatInputKey (cli/src/utils/chat-input-key-intercept.ts) so an open menu owns Up/Down even in a non-empty draft.
538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.unknowns: The diff does not show whether this commit changes Ctrl+Q queue editor behavior in the bash input mode path.

538b266fe1f102555546d12938940b7f0c0ed8ce.text: When you are typing a message and the list of slash commands (like /undo or /diff) or mention suggestions is open, pressing the Up and Down arrow keys now scrolls through that list instead of moving your text cursor. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, desktop app, or web assistant who rely on command menus while typing. You no longer have to close the menu to use the arrow keys, and left/right still move your cursor normally within your message.

a566ec2b780dc09c4cded7008af0081931421420.text: The code now keeps track of file paths that can't be processed during changes, instead of crashing when it encounters a problematic path. This is internal maintenance work used by Freebuff's developers to test and evaluate the system's reliability; it does not change how you write code or interact with the assistant. You will not notice any difference in your daily use of Freebuff.

6a9d9e9e002983b8cf2be0a282b2c4abc05c5592.text: The assistant gained a new slash command option that lets it switch to a different behavior mode, and it prints a confirmation message in the terminal when you choose it. This is for developers and contributors who build and maintain the tool's internal command set, not for everyday users of the assistant. Switching to this new mode does not affect your regular daily usage unless you explicitly type the new command, so nothing changes for you today.

1688b09cf6ac391bcef68b01a5449b7b0396cfee.text: The Freebuff software team published a new version of their coding assistant, which means all the recent improvements are now available to everyone who uses it. This update bundles together several changes, including a faster, more focused mode for simpler tasks, better tracking of how much time and money the assistant spends on evaluations, and an updated software kit for developers integrating the assistant into their own tools, it is live today and requires no action from most users.

c21fabe374e86cdcca1dad300951054a989389c0.text: The software's internal version label was cleaned up by dropping a temporary 'legacy' tag, leaving just the main version number. This is an internal packaging step that happens behind the scenes when new builds are prepared, so it does not reach you as a visible update. Anyone who downloads the assistant will get the current build, but you will not notice any difference in how it works today.

72c6c8f8de5e5e816d91ded74abe1b3c77617555.text: The helper that finds and lists relevant files was told, in plain terms, to stop writing any extra commentary and only return a list of file paths, one per line. This is internal tooling used by Freebuff's own automation to locate files, not something you interact with directly. You will not notice any difference in the app today; this change just keeps the automated file-finding output clean and predictable for the internal agents that rely on it.

6efb504e839be5cf133178229e29e27c59212454.text: The new release rolls up a batch of recent improvements into one published package, the most visible being a new way for the assistant to ask you questions with multiple-choice options right in the terminal, plus a fresh command for sharing referral codes. It also smooths out how the terminal accepts input, making navigation and editing feel more consistent across different input modes. Anyone running the assistant in their terminal gets these improvements just by updating, and you will notice the new question forms and the referral command right away, while the input handling changes make the overall experience steadier. This is live today.

fa42225b8f7fdc6467ee4e77aa42983e3f04d484.text: The Freebuff coding assistant just got a routine update numbered 1.0.552, which is now available to anyone who downloads or updates it today. This update bundles together a batch of minor improvements made over the past day: editor tools now read their responses more reliably from the assistant, a few behind-the-scenes agents are configured to think through harder problems with clearer instructions, and a small icon for copying your saved work onto your clipboard now lines up neatly next to your messages in the text screen. If you keep your copy of Freebuff up to date, these changes happen automatically and nothing needs to be turned on by you.

4d827e7c5c05a53c2d4676e4e11cd2eac13f0994.text: The assistant can now connect to Claude subscriptions and show whether you have remaining quota, along with color-coded usage bars. If you link your Claude subscription inside the assistant, the status bar will display your usage and warn you when you're running low. You only need to update the assistant to get these improvements.

977871824938ec93efe479f547e8e6f5c5cd5f7b.text: The Freebuff CLI received a new version label, bumping the installed release from the previous number to 1.0.595. This is an internal packaging step that lets the terminal tool report a fresh version to users; the actual user-facing improvements that come with this label were already shipped in earlier releases on the same day, including a clearer task-complete indicator, smoother typing support for international keyboards, and a login screen that now shows an SSH connection address. As soon as you update to this version, the assistant behaves exactly as it did before, only the reported version number changes.

bdfce88fa0d8196c7fe4ec31be5e7aee376b1938.text: The version label for the downloadable coding assistant was bumped from 0.0.24 to 0.0.25, which simply packages the new GitHub login option that developers can now use to sign into the assistant. This release is what people get when they install or update the tool today and it does not change how it behaves otherwise. No action is needed unless you install updates from the release channel.

5ebfc491f4c89d84a0bf7383fc856ba7af4e523c.text: Freebuff released a new version of its installable coding assistant package, updating the version label that tracks what is currently shipped. You do not need to take any action, but if you reinstall or update Freebuff through your normal package manager, you will pick up this release, which includes fixes so clicks no longer trigger follow-up actions after a session ends and the model picker no longer briefly shows a false "no wait" message when a session finishes. The version number itself is just an internal label, but updating to it gives you the user-facing improvements that shipped alongside it today.

4e4042f4b5db6f285a8e43b7f60806d24a3db553.text: The team simply updated the version number label on the Freebuff installer package to 0.0.76, a routine packaging step that records what goes inside the next release for Linux, Windows, and Mac downloaders. For you, installing or updating Freebuff now offers the included fixes: signing in on certain networks stops repeatedly asking you to authenticate, long coding conversations show clearer progress markers when they continue, and the bar at the bottom of the terminal no longer shows a redundant session status word. No action is needed from you, and existing installs keep working; the change only takes effect once you download the new version.

996258cf42269f4121e590f33229257b9814db65.text: The Freebuff program was re-labeled to a new version number today, which is a routine bookkeeping change that triggers updates for anyone installing or upgrading the tool. This release bundles several user-visible improvements at once, including a new on-screen message shown when a login link has expired, a web search tool that now uses a different provider, and a new tool for reading web pages during research. Users who update to this version will see the login-expiry notice if their access code is missing and can rely on the improved search and web-reading tools right away; no action is required beyond updating.

eebd6089f2b07ee217e4367ccdf074effed29364.text: When you open Freebuff's model picker in the terminal, pressing the up and down arrow keys used to only move between the list of AI models. Now, if you keep pressing down to get past the bottom of that list, the keyboard navigation flows smoothly into the referral banner below it, letting you highlight and activate its 'Copy invite link' and 'Use GLM 5.2' buttons without touching the mouse. When the picker is closed, the banner's buttons drop back to their normal look, so there is no leftover highlight stuck on a button when the list is gone. This makes the landing screen fully navigable by keyboard for anyone who opens the model picker and reaches the referral banner at the bottom.

454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.text: The assistant used to have to finish everything it was doing before you could give it new instructions, like waiting for a full reply to end before you could say the next thing. Now, you can slip a new message to it mid-task and it will read it and act on it during the very next step, without cancelling what it already started. This is for hosts that build on top of the assistant (like the CLI or other integrations), so it quietly reaches you today if your host already supports it, but it needs no action from you and you simply notice that your follow-up messages are picked up faster.

7bb5501109a4dd88daf5e262cb1356b7b815b200.text: The progress bar that tracks your standing in the Freebuff system now hides any oddball negative scores instead of showing them, so a rare data glitch can no longer make your progress look weird on screen. This only affects how your current standing looks while you are signed into Freebuff on the web, in the terminal, or on the desktop app, since those all share the same progress display. In daily use, you will not notice anything different unless you were somehow seeing a broken negative value before, which most people never did.

f61c4efa8a0d8fabb774756afdd610b7b7726010.text: The Freebuff command-line tool has released a new version that switches its built-in AI assistant to a newer model, adds security checks so that remote agents downloaded from a registry are only run if they come from trusted publishers, and now verifies the integrity of each downloaded file against a recorded fingerprint before installing it. This update is available to anyone who installs or updates the Freebuff CLI today. The visible effect for you is that installs and updates are now checked for tampering, and the built-in assistant uses the latest model version.

0d4d983708de983b28cd65e1727c595c48b46219.title: Freebuff session gate errors explain mid-run stops and re-admit
0d4d983708de983b28cd65e1727c595c48b46219.summary: handleFreebuffGateError now always sets an explanatory error message - 'Your free session ended before this message was processed...' when the prompt was dropped, otherwise 'Your free session ended, so the agent stopped here...' - then flips the session to `ended` for session_expired, waiting_room_required and session_model_mismatch so in-flight work finishes under the server-side grace period and the next send admits a new session. In cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts, PollController.abort aborts the in-flight fetch and arms a fresh AbortController so subsequent refreshes and admission use a valid signal. cli/src/hooks/use-message-queue.ts gains a watchdogTimeoutMs test seam and the watchdog now re-arms while a chain or agent stream is still running, resetting the lock only once no run is in progress. cli/src/utils/ai-sdk-warnings.ts adds createAiSdkWarningFilter so the AI SDK v2 compatibility notice - raised on every v2 model call - is dropped while every other warning is logged once per provider/model per process (MAX_REMEMBERED_WARNINGS = 500).
0d4d983708de983b28cd65e1727c595c48b46219.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts, handleFreebuffGateError now always calls updater.setError(...) with a message that depends on opts.messageWasDropped, then calls markFreebuffSessionEnded() for the session_expired, waiting_room_required, and session_model_mismatch cases; in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts, PollController.abort calls abortController.abort() and assigns abortController = new AbortController(); in cli/src/hooks/use-message-queue.ts, useMessageQueue accepts a new opts.watchdogTimeoutMs test seam and armWatchdog now re-arms when a chain-in-progress or active-agent-streams is still running, with new tests 'a queued run that outlives the timeout is not reported or reset as stuck' and 'a lock held with no run in progress is still reset'; in cli/src/utils/ai-sdk-warnings.ts, createAiSdkWarningFilter and installAiSdkWarningLogger are added so the v2 compatibility notice is dropped and other warnings are logged once per provider/model per process (MAX_REMEMBERED_WARNINGS = 500), with tests 'keeps real v2 calls off the terminal and out of the logs' and 'logs any other warning once per provider and model'

0d4d983708de983b28cd65e1727c595c48b46219.text: When your free coding session runs out mid-conversation (for example, right after you answered a question the assistant asked), the chat now clearly explains what happened and stops gracefully instead of hanging with a blinking cursor or silently restarting. This applies to the built-in Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app. You see a short message on the screen telling you the session ended and that you can send a new message to start fresh, with no need to restart the app or worry about a stuck run.

d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.1.1 published
d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package (`freebuff/cli/release/package.json`) version field is bumped from `0.1.0` to `0.1.1` following a release-bump commit that adjusts only the `version` field in the package manifest.
d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.evidence: Modified file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`: the `version` field changed from `0.1.0` to `0.1.1`.

d22c969cee10470f88c1dce87c6091f4426d0b99.text: Freebuff CLI 0.1.1 adds a step limit to web research, improves BYOK context-window detection, and fixes keyboard and time-zone handling. The web researcher now stops itself after 15 steps instead of running away and burning through thousands of tool calls in a single chat message, so research tasks finish predictably. When you connect your own model (BYOK), the CLI now asks the provider what its real context window is instead of guessing the default and aggressively compacting your conversation, which reduces unnecessary truncation. Slash and mention menus now correctly own the Up and Down arrow keys when you are typing a command or mention, so the menus scroll instead of moving your cursor in the draft. The desktop client now sends an identity header that names itself as the desktop app when creating or fetching sessions, laying groundwork for future desktop-only behavior. Time-zone lookups are now validated before use, preventing crashes on browsers that report an unsupported zone. Error logging now converts error objects into structured data, so failure messages reach diagnostics instead of appearing empty. CPU information probing now handles cases where system calls fail, falling back gracefully so startup fingerprinting still completes.

d9ecc85e1636aa3b8fc950f42de71c3ec8da7250.title: Muse Spark 1.3 added to the Freebuff free model picker
d9ecc85e1636aa3b8fc950f42de71c3ec8da7250.summary: Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta's agentic coding model with a 1M-token context, Contributor tier, rate-limited and shared across users, falling back to DeepSeek V4 Flash when busy) is promoted from Web/Cloud-only to the CLI, Desktop, Web, and Cloud pickers, per the widened doc comment on `FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_13_CONTRIBUTOR_MODEL_ID` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. The catalog edit is mirrored by three new bundled agent roots - `agents/base2/base2-free-muse-spark-1-3.ts` (a `noReview` base2 rollback root), `agents/base3-free-muse-spark-1-3.ts` (the CLI/Desktop single-loop harness), and `agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-muse-spark-1-3.ts` (its own-model reviewer so a base2 session does not 403 on a Flash fallback) - and by registering those roots in the free-agents maps. `FREEBUFF_SERVICE_ONLY_MODEL_IDS` is emptied so the row is no longer refused to every non-Web service account, and `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_SLOT_BOUND_MODEL_IDS` now includes `FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_MODEL_IDS`, making the model `slot-bound` on Desktop from the day it ships. Alongside the agents, `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md` add the row to each model table. This is the picker widening, plus six follow-on catalog and doc edits.

87acd39098734f870266915e02267851c4cd4a4f.summary: A new module adds `detectForeignFreebuffClient`, which inspects a request's `tools`, temperature, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, and `max_completion_tokens` fields to flag traffic that did not originate from a Freebuff client, and `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, which downgrades flagged requests to the `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` model according to one of four modes. adf5bef2be7cd107b6fdefb43b9e9e6fffadf1d7.unknowns: The diff introduces the Greg 2 constants, option rows, and pool membership but does not show which consuming package or runtime path actually routes a request to the crof/ endpoints, so the rollout and admission behavior for these models are not observable from this commit alone.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.title: Ox Alpha added to Freebuff Web and Cloud only
9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.summary: Ox Alpha (`stealth/DeepSeek`) is wired into the Freebuff Web/Cloud surfaces via `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MODEL_ID`, `FREEBUFF_SERVICE_ONLY_MODEL_IDS`, `isFreebuffServiceOnlyModelId`, `isFreebuffOxAlphaModelId`, and the `OX_ALPHA_MODEL` entry prepended to `FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS`, but deliberately left out of `SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS` and `FREEBUFF_MODELS` so the CLI and Desktop pickers cannot render it. Its price fence `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MAX_PRICE` is zero on both prompt and completion and is sent as OpenRouter's `provider.max_price`, which refuses any endpoint that charges so a stealth repricing fails closed before the first billed token. The model is pinned to its own roots across `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS`, `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL`, the Web and CLI base3 maps, and `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`, because a root allowed more than one model is a door onto everything else it allows and the price fence only holds if every turn stays on the one id. Limited-tier admission in `isFreebuffSessionModelAllowedForAccessTier` now takes the union over `FREEBUFF_WEB_LIMITED_MODEL_IDS` (rather than only `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS`) so a browser-only limited row cannot pass a picker that then fails the session gate. `agents/base-chat.ts` mirrors the new id in its serialized `CONTEXT_WINDOWS` table at `1_000_000`, kept in sync with `FREEBUFF_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` by `agents/__tests__/base-chat.test.ts`. Ox Alpha runs at `high` reasoning effort by default (provider default `max`) because measurement showed `max` truncating 1 of 4 samples at 4k tokens, and it discloses host retention with `dataUse: 'service'` rather than claiming a training grant the stealth terms do not give.
9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.evidence: Added `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MODEL_ID = 'stealth/DeepSeek'`, `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MAX_PRICE` (0/0), `FREEBUFF_SERVICE_ONLY_MODEL_IDS`, `isFreebuffServiceOnlyModelId`, `isFreebuffOxAlphaModelId`, and `OX_ALPHA_MODEL` row to `FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`; added `'stealth/DeepSeek': 1_000_000` to `CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `agents/base-chat.ts`; added Ox Alpha allowlist entries (`'base2-free-DeepSeek'` root, `base3-free-DeepSeek`, reviewer, `isFreebuffSessionModelAllowedForAccessTier` union change) in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`.
9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.unknowns: The diff does not show the Freebuff Web/Cloud client or completions handler that actually enforces the service-account gate and renders the picker row, only the shared constants and the allowlist roots.

changes.what: Defines `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MODEL_ID`, `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MAX_PRICE` (0/0), `FREEBUFF_SERVICE_ONLY_MODEL_IDS`, `isFreebuffServiceOnlyModelId`, `isFreebuffOxAlphaModelId`, the `OX_ALPHA_MODEL` row, and `OX_ALPHA_REASONING_EFFORTS`, and prepends the row to `FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS`, adds Ox Alpha.

Imports `FREEBUFF_OX_ALPHA_MODEL_ID` and pins the Ox Alpha root (`base2-free-DeepSeek`), its base3 twin, the per-model root lookup, the free-mode reviewer lookup, and the `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` allowlist entry to exactly one model.
Adds `stealth/DeepSeek` to the serialized `CONTEXT_WINDOWS` map with a 1,048,576-published window entered at 1,000,000 for parity with the Luna/Muse Spark rows.

654a906e6758ffe17974dae829d35423dcd827b3.text: Freebuff pulled the newer Muse Spark 1.3 model from its free list of choices and put the older Muse Spark 1.2 back in its place, because 1.3 is paused for cost and scarcity reasons, not because it broke. You, as someone using the free assistant, now see Muse Spark 1.2 offered where 1.3 used to appear, with the same rate-limited, queue-then-fallback behavior, and no action is required on your part. This is live today across the CLI, web, desktop, and SDK, alongside other changes in the same release batch such as a Solar Pro 4 pricing revert and production runtime smoke checks.

26f374dc2bc2abd17e24eabe0c254e426e49d350.text: The model named Muse Spark 1.2 was replaced by Muse Spark 1.3 as the version offered to you when you pick a model in Freebuff, so you now get the newer 1.3 by default. If you had previously selected 1.2, the system quietly redirects you to 1.3 when the session starts. Nothing breaks: older apps that still reference 1.2 keep running on it until they are updated, and you do not need to do anything to receive 1.3.

92c4f5ef87df3e074a688d0c635c551b51d46b37.text: Freebuff removed Muse Spark 1.3 from its list of free models and replaced it with Muse Spark 1.2, because 1.3 stopped responding to all connection attempts while 1.2 kept working. This affects anyone using the free assistant on the web, desktop, or terminal, and the fix rolls out to both existing users (whose saved picks are gently switched back) and new users (who now see 1.2 in the menu). In daily use, the change is invisible: you simply get a model that actually answers instead of one that leaves you waiting, and the list now reliably offers the working option everywhere.

d9ecc85e1636aa3b8fc950f42de71c3ec8da7250.text: Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 coding model, previously only available in a web browser, is now offered directly in the Freebuff terminal app, desktop app, and cloud version - but each user is sharing a limited number of requests with everyone else. When you pick it and the shared limit is full, you get put in a short queue instead of waiting forever, and if that delay is too long, the assistant simply continues your task using a different model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, so you are never left hanging. You will only see the new option appear after you update your Freebuff app to the next release, since the picker list is built into the app itself.

bd9237b1808e650373ecd6303080a5f3c29e1071.text: A model that had just been added to Freebuff's free model list has been removed again, on the same day it was added, because it was running slowly and failing too often for most people. Existing installed apps still recognize the model's name so they can finish conversations already in progress instead of crashing, but it will no longer appear as a choice in any new list. This only affects end-users who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app or SDK. Nothing else changes about their access, limits, or the other models available to them. If you happened to try this model while it was briefly available, you would have noticed that responses were coming back roughly seven times slower than expected, and that some conversations ended mid-way with an error.

4ac1fd1d59197d7f28602ac38da5d4c46e0277a3.text: Freebuff added Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash as a new model you can pick, across the terminal app, web, and desktop, starting today (September 3, 2026). It's aimed at Freebuff users who need to read or analyze files with sound and video clips (it's the only model here that can do that), and it offers a million-word memory for big projects, though it's also the most expensive model per conversation. If you choose it, your daily session allowance runs out faster than other models, and Freebuff shows the higher price before you start; otherwise, nothing changes, and the default DeepSeek model is unaffected.

8d7a935e56beac4db2faa5f2421e2af0f1c6a905.text: {"eli5": "The AI model called Ox Alpha has been removed from the free model picker that Freebuff users can choose from. This affects users of the Freebuff web app, desktop app, and CLI who were previously able to select or were automatically assigned to Ox Alpha as one of their free AI coding model options. Since the host that provided Ox Alpha ended its free promotion, anyone who previously used or would normally get Ox Alpha will now be automatically switched to another available free model instead, with no action required on your part."].

68b487b1f0fc0e9fd42f83503efa2533890ff411.text: Freebuff removed the DeepSeek V4 Pro model from the free catalog and replaced it with GLM 5.3 Flash as the new deep-reasoning option, and there is a new limit of two sessions per day for it. This affects users of the free tier on the CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. In daily use you'll see GLM 5.3 Flash at the bottom of the model picker, capped at two sessions per day, and DeepSeek V4 Pro is no longer available; existing saved picks are switched automatically.

f8ed82aaaa4ed3c5776a04b6c7423b894b294f74.text: A new experimental AI model called Ox Alpha has been added to Freebuff's list of free models, meaning you can now select it from the model picker in the CLI, desktop app, and web interface. It offers a large 1-million token context window and costs no session, though it is marked as experimental and may be withdrawn or changed without notice. This change affects all Freebuff users, particularly those in limited-access regions who can now choose Ox Alpha alongside MiMo 2.5 for their coding tasks. You will see the new model appear in your model selection menu, labeled with a 'TEST' badge to indicate its experimental status.

cbdf5030d0238565dfe2852e8eacc93bfc803b82.text: The MiniMax M3 model has been removed from Freebuff's free model selection so it can no longer be chosen for new sessions, and anyone who still picks it now gets a clear message telling them to switch to another model instead of being silently redirected. This affects Freebuff users who select models for their coding sessions across the CLI, web, desktop, or SDK. You will see MiniMax M3 disappear from the model list in your picker, and if your current client still offers it, the app will explain that it is no longer available and recommend a different model rather than quietly using another one on your behalf.

c8ad1e274f4ab909d17fd050698c542d99ec3b63.text: Freebuff swapped out which AI model your assistant uses by default. For full-access users in the US, Canada, UK, EU and other supported regions, the assistant previously used the strongest reasoning model (DeepSeek V4 Pro) as its default, but that model has been moved to the end of the picker list and is no longer recommended anywhere. Every surface now points you at GPT-5.6 Luna as the default choice, while the cheaper DeepSeek V4 Flash becomes the fallback only when you run out of daily sessions. This took effect live for anyone who installs or updates today, and existing users will see the default switch on their next session instead of DeepSeek V4 Pro.

477475a9e9f4723ccff8403fd2b739bf68b87c42.text: The new August 13 build of DeepSeek V4 Pro is now the version offered in Freebuff's model list, with a clearer label and the same reasoning options as the Flash model. If you use the free CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK to pick AI models, you now see this updated Pro build named with its date and marked as new. You will notice the Pro option describes itself as the strongest agentic build, and the picker no longer steers you away from it when you pick a recommended model. Who it affects: Freebuff end-users. Everyday impact: When you open the model picker or start a new Freebuff session, recommended picks and default selections will not nudge you off of DeepSeek V4 Pro, since that model's latest build now leads on agentic benchmarks.

28663a3cb73ad6b81408aa9cf131a8edf1f1f5ba.text: You can now save a full chat conversation directly to a file using the new /export command, which works like /copy but writes to a file instead of the clipboard. This is useful when a conversation is too long for the clipboard. If you previously used 'export' as a shortcut for /copy, that shortcut now runs the new /export command instead. Codebuff or Freebuff users who want a permanent record of a chat can type /export, or /export my-notes.md to name the file, and pick.json to get the raw messages.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new /export command that lets you save your entire chat conversation to a file as either Markdown or JSON, plus a refreshed model picker that now defaults to GLM 5.3 Flash across CLI, Web, and Desktop while keeping Muse Spark 1.3 in the free tier and dropping Gemini 3.8 Flash from the free picker. Key safety and control changes include a one-sentence sponsored consent dialog for advertiser-backed proposals, plan-mode now blocking file edits and commits during planning turns, and idle Desktop sessions for premium models automatically releasing after 10 minutes to prevent stuck concurrency slots. For daily use, you get more predictable billing with a $0.50 compute cap and $2 acceptance fee on sponsored proposals, clearer Freebucks metering that shows your remaining balance in the status bar when you are pay-as-you-go, and day-scale wait timers (like '26 days') instead of raw hours on usage limit walls. The CLI also gains a sponsor dock detail panel, sticky per-user ad bucketing so you do not see the same offer repeatedly, and aborting mid-task no longer waits through full retry backoffs. Together, these changes give you more export control, clearer spending signals, and tighter safety rails around plan-only sessions and sponsored work.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: This release adds a new /copy command that exports your whole conversation to Markdown and saves it to your clipboard, so you can easily share or save chats. It also makes the premium model picker show a live reset countdown at all times, including a Pacific-day fallback so the timer still works before the server reports a reset time. A new login analytics funnel tracks the steps between launching the CLI and successfully logging in, helping identify where users stall. The referral banner now links to /get-started with a personalized ?referrer= parameter and includes a one-click copy button for invite links. GLM 5.2 is added as a weekly referral reward served by Fireworks, appearing only in the referral banner and excluded from the regular model picker. Finally, the waiting room now promotes the full ASCII logo on mid-height terminals when the model picker is collapsed, filling dead space and reducing flicker.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff update adds a new /diagnostics command that lets you see which model is running, how much compute you have left, and how many sessions are active. The default model switched to DeepSeek V4 Flash as the recommended free option, with GPT-5.6 Luna and MiniMax M3 remaining available, while older models like Kimi K2.7 Code were removed from the free picker. When you try to switch to a different model while a session is still locked, the CLI now actively ends the stale session instead of silently ignoring you, and it shows a message when a switch is blocked. The installer now works through HTTP proxies and safely resumes interrupted downloads. Daily session limits for premium and limited tiers are now 6, and referral rewards were simplified to grant sessions only. Upgrading gives you a more responsive landing screen that adapts to your terminal size, clearer model picker labels, and fewer stalled or corrupted chats because active runs abort when you switch conversations.

358336a18e557894e7bbdd623c43e34f1bc54f6f.text: This release updates the Freebuff CLI to version 1.0.688 with several improvements to advertising, model access, and account management. Sponsor break ads now render more safely with a new parser that prevents formatting errors, and Freebuff Pro sponsor breaks include new creative assets. The CLI now shows a countdown to your daily Freebucks reset, displays peak pricing badges with local-time surcharges, and tracks session refunds explicitly to prevent race conditions. Model access changes replace Muse Spark 1.3 with Muse Spark 1.2 in the free picker after 1.3 repeatedly failed to load, and GPT-5.6 Luna is no longer restricted to Pro-only users across all interfaces. The free promotion spend windows now correctly align with price changes, fixing a bug where free usage consumed daily budget on weekends. Daily spend ceilings are retired in favor of soft session pacing, so the CLI no longer blocks calls based on hard spend limits but instead adds pauses when needed. The Freebucks daily compute cap is raised from 3 times to 4 times the Freebucks value, and the Freebucks intro card no longer triggers unintended model row selections when dismissed.

a733b317c1e05ace5fe868e3d4f52d300dbd018c.text: The daily limit on the GLM 5.2 model you get from inviting friends has been lowered from unlimited to 1 per day. This affects Freebuff users who earn their daily GLM 5.2 sessions through referrals, streak bonuses, or special grants. In practice, even if you have many referrals, you will not receive more than 1 GLM 5.2 session per day, and the referral banner now shows your progress toward that 1-session cap.

bd5c18ff73257a748a3bd0e402e25af4c012649f.text: The size of the paid subscription plans was adjusted so the larger plan is no longer just an exact multiple of the smaller one. Subscribers in regions that normally only see a limited set of models can now access the models their plan covers. You may notice the larger plan offers fewer extra sessions than before, and if you are in one of those limited regions with a paid plan, additional models should appear in your picker. No action is needed on your part; the new allowances take effect automatically.

fd3c20c290bf78152ecc86ab7ba9191f420ca1ea.text: Freebuff has switched the model that starts up by default when you open the app, whether on the command line, in a browser, or on the desktop. The new default is GLM 5.3 Flash, which replaces the previous model (GPT-5.6 Luna) and now appears first in every model list you see. Who it affects: this applies to anyone using Freebuff for free, so people writing code in their terminal, building apps in the browser, or running the desktop app. Everyday impact: your next coding session now begins on GLM 5.3 Flash automatically, and that choice shows up at the top of the model menu.

ed706ca47d476c9a68e7302b22b3c615dd522dd1.text: Freebuff switched its default AI model to DeepSeek V4 Pro, which is now available at all times, while DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 is now paused during peak hours (the busiest part of the day). This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK who pick models in the regular picker. Starting today, if you open Freebuff or start a new session, you'll see DeepSeek V4 Pro listed first and selected by default, and if you try to use Flash during its paused window it will automatically fall back to Pro instead of the unlimited model. The model list no longer shows any 'recommended' badges or 'superseded' notices, so the top-to-bottom order is the only signal left for where to start.

2a3c3c791364d4f39c2c61d80162909cd199cd29.text: Freebuff has published its paid subscription plans so the app can show you what they cost and what you get. There are three plans - Starter, Plus, and Pro - each with increasing numbers of AI sessions per day, over a rolling five days, and per month. A key constraint: only a portion of your daily sessions can be used on the most expensive AI models (like GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Pro), keeping the worst-case cost of the plan predictable for everyone. If you are on the lower-tier plans, you will also see a note that certain models are unavailable during peak hours, but Pro users get full access all the time. This is live today for users in the subscription rollout audience.

9d0e435b3802e4b6b833c1ed349d604e5b804f0d.text: The web and cloud versions of Freebuff now offer a new free AI model called Ox Alpha (stealth/DeepSeek) for coding tasks. This addition is only available on browser-based surfaces (freebuff.com and cloud environments), and is deliberately blocked from the desktop app and CLI tool, so if you usually run Freebuff locally you will not see it. The model is served at no charge while it is being evaluated, but Freebuff added a zero-cost safety cap so that if the provider ever starts charging, the model simply stops working instead of unexpectedly billing anyone. No action is required from you; the change is live today and affects only people using the browser or cloud-hosted Freebuff.

84c46ec290a6e544a29a30189b87a2fa1fa4ec90.text: The Pro subscription plan ($60) has been removed from the list of plans available for purchase, so only Starter ($8) and Plus ($25) can be selected during sign-up. The plan's billing setup still exists behind the scenes, so it can be offered again later without extra billing work. This change was applied to Freebuff's subscription systems today, and no action is needed from current subscribers, but anyone trying to sign up for Pro will find it unavailable until it is added back.

adf5bef2be7cd107b6fdefb43b9e9e6fffadf1d7.text: Two new experimental AI models, Greg 2 Ultra and Greg 2 Super, have been registered in Freebuff's system as premium options available only on the web version for users with special access. These models, provided by CrofAI, are significantly more expensive and are kept off the public model picker due to their high costs and large hidden token overhead. Currently, this change only adds them to internal records; the actual routing and user-facing integration happen in later updates.

87acd39098734f870266915e02267851c4cd4a4f.text: Freebuff now includes a guard that watches incoming requests for signs the caller is not actually using a Freebuff product. When it spots a request that does not match a Freebuff client (by checking the tools being offered first, then sampling parameters as a fallback), it can downgrade that request to a free model that costs nothing, instead of letting it consume the paid compute budget. The behavior only activates when Freebuff has this turned on via a configuration mode, so it is in place and ready but does nothing until the operator enables it. There is no visible effect for legitimate Freebuff users right now, because the detection favors real Freebuff tool sets and never downgrades traffic that looks like it came from a genuine client.

bf245a37e473e354eca1d24fc06a78c14059dde6.text: The Freebuff CLI now greets first-time users with a row of clickable starter prompts on a blank chat, so new users can kick things off with a single click instead of staring at an empty input. These prompts only appear for people running the free Freebuff assistant when they have never sent a message before, and they quietly disappear the moment you type or click anything for the first time. They are drawn from a small default set, show the full question when you hover with enough terminal width, and are skipped entirely while menus, overlays, or other input modes are active. The change is live today for Freebuff users and requires no setup.

6f535608014e6e0fe6727ac65f2c83d4147e1873.text: The assistant now requires you to explicitly trust any third-party publisher before it will run an agent downloaded from the public agent registry that contains custom behavior logic, because that logic runs as code on your machine. This affects anyone who runs a published agent from another person or team through the CLI or SDK, not people using the built-in agents or local files. If you try to use an untrusted publisher's agent, the run stops with a clear error telling you exactly how to add that publisher to your trusted list, otherwise nothing changes for your usual workflow.

c8464c6866193ec4780e23b225ab06252eee2ffc.text: The Freebuff team released a new version of the Freebuff app (the free coding assistant) and the Codebuff app (the paid version it lives alongside). In this update they kept the old name for a lightweight Google model around so that older copies of the app that still use that name keep working after Google renamed it. This is mostly behind-the-scenes work to keep existing installs running smoothly, so you won't notice anything different in your daily use right away.

1d9a61e734810b53404ced16489971b33109725e.text: On the Freebuff website, the paid-tier DeepSeek V4 Pro model is now automatically hidden and reopened based on the time of day, using the same peak-hour window already used elsewhere in the product. This only affects people using Freebuff in a web browser; the desktop app and command-line tool keep offering that model exactly as before. If you are not eligible to pay for a subscription, nothing about the model picker or your sessions has changed. This gating is wired and live today.

385a72397d899dcd80b9715f1b86adff24faa644.text: The part of the app that picks which AI model to use now asks for your permission upfront whenever your stored balance can't be checked at that moment, instead of guessing or falling back to an old number. It affects you, the Freebuff CLI user, the moment you reach for a paid or metered model on a Freebucks account and the app can't confirm how much Freebucks you have left. In daily use this means a clearer prompt: rather than a confusing refusal tied to an outdated balance, you'll see a plain "balance unavailable, Enter may spend wallet Freebucks" note and can confirm to start the session anyway - and the old balance is cleared instead of quietly reused.

657d06d953134758769d273970853bd370e89c3e.text: After a period where advertisers could run campaigns for free, Freebuff has turned paid advertising back on, so businesses running promotions on the platform are now being charged again. This affects advertisers using the Freebuff self-serve ad marketplace, not developers or users of the coding assistant. Advertisers who publish posts through the Earn page will once again go through the normal checkout flow instead of having campaigns automatically marked as funded. Nothing changes for you unless you are buying ad space on Freebuff.

9501bb0a55ec3bbbd225e477130c427534dc3f11.title: Solar Pro 4 added to Freebuff free model picker
9501bb0a55ec3bbbd225e477130c427534dc3f11.summary: Solar Pro 4 (Upstage), served through OpenRouter and constrained to Upstage by `applyOpenRouterProviderRouting`, joins the Freebuff free model picker as a limited-time trial row in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` with the new identifier `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL_ID` set to `upstage/solar-pro4`. Three new agent definitions wire it into the base2, base3, and code-reviewer harnesses (`agents/base2/base2-free-solar-pro4.ts`, `agents/base3-free-solar-pro4.ts`, `agents/reviewer/code-reviewer-solar-pro4.ts`), and the model is registered across the root-agent, base3, reviewer, and desktop-bucket mappings in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`. The picker table now lists the row as Full access with 524,288 context, text only, and the `upstage/zdr` zero data retention tag, and the change set touches the README, README.zh-CN, and the CLI release README plus the chat agent's local context window map.
9501bb0a55ec3bbbd225e477130c427534dc3f11.evidence: Added `FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL_ID = 'upstage/solar-pro4'` and a `SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL` row to `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`; registered Solar Pro 4 roots and a reviewer via new entries in `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL`, `FREEBUFF_WEB_BASE3_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL`, `FREEBUFF_CLI_BASE3_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL`, `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`, `FREEBUFF_REVIEWER_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL` in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`; added the context window entry `upstage/solar-pro4` to `CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `agents/base-chat.ts`; and added Solar Pro 4 rows to `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md`.

changes.what: Added SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL row and FREEBUFF_SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL_ID constant; registered it in SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS, FREEBUFF_MODELS, FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS, FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_PREMIUM_BUCKET_MODEL_IDS, FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_MODELS, and FREEBUFF_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS.
Registered Solar Pro 4 base2, base3, and code-reviewer roots across the root-agent, base3-by-model, reviewer, and free-mode-agent-models mappings.
Added three new agent definition files for Solar Pro 4 orchestrators and reviewer.
Added Solar Pro 4 rows to the model picker tables in both English and Chinese READMEs plus the CLI release README.
Added upstage/solar-pro4 entry to the CONTEXT_WINDOWS map for chat thread pruning.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.title: CLI and Freebuff release manifests bumped
77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.summary: This release-bump commit increments the Codebuff CLI package from version 1.0.685 to 1.0.686 and the Freebuff CLI package from 0.0.161 to 0.0.162. Both edits land exclusively in their respective release package.json files with no accompanying code, model, or ad-routing changes in the snapshot.
77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.evidence: The diff shows only version field changes in cli/release/package.json (1.0.685 -> 1.0.686) and freebuff/cli/release/package.json (0.0.161 -> 0.0.162), with no other file modifications in the snapshot; the analysis notes confirm CLI release 1.0.686 published as a release-bump commit.

f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.title: Halve PAID and PRO PLUS credit limits and add Stripe customer
f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.summary: The `CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS` map in `common/src/constants.ts` now sets PAID to 5,000 and PRO_PLUS to 27,500 credits for production users (halved from 10,000 and 55,000), with matching reductions in the local overrides. A new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` migrates existing Stripe customers from the $99/month tier to a new price using `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, records prior usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`. These changes align with the commit message 'Cut costs and credits by half' and update billing documentation in `backend/src/billing/billing.knowledge.md` and `web/knowledge.md` with migration best practices. The pricing page in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` also adjusts displayed prices, now showing Pro at $49/month, Pro Plus at $249/month, and Team at $99/seat/month.

It also adds a new script `scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts` that reads `env.STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID` and `env.STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`, updates Stripe subscriptions for customers on the $99/mo plan, records usage via `billing.meterEvents.create` with `event_name: 'credits'`, and applies a coupon `wwu4ER94` with `proration_behavior: 'none'`.

f670fdb7932f87bef16edeb24cf73db2b5d6077d.unknowns: The actual rollout status of the new Stripe price IDs and whether the coupon applies to all customers or only a subset.
