42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash availability reopened; peak pause removed
42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` switches back to availability: 'always', reversing the 2026-08-24 peak closure after re-measurement showed its reopened row cost half the Luna fallback it routed traffic to and the Luminal lane now serves it cheaper by 4x. The corresponding `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_PEAK_PAUSED_MODEL_IDS` set in `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` was emptied, so plan sessions on Flash no longer pause inside peak hours and the `deepseekPeakHoursExcluded` tier disclaimer field was removed. The CLI release in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped to version 0.0.158. This is a behavior change to serving hours and a packaging increment, with two further edits to subscription tier shape.
42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, the `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL.availability` field changed from `'off_peak_only'` to `'always'`, with a 2026-08-28 comment stating the closure was reversed after re-measurement showed Flash's reopened row became half the price of the Luna fallback it routed to, and `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumped the version from 0.0.157 to 0.0.158. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`, `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_PEAK_PAUSED_MODEL_IDS` was emptied from `[FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID]` to `Object.freeze([])`, removing the peak-hours plan pause for DeepSeek V4 Flash.
42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.unknowns: The diff does not show when the Luminal lane capacity or the Luna prefix-cache routing shift was deployed, which is what made reopening safe. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: The `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL.availability` value moved from `'off_peak_only'` to `'always'` and the 2026-08-24 peak-closure rationale was replaced with a 2026-08-28 reopening note tied to re-measured Luna and Luminal prices.

The `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_PEAK_PAUSED_MODEL_IDS` constant was emptied to `Object.freeze([])` and the `deepseekPeakHoursExcluded` field was removed from the `FreebuffSubscriptionTier` interface and tier objects.
The release package version was incremented from 0.0.157 to 0.0.158.

3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.title: House ad copy now interpolates subscription price and sessions
3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.summary: The house subscription promotion in `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts` now reads the entry price and daily/monthly session counts from `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS` instead of hardcoding them, so copy drifts from the catalog rather than from a hardcoded number after the `starter` tier was resized on 2026-08-27. Each `HOUSE_AD_VARIATIONS` surface now carries four rotation frames (price, queue, model list, ads angles) with variation 0 pinned as the deterministic floor served by `HOUSE_AD_CREATIVES`, so the CTR creative bias has more than one angle to choose between and `HOUSE_AD_TITLE_BUDGET`/`HOUSE_AD_TEXT_BUDGET` are asserted against the real `getInlineAdLayout` rather than eyeballed. `MAX_PLACEMENT_CREATIVES_PER_CAMPAIGN` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` was raised from 10 to 25 so the house campaign can carry a variant per angle per surface without the builder form and the API disagreeing on the ceiling.
3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.evidence: Commit [3623ca3f] rewrites `common/src/constants/freebuff-house-ad.ts` to interpolate the price and session counts from `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS` (via `ENTRY_TIER`, `PRICE = $${ENTRY_TIER?.priceUsd ?? 8}/mo`, `SESSIONS_PER_DAY = ENTRY_TIER?.dailySessions ?? 3`, `SESSIONS_PER_MONTH = ENTRY_TIER?.monthlySessions ?? 50`), exports `HOUSE_AD_TITLE_BUDGET`, `HOUSE_AD_TEXT_BUDGET`, `HOUSE_AD_VARIATIONS`, `HOUSE_AD_DISPLAY_VARIATIONS`, and replaces the single static creative per surface with rotation arrays whose variation 0 backs `HOUSE_AD_CREATIVES`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` adds `MAX_PLACEMENT_CREATIVES_PER_CAMPAIGN = 25` (raised from 10) alongside a comment stating the house subscription campaign wants a variant per angle per surface.
3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.unknowns: The diff does not show the serve path that consumes `HOUSE_AD_VARIATIONS` and `MAX_PLACEMENT_CREATIVES_PER_CAMPAIGN`, so the rollout wiring and any campaign-builder UI changes that depend on the new ceiling are not visible here. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.title: SDK bumps bundled ripgrep to 15.2.0
a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.summary: The SDK refreshes its vendored ripgrep binaries from 14.1.1 to 15.2.0 and adds an arm64 Windows download entry in `fetch-ripgrep.ts`, so the next fetch-vendoring step pulls the newer release for all supported platforms. `getBundledRgPath` in `sdk/src/native/ripgrep.ts` now resolves the platform directory through a new exported helper backed by a `PLATFORM_DIRS` record, replacing the inline if/else chain, and a new binary lands at `sdk/vendor/ripgrep/arm64-win32/rg.exe` alongside re-vendored binaries for the other platforms. This change exists so the bundled code-search dependency can advance to the latest ripgrep release and cover Windows on arm64.
a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.evidence: The diff modifies `sdk/scripts/fetch-ripgrep.ts` to change `RIPGREP_VERSION` from '14.1.1' to '15.2.0' and adds an `arm64-win32` platform entry; it modifies `sdk/src/native/ripgrep.ts` to replace inline platform-directory if/else logic with a new exported function `ripgrepPlatformDir` backed by a `PLATFORM_DIRS` record; it also adds a new binary at `sdk/vendor/ripgrep/arm64-win32/rg.exe` and re-vendors updated binaries for all other platforms.
a4837a425cd7f9ac57d590d53a9ef1bc20fa63f6.unknowns: The consumer of the new ripgrepPlatformDir helper and rollout timing are not visible.

changes.what: Bumps vendored ripgrep version to 15.2.0 and adds an arm64-win32 platform entry.
Replaces inline platform-directory logic with an exported ripgrepPlatformDir helper backed by a PLATFORM_DIRS record.
Adds arm64-win32/rg.exe and re-vendors updated binaries for all other platforms.

38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.title: CPC yield experiment assignment and Imprezia ad outcome observer
38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.summary: Added `common/src/util/yield-experiment.ts` with FNV-1a-based `cpcYieldExperimentArmForUser` that assigns signed-in users to mutually exclusive control, shadow, or treatment arms using basis-point cohorts and a default salt `ads_cpc_yield_2026_08_27`, validated by `isValidCpcYieldExperimentConfig`. Extended `postToImprezia` in `common/src/util/imprezia-client.ts` with an optional `signal?` deadline and `onFailure` callback, and added the `ImpreziaChatAdOutcomeObserver` type threaded through `fetchImpreziaChatAd` via the new `onOutcome?` parameter to report bounded fill, no-fill, timeout, and provider-error outcomes. Wired the outcome observer through the existing abort path so a caller abort is reported as a `timeout` without exposing its reason, and expanded `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` with yield shadow and yield live telemetry fields.
38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.evidence: New file `common/src/util/yield-experiment.ts` defines `CPC_YIELD_EXPERIMENT_BASIS_POINTS`, `CPC_YIELD_EXPERIMENT_SALT`, `CpcYieldExperimentConfig`, `isValidCpcYieldExperimentConfig`, and `cpcYieldExperimentArmForUser`; `common/src/util/imprezia-client.ts` adds `ImpreziaChatAdOutcome`, `ImpreziaChatAdOutcomeObserver`, optional `signal?` and `onOutcome?` params, and an `onFailure` callback to `postToImprezia`; `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` adds yield shadow and yield live fields to `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS`.
38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.unknowns: The diff shows no reader yet consuming the new CPC yield experiment constants, so the policy is in place but inactive at runtime.

2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.title: Keep caller cancellation alive while Imprezia response body is read
2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.summary: postToImprezia in common/src/util/imprezia-client.ts now reads the response body inside the try block instead of after the response.ok check, so the AbortController timeout and the caller cancellation listener registered in the finally block remain active until response.json() is consumed. The previous layout resolved the return value before the finally block, which could leave the caller cancellation listener removed before the body finished streaming. The body read is now wrapped in a catch that re-throws genuine aborts while routing malformed JSON to the existing null-body path.
2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.evidence: The 'finally' block in postToImprezia now sits after the return statement for the response body instead of before it, and the body is read with response.json() inside the try block rather than after the response.ok check.
2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.unknowns: The commit message does not state what operational symptom motivated the change, such as stalls observed in Ad request failed or timed out logs. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

dc18d1a2063a92cc1939648a0280c0847a662c73.text: The Freebuff CLI now has a '/diagnostics' command that displays local resource usage (CPU, memory, uptime) and the process IDs of currently running terminal tools, without exposing command-line arguments or environment variables for security reasons. This change affects Freebuff CLI users on the free tier who may need to share debugging information when reporting issues. When you run '/diagnostics' in a Freebuff chat, the app outputs a formatted summary of its current process state directly in the conversation, which you can then copy into a bug report or support request.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new /export command to save your conversations to a file in markdown or JSON, puts Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 coding model into the free model picker across the CLI, Web, Desktop, and Cloud, and swaps GLM 5.3 Flash back in as the default free model after it briefly led the list. Solar Pro 4 moves to unmetered access at full tier and limited access for everyone else, while a new Freebucks meter in the CLI shows model prices as currency and carries an intro card the first time you see a metered model. Sponsored ad proposals gain a one-sentence consent screen with yes/no choices, per-model rate caps and spend ceilings, and account-deletion proofs are now HMAC-shielded so Convex purges cannot be forged. If you are a free user, the landing screen now shows week and month windows alongside today, and near-limit warnings trigger at 80 percent usage. Upgrading gives you a conversation-export command, the Muse Spark 1.3 coding model with a 1M-token context on the free tier, and a clearer Freebucks cost display that tells you exactly how much credit each model consumes before you pick it.

c3521fd87fc4c8f683e73c08251772dc976ca8ec.text: Freebuff now creates a tamper-proof digital receipt that confirms an account deletion has been fully processed before any permanent purge happens on the backend servers. Only the Freebuff operations team, not developers or end users, consumes this verification step. For users there is no visible change today; it silently strengthens the safety check that guards against deleting something still mid-deletion. Because nothing presented to browsers reads this proof, no user-facing feature ships now, though the code is live and enforced behind the scenes.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release updates the Freebuff CLI with a refreshed set of AI models and new ad and session-handling behavior. The free model picker now defaults to DeepSeek V4 Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna is added as a new selectable free model, Kimi K2.7 Code is removed, and MiniMax M3, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and MiMo 2.5 are marked as superseded so the picker steers you toward newer options. Ads in responses now show the first one later and space them farther apart, and the landing screen adapts its layout to fit compact terminals. New sessions that hit the daily budget now get a clear message telling you to run a command to end them before switching models, and the exit handling consolidates all quit paths through one cleanup routine. If a network stream drops mid-response, the CLI now retries the connection automatically instead of stopping. Upgrading gives you the latest free models, clearer session and budget messages, fewer dropped responses, and a landing screen that fits smaller windows.

6a4ad1d04afdcc25bf6aea1e3503199ae65e39c3.text: Freebuff has replaced the Meta Muse Spark model it offers, moving everyone who was using the older version onto the newer one, while the older option is quietly taken off the menu. The only people this affects are those using the Freebuff web or cloud version (it never reaches the desktop or terminal app), so anyone coding in the browser will automatically see the upgraded helper appear instead. The old model will still finish any work you already started, but no new tasks get sent to it, and your saved choice gets rewritten behind the scenes so you do not have to switch anything yourself. For now the change is live: you can use the newer model, and there is nothing else you need to do.

590e6d257bf4128557f1e5823077c586bb424138.text: A campaign being deliberately wound down now spreads its remaining posts across each rolling hour of the day instead of releasing a burst at the Pacific-day reset. This affects advertisers running a capped ad campaign that is tapering its daily budget. You will not notice anything, because only advertisers see these delivery caps, and they only change when a campaign is set to wind down.

57c010db236b4b5ffba7030cb4eff4bb50a4a333.text: When you open the model picker in the Freebuff CLI, paying subscribers now see a small line that states the name of their plan tier and the usage limits for the day, the last five days, and the current billing cycle, using the same wording and numbers that the web and desktop versions show. If a limit is currently preventing usage, an extra row appears beneath that line naming which limit is full and how long until it resets, except for the five-day rolling window which has no single reset time. The picker's first frame now reserves space for these new rows so that blocked users no longer see the warning clipped off the bottom of the screen.

8542dfe658589b2433a7d039b031d1e0eab1be07.text: The engineers who set the rules for Freebuff's ad system added the building blocks for a new trust score that will one day decide how much unpaid ad spend an advertiser can run. These are just the rule numbers and limits for now, like a speed-limit sign that exists before any car is on the road, and nothing in the app reads them yet. This is internal setup work for advertisers who pay to show Freebuff's first-party text ads, not for people using the free coding assistant. You will not see or feel this change in your coding sessions today.

3623ca3ffeb9e8ed71a65207075c1d4d18e639f3.text: The house ads that promote Freebuff's paid plans are now generated directly from the subscription catalog (price per month, sessions per day, sessions per month), instead of being hand-written as static strings. Freebuff's own promotion copy is for internal use only (maintainers), so subscribers, free users, and advertisers are not affected; the floor fallback ad still reads the same, it just stays in sync with the subscription catalog automatically. In practice you see no difference yet, because the copy is still seeded into a campaign and the strings that print are unchanged at this moment.

42989afa85b9d0c2cf43c220309ef9f05951d3bb.text: The DeepSeek V4 Flash model is available to use at all hours again, including during times when it was previously paused. This matters for you if you use the assistant during what used to be peak hours, when the system used to switch you to a different, more expensive model instead. The peak-hour pause and its explanatory text have been removed from the paid subscription plans, so you no longer see a note saying DeepSeek models are unavailable during weekday peak hours. If you are a developer using the Freebuff command-line tool, you will get the updated version (0.0.158) that includes this change, and there is nothing you need to do to turn it on.

cb3ef3135c27c68f08c1c3e92290607a08732afc.text: The daily limit of two GLM 5.3 Flash sessions per user has been removed, so the model now draws from the same shared session pool as other models instead of its own separate, capped bucket. It applies to anyone on the Freebuff free tier (CLI, web, or desktop) who uses the Freebuff model picker. You will no longer see the earlier message that warned about a two-a-day cap on this model, and you can use it up to the limit of your normal daily sessions, like the other models in the catalog. This change is in effect today, following the cap being lifted on 2026-08-27 once its cost was confirmed.

2f4829e864d268f1cd6987537fd7956f6c67d0dc.text: Freebuff has added new marketing text and pricing information for a last-resort advertisement that only appears when no paid ads can fill a space, so the company never leaves an ad slot blank. The price shown in these ads now automatically matches the current subscription pricing instead of being written in manually, preventing outdated prices from being advertised. This affects anyone using the free version of Freebuff who sees ads in the chat interface, waiting room, or web/desktop app, and they will now see up-to-date promotional messaging that directs them to the pricing page.

8f390e940d2f9457ea52bca4567f727f0a049277.text: When the assistant is thinking through a problem, its reasoning sometimes leaks into the main text display instead of staying in the separate thinking section. Freebuff has updated the agent runtime to better detect and redirect this leaked reasoning back into the proper thinking area. Users of the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, and SDK may notice this change when the assistant is working through complex tasks. No action is required on your part; the correction happens automatically behind the scenes.

2cf1163dc72fd40df1b7d56a4ed94d668116dc47.text: The ad request handler now waits to finish reading the response data before cleaning up its timeout and cancellation tracking, so a slow ad server can no longer cause the app to lose track of an in-flight request. This is an internal reliability fix used only by Freebuff's ad-serving systems. You will not see this change in the chat or coding assistant. It is live today. The change affects how Freebuff fetches and displays its first-party text ads. It keeps the internal ad request logic correct when ad servers respond slowly, which only matters to the systems that choose which ads to show. You do not interact with this change directly, and it does not affect your coding sessions, message limits, or Freebucks balance. No action is needed.

38feaebb146a689d5dbf3a38b322e7db2e63f071.text: Engineers added a behind-the-scenes system that sorts signed-in users into one of three groups (a control group, a shadow group that watches without changing anything, and a treatment group that tests a new approach) so they can quietly experiment with how to make ad revenue per click more effective without risking the experience for most people. They also built a new observation tool that records whether each ad request succeeds, fails, times out, or gets no ad, purely so the team can measure performance in aggregate. This is internal plumbing for the Freebuff service operators that does not change anything you see or do in your coding sessions today. No visible impact, no action needed, and advertisers have no settings or budgets tied to this at the moment.

Existing LinkedIn comment-URL validation that previously fell through to the LinkedIn shape is now guarded by the explicit github branch.

4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.title: First-party ad views get resilient acknowledgement transport
4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.summary: A new acknowledgement module in `@codebuff/common/ads/first-party-view-ack` records first-party ad impressions with a best-effort retry sequence: three attempts at a two-second timeout each with 250ms and 1s bounded delays, retrying only server errors, timeouts, and network failures, never 4xx responses. The CLI's `useGravityAd` hook now dispatches this transport only for `first_party` providers, leaving third-party ads on the legacy pixel path, and surfaces observations as the operational-only event `ads.first_party_view_ack` through a server-validated telemetry allowlist that rejects any unknown fields. The landing-screen ad banner now orders ads by canonical request order via `orderedRequestedAds` and reads visible waiting-room placements from a new `waiting-room-placements.ts` module instead of the local `MIN_CARD_WIDTH` constant.
4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.evidence: New module `common/src/ads/first-party-view-ack.ts` defines `acknowledgeFirstPartyView`, retry delays, and outcome constants, and is wired into impression recording in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` via `dispatchFirstPartyViewAcknowledgement`, with telemetry validation added in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` and a new `AnalyticsEvent.ADS_FIRST_PARTY_VIEW_ACK` event in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`.
4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.migration: No action is required; first-party ad acknowledgement is enabled automatically when an ad is served to a waiting-room or inline surface.

8238d829cad6ce2b95694de923e6e58c9a240e5d.title: Add monthly spend ceiling to Freebuff subscription tiers
8238d829cad6ce2b95694de923e6e58c9a240e5d.summary: The FreebuffSubscriptionTier interface in `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts` now carries a `monthlySpendLimitUsd` field, set to `40` for Starter and `100` for Plus, and `freebuffSubscriptionTierDisclaimers` pushes a new disclaimer string referencing that value. The matching session type `FreebuffSubscriptionTierOffer` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adds `monthlySpendLimitUsd`, while `FreebuffSubscriptionUsage` adds `monthSpendUsd` and `monthSpendLimitUsd` to report provider spend against the tier ceiling, and `FreebuffSubscriptionInfo.blockedBy` gains a `'monthly_spend'` case to gate the paywall when the ceiling is spent. 3975224904d989f60ad8db9139bf51b7390e67c0.text: The assistant can now show special "sponsored proposal" cards in the chat - these are offers from companies who paid to have their work done in your project. For now, nothing actually shows these cards yet because the code to make them appear hasn't been turned on, but the system is ready. You gain five new commands starting with `/ads:` like `/ads:proposal` to interact with these cards (opening menus, dismissing offers, reporting, or turning them off permanently). The cards also follow rules so a failed action won't get stuck looking finished, and the keyboard controls won't fight with what you're typing.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This Freebuff release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model you get when coding for free across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, and adds Solar Pro 4 (from Upstage) as another free option in the model picker. It introduces a new `/reasoning` slash command that lets you control how deeply the selected model thinks before answering, with your choice saved per model in your settings. The desktop app's auto-run agent now properly recognizes the updated service path, the CLI copy-to-clipboard now falls back to OSC 52 when native clipboard tools are unavailable, and the spend ceiling system now blocks accounts using VPNs or privacy networks unless they connect directly, replacing the flat $50 daily limit with per-account ceilings that vary by region and risk. Ad billing for placements is enabled again after a free-campaign window, campaign durations are capped at 7 days, and the Trust engagement ladder now drives free and premium session bonuses through 11 rungs. Upgrading gives you a new default model, optional deeper reasoning control, better clipboard reliability in the terminal, and improved protection against abusive accounts that try to exploit the free compute credits.

a49b46d62f39fd4cf45e3ba02499b8aefbca0d24.text: When you run out of free coding hours in Freebuff, your terminal now shows a button or link to upgrade to a paid plan instead of just leaving you stuck with no next step. If you are a Freebuff developer using the command-line tool, you will now see an option to move to a paid tier when you hit your daily or weekly free-session limit. It does not change how many free sessions you get, but it does let you reach a paid plan quickly from the same screen that told you to come back later.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a /export slash command so you can save a conversation to a markdown or JSON file, brings Meta Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor into the free model picker across CLI, Desktop, Web, and Cloud, and makes Solar Pro 4 available in limited mode as an unmetered option for full-access users while removing its experimental label. Concrete highlights: (1) You can now type /export [filename] mid-chat to write the current conversation to a file in your project root, with.json files saved as raw JSON and anything else rendered as the same markdown view as /copy, so your discussions are no longer trapped in the terminal. (2) The free model picker now includes Muse Spark 1.3, a Meta coding model with a one-million-token context that is rate-limited and shared across users, falling back to DeepSeek V4 Flash when busy, and the CLI gains three new bundled agent roots tuned for it. (3) A referral or streak reward now grants full-tier users an extra daily premium session instead of unlocking GLM 5.2, and the CLI landing screen shows an upgrade prompt beneath rate-limited and spend-limited session screens so a walled free session can reach a paid plan. (4) Sponsored proposal work added local consent flows, git-worktree execution boundaries, a /ads:accept-proposal command, and a one-sentence consent dialog, while a new sponsor dock detail panel (Ctrl+O) and Escape-to-close behavior let you inspect sponsored ad details without disrupting other keyboard shortcuts. Everyday impact: Upgrading gives you a way to persist and share conversations, expands the free tier with a 1M-token coding model plus an unmetered Solar Pro 4 option, and makes referral rewards more flexible for premium users, while hardening how sponsored runs execute locally and how ad-driven sessions surface in the terminal. The model selector now prices rows by Freebucks balance instead of legacy session counts, the Freebucks intro card appears once on first metered launch, and monthly reset waits render in day-scale terms so quota walls read in plain language. Account deletion proofs and placement CPC floor validators tighten safety around identity purges and ad billing, and geo-aware first-party ad routing plus Imprezia viewability tracking make served ads more accountable without changing what you see.

adbcb4e4a515334bd3f46580fe8188ba3d27bf84.text: The referral promotion for advertisers has been simplified so that a referring advertiser qualifies for a reward only after the new advertiser has both paid in and spent at least one hundred dollars on an active, reviewed campaign, and then each side receives five hundred dollars in credit. This change affects advertisers who buy ad placements on Freebuff, not developers using the coding assistant. The new rule is already live, but it only applies to advertisers running the referral promotion, so individual users will not notice any difference in their coding sessions or credits.

6f7cf660e827d750b278497432eebfa763ca58e5.text: Freebuff added support for a second kind of ad to its technical code-assistant tool. When someone using the free version opens a new browser tab in the desktop app, the software can now fetch and display a promotional message there, in addition to the ads it already shows during chat conversations. The change is internal infrastructure, so end users probably won't notice anything different right away. It is live today, but only takes effect once the team finishes wiring the new ad slot into the actual screen.

47c4bf8cf7f311a30adfb47f4ca09d914cc3ce9a.text: The changes are internal settings that define how Freebuff's advertising system handles advertiser billing rules, such as minimum click prices, automatic price adjustments, and how disputed payments are recorded. These are configuration constants and ledger updates for the ads side of the system, and no runtime code consumes them yet, so they do nothing visible today. Advertisers do not see this change yet, and it does not affect your Freebuff coding sessions, credits, or personal quotas. This is internal preparation work for the advertising platform, not a feature available to end users.

9066513a775a950c3c5f620141e41cd8ebfc76b3.text: The Freebuff team added a timer that tells the desktop app how long to hold onto a free session when nothing is happening. It is set to ten minutes, which the developers say is meant to roughly cover the time you spend reading a long answer and typing your next message. Nothing in the app uses this timer yet, so it has no effect on your sessions right now. When it is turned on later, it will stop a desktop tab from sitting idle and blocking everyone else from using their free model.

e30c58d37ea03426da0f01a727c5acff3895a462.text: When you ask the assistant for a model that has been permanently withdrawn from the free tier, the session now starts on the default replacement model and immediately shows you a system message naming the model you picked and the recommended one, instead of silently beginning on a different model. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web, or desktop app who picks a model that later disappears from the free list. You will see the explanatory note at the top of your new session when this happens, and your saved model preference stays unchanged for next time.

b3e1d17c5a89e05ad7692f0dd70466a97851a3c7.text: Freebuff's crash reporting system was sending one billable error report to PostHog for every single repeat of the same bug, which on one bad day generated over a million reports from a client stuck in a loop. The fix caps how many times the same error gets reported (the first, then the 10th, 100th, 1000th, etc.) and keeps a true count on each surviving report. This is an internal cost-control measure on the analytics backend, so you see no change in how the assistant runs or how crashes appear.}.

28d0514641dc8804ec29db0727c13bb9f2bc2ca1.text: When you buy a Freebuff subscription, its sessions now add on top of the free ones you already had, rather than replacing them. So if you used to get 5 free sessions and your plan adds 4 more, today you can use 9 total instead of losing the 5 free ones. You now see the same combined total whether you look at the session panel or any of the model menus, since both now read from the same up-to-date count. Quota-exempt accounts (god/admin) also now receive an honest report of the free portion of their allowance, though it still does not limit them, and the free usage numbers now drive every place the total is shown.

9043277365c41dd3d8c20f4d192b64d879823dce.text: Advertisers setting up a paid promotion now start from a written prompt instead of picking from four generated sample comments, and the system tells people who engage with those promotions to write their own original comment rather than copy a suggested one. The change affects the advertiser marketplace inside Freebuff, so it applies to advertisers and sponsors buying ad placements and running sponsored campaigns. When you engage with one of these promoted posts, you now see a short list of rules asking you to write something genuine and specific yourself, and the advertiser's campaign form is prefilled with default guidance so an advertiser with no strong opinion still ships useful instructions. It is live today for advertisers creating new campaigns, and existing campaigns are unaffected.

c359f63c20bbc0f7d23fb950af7764257b6ec274.text: When a model that costs more during busy hours is temporarily closed, the assistant now tells you exactly when it reopens using a single, clearly labeled time instead of a vague phrase. The message names the timezone (for example "10:00 AM UTC") so you do not have to guess which clock it refers to, and on the CLI, Desktop, and web app the same moment is shown in your own local timezone. You just get a clearer, unambiguous answer to "when can I use that model again?" with no action required on your part.

72f1310353bddeacfee88d760a6193527ff69dd2.text: Freebuff has removed the daily limit on how many of your paid sessions can use the most powerful AI models (GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Pro), so on both the Starter and Plus plans you can now spend all of your daily sessions on those premium models if you want to. This affects anyone who subscribes to the paid Freebuff tiers. In everyday use, you will no longer see the restriction that said only a portion of your daily sessions could be spent on the fancier models, and the plan descriptions on the website and app have been updated to drop that now-inaccurate rule.

ec01bf10020d29d13062f0218f3176e5a0e3f4b0.text: Freebuff added two clear, written reasons to its ad-placement console: one for when a campaign has been paused because it hit its daily spending limit (it resumes at midnight Pacific time), and one for when a campaign has fully spent its total budget. This change is configuration and copy only in a shared constants file, so it defines the exact wording advertisers will see but does not by itself wire that wording into any visible ad surface. Advertisers are the only audience who will notice this, and only once the console surfaces start actually reading these new reasons. The feature is in place in code today, but the diff does not show any consumer change that renders the new messages yet.

cb3ea78eda6ea14b43bc1624d0e854fdd9a898d0.text: Freebuff's ad system now lets advertisers promote their work on GitHub by asking users to star a repository, which is a single click with no comment required. This affects only the paid advertising program that runs alongside Freebuff, not Freebuff's free coding features or your usage allowance in any way. You will not see anything different unless you are an advertiser setting up a campaign, in which case GitHub appears as a simpler ad option with a star instead of a comment. The change is live today.

8238d829cad6ce2b95694de923e6e58c9a240e5d.text: A monthly spending cap has been added to Freebuff's paid subscription plans, with Starter subscribers getting $40 and Plus subscribers $100 per month. This cap works alongside the existing session limits, meaning that if a subscriber hits this dollar amount, their paid plan sessions pause until the next billing cycle while their free sessions continue to work. The pricing page text has also been updated to explain that these spending limits can change. No action is needed from subscribers, since the assistant will automatically enforce this new spending limit when it applies.

4a41787b377f56263a296bc5a8458ad2707aafae.text: The assistant now sends a more reliable message to confirm it actually showed you a first-party advertisement. When an ad appears on the landing screen or inline in the chat, the client attempts to record that view with a resilient transport that retries only on genuine server or network issues, never on bad requests. This applies only to in-house ads served by Freebuff; ads from external networks continue using the older pixel-based tracking. Nothing requires your action, and you will not notice anything different unless an ad previously failed to register as viewed. It is live today as part of the Freebuff CLI, web, desktop and chat surfaces.

10218ba5aa9794a3327524cc1922daa9f3e39ce1.text: Freebuff now shows you, while a peak-priced model is open, the local-time window when it is available (for example, "Open 3:00 AM - 5:00 PM"), so you can plan a session around it instead of learning the model is shut only when you try to use it. This visible label applies to Freebuff users who pick from the free model list or read model hints in the picker; it does not change which models exist or how many free sessions you have today. A few behind-the-scenes fields were also added so future paywalls and plan-pause messages can be worded correctly, but those have no effect until later versions wire them up, so you will not notice them yet.

38b9fb0ffb5f0f14035dcf78969d153d7b0acfd8.title: Sponsored proposal accept and run land in the Freebuff CLI terminal
38b9fb0ffb5f0f14035dcf78969d153d7b0acfd8.summary: Add Phase 2 of the sponsored proposal channel to the CLI: the /ads:accept-proposal, /ads:pull-request and /ads:remove-worktree slash commands and the consent panel that gates them. Accepting opens an in-terminal consent that can refuse and starts nothing, then a linked worktree is cut under the project's .freebuff directory and the advertiser's procedure runs sandboxed on this machine. The polling producer (useSponsoredProposal) and the store callbacks (onSponsoredProposalAccept / onSponsoredProposalConsent) are new, and exit-cleanly.ts now settles an interrupted sponsored run to a terminal state and prints a notice naming the workspace and branch.

New modules sponsored-agent.ts, sponsored-availability.ts, sponsored-proposal-target.ts, sponsored-run-exit.ts, sponsored-run.ts, sponsored-worktree.ts, and use-sponsored-proposal.ts are added.

Adds the accept and state-report REST transport with detailed failure reasons.

7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.title: Consent-bridge refusal and macOS device node grants
7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.summary: A sponsored local run that cannot reach a desktop consent screen now fails with a new `no-consent-bridge` reason and dedicated copy in the card, instead of being blamed on the operating system. The macOS sandbox profile gains `SPONSORED_DEVICE_WRITE_LITERALS` for `/dev/null`, `SPONSORED_DEVICE_WRITE_SUBPATHS` for `/dev/fd`, and `SPONSORED_RESOLVER_READ_LITERALS` for `/dev` and `/var`, so a toolchain can write `/dev/null` and the `/dev/fd` stdio aliases without widening the boundary. Linux containment mounts a fresh `/dev` through `bwrap --dev` so the device enumeration concern does not apply on this arm. The change is grounded in the ablation measurements recorded beside each constant.
7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.evidence: The diff adds a new `no-consent-bridge` reason to the `SponsoredLocalUnavailableReason` type and a matching entry in `SPONSORED_LOCAL_UNAVAILABLE_COPY` in `common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts`, and defines new device and resolver literals plus their use in `sponsoredMacProfile` and `spawnLinux` in `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`.
7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.unknowns: The diff does not show which caller supplies the consent bridge state that drives the new `no-consent-bridge` reason or when that wiring lands.

changes.what: Added `no-consent-bridge` to `SponsoredLocalUnavailableReason` and a corresponding sentence in `SPONSORED_LOCAL_UNAVAILABLE_COPY` so a missing consent window is not misreported as an unsupported platform.

Added `SPONSORED_DEVICE_WRITE_LITERALS`, `SPONSORED_DEVICE_WRITE_SUBPATHS`, and `SPONSORED_RESOLVER_READ_LITERALS` constants and wired them into `sponsoredMacProfile` so git can write `/dev/null` and `/dev/fd` stdio aliases while loopback and other device nodes stay denied.

Clarified the Linux arm to mount a fresh `/dev` via `bwrap --dev` rather than enumerate host device nodes, noting the behavior is read from bubblewrap documentation and not yet verified on a Linux host.

115a6a5cc676b1a4969d2045ad34ebb5d8bd00ab.summary: `validateOnboardingSubmission` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` no longer treats an unanswered question as an error, so a submission with some questions left blank passes validation and only the answered questions are persisted. Re-exported extractDomain, getAdDisplayLabel, and getInlineAdLayout from common and removed their local definitions.

ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash reopens at peak, V4 Pro closes, Flash becomes
ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 switches from `off_peak_only` to availability: 'always' and drops its `unavailableFallback` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, while DeepSeek V4 Pro flips to `availability: 'off_peak_only'` with `unavailableFallback: FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID` because Pro returned to the DeepSeek direct lane that doubles rates at peak and Flash is the cheaper row users are steered to. `FREEBUFF_MODELS` reorders to lead with `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL`, and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` now resolve to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID` so a default is joinable at every hour. `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` re-adds the `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` entry at limit 1, and `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` rewrites the peak-window message to describe Pro closing rather than Flash.
ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL.availability` changed from `off_peak_only` to `always` and its `unavailableFallback` was removed; `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL.availability` changed from `always` to `off_peak_only` and adds `unavailableFallback: FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`; `FREEBUFF_MODELS` reorders to lead with `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL`; `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` now resolve to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`; `FREEBUFF_PER_MODEL_SESSION_CAPS` re-adds the `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` entry with limit 1; README files and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md` update the default model and caps text; `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` in `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts` rewrites the peak closure message.
ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.migration: No action required: existing Freebuff sessions keep running on their current model, and surfaces that know the live quota continue to step down to `FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` once the daily premium pool is spent.
ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.unknowns: The diff does not show updated consumer code in the Web/Cloud picker or CLI model selector that reads the reordered rows and new caps at this revision.

changes.what: Flips DeepSeek V4 Flash to `availability: 'always'` and removes its `unavailableFallback`; flips DeepSeek V4 Pro to `availability: 'off_peak_only'` with `unavailableFallback: FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`; reorders `FREEBUFF_MODELS` to lead with Flash; sets `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID`.
Rewrites `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` from describing Flash pausing at peak to describing V4 Pro pausing at peak with a limit of 1.
Updates the Models table and limits paragraph to lead with DeepSeek V4 Flash as the default and describe V4 Pro as one session a day paused during peak hours.
Mirrors the English README model table and limits paragraph updates for the Chinese documentation.
Updates the FAQ model paragraph and default-model line to name DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 as the CLI default, and rewrites the peak closure description to say V4 Pro is paused during peak hours.

1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.title: SDK translates Git Bash paths before resolving file paths
1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.summary: The SDK file tools now translate Git Bash style paths to native Windows paths before resolving them, so an MSYS drive path like /c/Users is mapped to C:\Users inline, while a single-leading-slash path is resolved via cygpath.exe spawned from the detected Git for Windows bash. This fixes path resolution for agents that emit POSIX-style paths in the Git Bash shell the SDK exposes on Windows, where native absolute paths retain their drive or UNC prefix. The change is confined to the @codebuff/sdk packages/sdk path utilities and the windows-bash path translation module.
1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.evidence: Commit 1e69baf9 adds translateGitBashPath, isGitBashAbsolutePath, resetTranslationCache, and the WindowsShellPathDependencies type to sdk/src/tools/windows-bash.ts, and rewires resolveFilePathWithinProject, resolveFilePath, and getProjectPathLookupKeys in sdk/src/tools/path-utils.ts to call translateGitBashPath(filePath, dependencies) instead of passing filePath through path.isAbsolute directly.
1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.migration: No action required; existing SDK callers that rely on default dependencies continue to work, as the new behavior falls back to the original path when bash or cygpath is unavailable.
1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.unknowns: The diff shows the path translation layer and its tests but does not show which SDK consumers call run_terminal_command or the Desktop surfaces that consume the translated paths in production.

3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.title: Drop peak-hours spend ceiling reduction from billing and session types
3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.summary: The peak-hours spend-ceiling reduction feature is removed from `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts`: the `at` and `peakMultiplier` inputs are dropped from `FreebuffSpendCeilingInput`, the `peak` field is removed from `FreebuffSpendCeiling`, and `resolveFreebuffSpendCeiling` no longer applies a reduction, returning the winning ceiling's `usd` directly. Corresponding exports fall away in `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` (`isDeepSeekPeakHour`, `nextDeepSeekWindowBoundary`, `formatDeepSeekPeakWindowsLocal`), and the `spend_limited` variant of `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` loses its `peak` object so clients no longer receive peak window detail on a spend-limit rejection. `resolveFreebuffHardSpendCeiling` is unchanged.
3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.evidence: Removed exports `isDeepSeekPeakHour`, `nextDeepSeekWindowBoundary`, `formatDeepSeekPeakWindowsLocal`, `FREEBUFF_PEAK_LIMIT_NOTICE`, and `FreebuffSpendCeilingPeak` from `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` and `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts`; deleted the `peak` field from `FreebuffSpendCeiling` and the `at`/`peakMultiplier` inputs from `FreebuffSpendCeilingInput`; removed the `peak` object on the `spend_limited` status in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`.
3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.migration: Any caller importing `isDeepSeekPeakHour`, `nextDeepSeekWindowBoundary`, `formatDeepSeekPeakWindowsLocal`, `FREEBUFF_PEAK_LIMIT_NOTICE`, `FreebuffSpendCeilingPeak`, or reading `FreebuffSpendCeiling.peak`, `FreebuffSpendCeilingInput.at`, `FreebuffSpendCeilingInput.peakMultiplier`, or the `spend_limited` status's `peak` object must drop those references.
3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.unknowns: The diff does not show whether a replacement peak-hours UI or a different mechanism for communicating temporary allowances exists, or which consumer previously read these exports.

9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.title: Model picker shows peak-hour return time for closed rows
9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.summary: The CLI model selector now imports `getFreebuffModelUnavailableLabel` from `@codebuff/common/constants/freebuff-models` and renders a per-row `closedNote` so non-deployment-hours closures display a return-time label instead of only greying the row. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `isFreebuffModelAvailable` and `isFreebuffSessionModelAvailable` are refactored onto a shared `isAvailableAt` helper so the picker's joinability check and the session admission check read availability identically, and `getFreebuffModelUnavailableLabel` returns a local-time Back at <time> string for `off_peak_only` models using `deepSeekExpensiveWindowEndsAt`. `common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts` rewrites `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` to a shorter three-clause signed notice while `FREEBUFF_PAUSED_MODEL_NOTICE` is unchanged.
9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.evidence: Imports `getFreebuffModelUnavailableLabel` from `@codebuff/common/constants/freebuff-models` into `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` and calls it per row to render a `closedNote` label alongside `deploymentAvailabilityLabel`; defines `getFreebuffModelUnavailableLabel` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` returning Back at <time> for `off_peak_only` models via `deepSeekExpensiveWindowEndsAt`; refactors `isFreebuffModelAvailable` and `isFreebuffSessionModelAvailable` onto a shared `isAvailableAt` helper in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`; replaces the inline `off_peak_only` check in `isFreebuffSessionModelAvailable`.

Adds `getFreebuffModelUnavailableLabel` and refactors both availability checks onto a shared `isAvailableAt` helper.
Rewrites `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` to a shorter signed notice; `FREEBUFF_PAUSED_MODEL_NOTICE` is unchanged.

7f41c17658f1631e318a9aa7b0e4d9bd26ad58da.text: The error message shown when a sponsored task cannot ask you for permission has been made clearer and more accurate: instead of blaming the operating system, it now tells you that the Freebuff desktop app must be opened to approve the task first. The macOS sandbox profile was also adjusted to allow a tool to write to /dev/null and the /dev/fd standard-stream aliases it needs to run, without granting broader access to the rest of the /dev directory. These changes are live today and affect anyone who runs sponsored tasks locally, most noticeably on macOS where a toolchain that previously failed to start inside the sandbox can now execute git init, add, commit, and log correctly; Windows users remain told that sponsored tasks are not supported on their operating system.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release reshuffles Freebuff's free AI model lineup and tightens up ad-supported access controls. GLM 5.3 Flash becomes the default free model across the CLI and web, and Solar Pro 4 joins the picker as a limited-time option, while DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiniMax M3 are pulled from the free catalog. A new /reasoning command lets you request or check how deeply the chosen model thinks through its work, and desktop sessions can now auto-run a planning agent without hitting credit errors. Ad delivery shifts to first-party placements with sanitized creative text and a daily-budget taper that smooths spending, and signups can be gated by reCAPTCHA with distinct failure reasons. Time-gated models now show readable return windows in your local time, and referral-abuse detection gets stricter with more disposable-email domains blocked and a one-star-per-day cap on GLM 5.2 referrals. Upgrading means you start on GLM 5.3 Flash by default, gain a /reasoning knob for model depth, and see clearer refusal messages when a model is closed or capacity is limited.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This CLI release adds a new /export command so you can save an entire conversation to a file, ships the Freebucks currency meter so metered models show a per-model price and your remaining balance instead of abstract session counts, and swaps the Freebuff free default back to GLM 5.3 Flash while also widening Muse Spark 1.3 to the CLI, Desktop, Web and Cloud pickers. The landing screen now shows upgrade prompts when you hit rate or spend limits instead of dead-ending, referral rewards now grant an extra full-tier premium session per day, and Solar Pro 4 is treated as a limited-access unmetered model with a 1-session-a-day measurement window. The sponsored-proposal flow now refuses to proceed while a proposal cannot refresh, and the desktop premium bucket drops GLM 5.3 Flash since its unmetering invalidated the concurrency cap. You get a clearer free-to-paid path when you run out of free sessions, accurate token usage that no longer double-counts cache reads, and a model picker that surfaces real per-session pricing and remaining balance for the models you actually use.

dc2947f208c695a64f1781053d8afe1a3968a40a.text: When the assistant talks to an AI model and that model sends back a problem partway through its reply (rather than stopping cleanly), the system now captures the full reason for the failure instead of a vague summary. Developers who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK will see clearer error messages when a model refuses or breaks mid-response, so it's easier to understand what went wrong. No action is required from you, and the change is already live.

dd1d934b7418b612d453d52e5fc2091011923dbc.text: Freebuff now opens every new session on DeepSeek V4 Flash instead of GLM 5.3 Flash, so you start coding with a faster, unmetered model by default. This affects anyone who uses the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or cloud sessions. If you had previously let Freebuff default to GLM 5.3 Flash, your saved pick quietly switches to DeepSeek V4 Flash on first launch, while any model you picked yourself stays unchanged.

38b9fb0ffb5f0f14035dcf78969d153d7b0acfd8.text: A sponsored proposal is an advertiser-funded task that an advertiser offers to run against your repository, paid for by the advertiser rather than billed to you. This update adds the ability to accept and run such a proposal directly in the Freebuff CLI terminal, so you no longer need to switch to the web or desktop surface to act on an offer that lands in your terminal chat. It is live for Freebuff CLI users today where the feature is reachable, and the effect you notice is a new in-terminal consent screen and the ability to run the task in an isolated workspace on your own machine. The audience is Freebuff CLI users who have been offered a sponsored proposal in their transcript.

4ff202b7d262eb975b755a5da73965c661801cc6.text: When you run out of free sessions or hit a spending cap, the system now attaches a direct upgrade suggestion (with a URL and message) to the refusal response, so paywalls can point you to the next step instead of leaving each app to hardcode its own. The subscription disclaimers and plan displays now describe session allowances in hours and use the word 'tokens' where it previously said 'compute'. This affects users of the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, and SDK who encounter rate-limited or spend-limited refusals or view subscription plan details. In daily use, refusals now carry a clickable upgrade path when one is available, and tier descriptions now consistently read in hours with clearer token language.

061b2465fb339069a9a7b09081c6125a5919a574.text: GPT-5.6 Luna is now the model Freebuff picks by default when you start a new full-access session, with DeepSeek V4 Flash returning to a fallback role. This is live today for Freebuff users in supported regions using the CLI, desktop app, or web; the previous default had been DeepSeek V4 Flash. For anyone on a paid plan, a scheduled downgrade or tier change now shows up as pending and only takes effect at the next renewal instead of acting immediately. You don't need to change anything; just notice that new sessions now start on GPT-5.6 Luna rather than DeepSeek V4 Flash by default.

d9e94b083c24c9e1fa9655b0e55f5cdfc6506865.text: GPT-5.6 Luna no longer has a daily usage cap, so you can use it as freely as the other models in your regular daily session allowance. You get the full Freebuff experience with every model sharing the same daily quota, and MiMo remains completely unmetered. If your account qualified for the smaller model set because of your connection or region, you will see the updated notice the next time you open the model picker, which now states that no per-model caps remain. This is live today and needs no action from you. - ❤️ Freebuff Team, August 24, 2026.

8d2fe1d276001824281f633df332852e67e82564.text: Freebuff added five new throwaway email domains that are now blocked from earning referral rewards. The system now treats signups from gmaoiil.com, duojumbo.online, duojumbo.com, itesun.com, and geusil.com as suspicious based on honeypot probing behavior. This is an internal change that affects how the referral system identifies and blocks abuse patterns. You will not see any change in your daily use of Freebuff, whether you are a free tier user or a subscriber.

8bf398cd72689f7ca4bea6eb14ad7a7b162763ee.text: The DeepSeek V4 Flash model is now available to use without limits, meaning it no longer counts against your daily usage allowance when you use the free version of Freebuff. This applies only to the full-access catalog, so users who get the limited model set are not impacted. If you are on the free tier and have been avoiding Flash because it was metered or closed during busy hours, you can now pick it at no extra cost during off-peak times. The CLI itself was also bumped to a newer build with this change.

2b718cc3be65d5704cf71390e398c989c1641b84.text: Freebuff turned off automatic routing of ad slots to its own first-party ad network by default, so a missing configuration value no longer accidentally sends paying advertisers to Freebuff's internal ad system instead of the paid networks advertisers paid for. The change also adds two new operational log events that record when a first-party ad is selected and how that settled to the billing system, but without logging campaign names, advertiser names, or user/session identities. This is a setup and logging change for advertisers buying ad placements, and operators of Freebuff must explicitly set the ad-routing configuration to opt in. You won't see any difference in your coding sessions; this does not affect the assistant's models, tools, or your personal usage limits.

990ae116fee764e1daf72f0fda57880cf3d369b7.text: The daily one-per-session limit on DeepSeek V4 Pro has been removed, so it now draws from the same shared pool as Flash, while GPT-5.6 Luna stays the only model with a strict two-sessions-per-day cap. This is for the Freebuff team's internal model-availability and cap tables, not something end users edit or see directly. A developer using Freebuff today notices nothing: V4 Pro is no longer artificially throttled beyond the normal daily session budget, and Luna is still limited to two sessions per day. The change is live now.

4fa5ea05a929de13ec11d3f1a4549953efa6c09b.text: Freebuff turned on its own in-house ad delivery system. Advertisers can now buy real ad slots that appear inside Freebuff's chat interfaces (the web chat, desktop chat, and CLI transcript), instead of seeing placeholder test ads. The system now records actual impressions and charges advertisers' bills when someone clicks an ad, plus it includes new safety checks that strip hidden or malicious characters from ad text so ads can't mess with your terminal display or redirect you improperly. The ad routing still only reaches real users when enabled by the operator, so most people will notice nothing different right now.

5a504c380ad0497547ff88e63624d6101795cc92.text: DeepSeek V4 Pro, a reasoning-focused AI model, is now available to choose at any hour of the day instead of only during off-peak times. Freebuff users who were previously blocked from picking it during busy hours can now select it whenever they like. No action is needed from users, but you may now see V4 Pro open and selectable when browsing the model list at times when it used to appear grayed out.

ac2a035d604166a86390a7272dd56b60efd8a556.text: The model that starts as the default in Freebuff's picker has changed: DeepSeek V4 Flash is now the first and recommended model across the CLI, desktop, and web, while DeepSeek V4 Pro has moved to the end of the list and is restricted to off-peak hours only. If you pick V4 Pro during peak times, you'll be automatically switched to Flash instead. This affects anyone using the free tier of Freebuff who relies on the default suggestions, and you'll notice that Flash is now the suggested starting point, with Pro available but capped at one session per day and paused during busy hours.

95e94c20aecc773fd13da69de9eebff40f6436bb.text: Freebuff has added a new ad network (Imprezia) as a shared integration inside the common core, including experiment bucketing that assigns roughly 10% of signed-in users to a new ad arm while keeping everyone else in the control group. This is an operator-side change: whoever runs the Freebuff service must wire this new module into the web chat route, CLI/Desktop ad provider, and auction endpoint before any ad ever reaches you. Right now, the integration exists in place but does nothing yet, since no caller is hooked up to it within this change. If you are a signed-in Freebuff user, you would only notice anything after the operator enables and connects it; otherwise your experience is unchanged.

3f3cb3851705ca43846d8a13c2c12a7ebfe94a38.text: Freebuff removed a feature that temporarily lowered free users' spending limits during DeepSeek's peak pricing hours, which used to double the cost of model usage. This change is internal and affects how the Freebuff billing and session systems track usage caps, but it does not change anything a free user sees or does today. The peak-hours reduction logic, the notices shown to users when limits were hit during those times, and the data sent to clients about those temporary reductions have all been taken out.

9311890b70d198454df8e25b72df2d064854dc48.text: When a model you can use for free is temporarily closed (say, because the upstream provider charges extra-high rates at certain hours), the picker now shows a plain-English note like 'Back at 3:00 AM Pacific' in your own clock, instead of just going grey with no explanation. This hits Freebuff free-tier users on free, off-peak-only models when they browse the model picker, so you'll actually know when a greyed-out row comes back rather than thinking the list is just broken. No action needed from you. It is live today.

115a6a5cc676b1a4969d2045ad34ebb5d8bd00ab.text: The post-signup survey now lets you skip any question and still save what you did answer. Leaving a question blank is no longer treated as a mistake, so partial answers get recorded and only a completely empty survey is turned away. This applies to everyone who signs up for Freebuff today, and you will notice it the next time you fill out the survey: you can leave questions unanswered and your chosen answers will still be kept.

1e69baf9bf0ba91e9f693f1a6942e2b92c880783.text: The SDK now translates Git Bash-style paths (like /c/Users) into proper Windows paths (like C:\Users) before trying to find files, so paths agents emit in the Git Bash shell resolve correctly on Windows machines. It affects developers who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK on Windows. You do not need to take any action and will not see anything new, but file-based operations from the terminal will now work with the path style the assistant writes in Git Bash on Windows.

ee79648a9e2aff11d54250c2dd488709b9fb3626.text: The daily limit on the Luna model went up from two to three sessions, so Luna users can run three per-model sessions each day instead of two. This affects Freebuff users who use Luna and is already live, with the notice shown in the model picker updated to match. You will see the new limit reflected in your session counts and the Luna row now shows three instead of two as the per-model ceiling.

a4d50e7363432ab28c574b022a0b2fc76de0ab2a.text: Freebuff's engineering team added two new operational log entries so their internal telemetry system now records when a first-party ad click is counted and when a first-party ad impression is counted. These logs go to Axiom, an internal tool, and they record only generic data like which ad service handled the event, where it showed up, and a rough count of tracking pixels, while deliberately excluding any campaign, advertiser, or creative identities. This affects only Freebuff maintainers, the engineering team that operates the service, since it changes only internal infrastructure and does not change what you see or do. In everyday use, you notice nothing, and there is no action required.

ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.title: Run() aborts user lookup and agent-run registration via AbortSignal
ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.summary: The SDK now forwards an AbortSignal through the user-lookup and agent-run-registration requests that precede the first model call, so an abort ends those requests and their backoff retries instead of waiting out a silent socket. `fetchWithRetry` checks `signal?.aborted` before each attempt and during backoff sleeps, and `runOnce` catches the abort from `getUserInfoFromApiKey` to resolve with Run cancelled by user. The agent runtime treats an abort landing after `startAgentRun` as a cancel rather than a failure. These changes are surfaced in the SDK changelog under [Unreleased].
ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.evidence: common/src/types/contracts/database.ts adds optional `signal?: AbortSignal` to `GetUserInfoFromApiKeyInput` and `StartAgentRunFn`; sdk/src/impl/database.ts threads `options.signal` through `fetchWithRetry`, `getUserInfoFromApiKey`, and `startAgentRun` to abort in-flight retries, and packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts treats an abort after `startAgentRun` as a cancel via if (signal.aborted) return ... 'Run cancelled by user'
ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.unknowns: The changelog mentions dropping `knowledge.md` from the knowledge-file priority list, but the diff for this commit does not show that change.

changes.what: Forwards the AbortSignal from run options through getUserInfoFromApiKey so an abort ends the lookup and its retries promptly.
Treats an abort after agent-run registration as a cancel returning Run cancelled by user rather than a failure.
Documents the abort-aware user lookup and registration in the changelog Unreleased section.

3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.title: Freebucks meter drops legacy monthly dollar allowance reporting
3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.summary: The Freebucks meter no longer surfaces a monthly dollar allowance: the CLI header's freebucksHeaderLine drops its monthly branch, the session types mark the monthly allowance and spend-ceiling blocks as deprecated, and the plan summary sheds its spend line. This aligns with current servers using session pacing instead of a legacy spend cutoff, so the deprecated fields are retained as optional for older clients but no longer rendered. The change spans CLI, Shared/Core, and SDK surfaces across 8 files, with the picker-row meter and the header line leading the user-relevant edits.
3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.evidence: cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts removes the `if (freebucks.monthly)` branch from freebucksHeaderLine; common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts marks FreebuffFreebucksMonthlyAllowance.monthly and FreebuffFreebucksSpendCeiling.spend as @deprecated and optional; common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts drops the spend field and the monthly_spend blocked label from the plan summary; common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts removes monthlySpendLimitUsd from the tier shape and the plan disclaimers that referenced it.
3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.unknowns: The diff does not show which downstream consumers still read the deprecated spend/monthly fields or when the last legacy client that depends on them will be cut over. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: freebucksHeaderLine no longer appends the monthly dollar-allowance segment, leaving the daily, reset-countdown and wallet figures in place.
The session types mark FreebuffFreebucksMonthlyAllowance.monthly and FreebuffFreebucksSpendCeiling.spend as @deprecated and optional, and the subscription tier shape loses monthlySpendLimitUsd.
freebuffPlanSummary drops the spend field and the monthly_spend blocked label, and the tier disclaimers no longer cite a monthly token-compute cap.
The spend-ceiling documentation is re-commented as compatibility notice text, and the legacy per-account spend constants and resolver are stripped.
The turn-spend-limit error code and message are re-commented as a legacy older-server refusal retained by recovery handlers.
The SDK carries the deprecated spend fields through deserialization since the wire types mark them optional rather than removing them outright.

ad5815a052e41a708572f75b0f8e23fb3f334e5c.title: Remove legacy backend package and refactor CLI agent loading
ad5815a052e41a708572f75b0f8e23fb3f334e5c.summary: This commit removes the entire legacy backend package, including its Express server, WebSocket implementation, LLM provider adapters, admin tools, and authentication middleware. A second helper, `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit`, carries the count across the SDK persistence boundary edits in `buildCancelledSessionState` by applying the message-history delta rather than a full recount.

Two other areas changed as part of the same snapshot: the planner-agent routing in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, and the limited-tier model allowlists and geo-exemption lists in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`.
