78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release lets you save your conversation to a file and adds Muse Spark 1.3 as a new AI model you can pick, while making DeepSeek V4 Flash the default model your session opens on. The CLI now shows a Freebucks meter so you can see how many credits a model costs before you start, and a one-time intro card explains how pay-as-you-go credits work on your first metered launch. You can now export your full conversation to a markdown or JSON file using the new /export command, and the model picker on desktop and cloud has been reordered so GLM 5.3 Flash leads the list again after a brief switch to DeepSeek. When you hit your free usage limit, the landing screen now offers an upgrade button instead of a dead end, and it shows day-scale wait times like '26 days' instead of hours when your reset is far away. The sponsored proposal flow has also landed in the terminal: you can now accept an advertiser-funded coding task through an in-terminal consent panel, which runs sandboxed in its own worktree and refuses to connect without your explicit yes.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff now defaults to GLM 5.3 Flash as the recommended free AI model, with Solar Pro 4 also available in the free picker, while DeepSeek V4 Pro, MiniMax M3, and earlier DeepSeek variants are no longer shown as free options. A new /reasoning command lets you control how deeply the model thinks during a task, with your preference saved between sessions. The model selector now shows when a row is closed and when it reopens (for example, 'Back tomorrow'), and it hides misleading quota counts for users whose usage is exempt. Ad slots are now real first-party inventory instead of test placeholders, which means the ads you see come from Freebuff's own ad rail. The spend-ceiling safety system was reworked so accounts routed through privacy tooling such as VPNs face tighter per-day limits and a clear refusal message, while ordinary accounts keep their normal access. Together, these changes give you a clearer, safer default experience and surface accurate availability and quota information at the moment you pick a model.

3e63daca691768e95055f250f95cdf1404b251ad.text: The Freebucks meter in the CLI no longer shows a legacy monthly dollar allowance, aligning with the current server-side session pacing approach instead of an outdated spend cutoff. This affects Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, and SDK users by simplifying the header display. You will no longer see a monthly usage left line in the header; the wallet balance and daily countdown remain. The underlying Freebucks spending and refusal logic is unchanged.

358336a18e557894e7bbdd623c43e34f1bc54f6f.text: This release adds Freebuff Pro sponsor breaks with new hero assets and a headline parser that highlights one accent word on the desktop card, plus a Freebucks daily reset countdown in the CLI header. It swaps the free model picker so Muse Spark 1.2 is back on the list (Muse Spark 1.3 is paused after 404 errors) and leads the limited tier with GLM 5.3 Flash while keeping DeepSeek V4 Flash as the safe fallback. Spend ceilings, refund receipts, and the peak-pricing badge are corrected or added so on-meter accounts and limited-tier users see accurate allowances and refund status. Upgrading keeps your free sessions from locking you out when a free model is promoted, shows you exactly when your Freebucks reset, and stops a key press on the intro card from accidentally starting a session for a model you did not pick.

9a9f7dd95b7843187a4048b1b950b3539ab8fd5c.text: The code that decides exactly how a text ad fits into the width of a terminal window has been moved out of the terminal program and into a shared location, so the same rules now govern both how ads appear in your terminal and how they are previewed by advertisers composing them. This guarantees an advertiser sees precisely what a developer will see, eliminating any mismatch between the preview and the actual rendering. This is internal work for the advertising system that paid promotions run through; the Freebuff assistant itself is not affected, and most developers will notice no change unless they are building ad creatives in the campaign console.

0b60b7df7979a111f67629386bd2a64f36885060.text: When you start a coding task on a repository, Buffy now receives a concise summary of the project's git history and the files that have changed, rather than a large dump of raw git status and diff text. This affects you as a Freebuff or Codebuff user when you run the assistant against a code repository. You will notice the assistant begins tasks with clearer context about the project's size, recent activity, and which files are in flux, which helps it make better decisions without being overwhelmed by verbose git output.

b4e5713b824dff395fcf7112cfc5ccae94429984.text: A new switch was added to the advertiser marketplace settings so you ad campaigns no longer need a manual review by an operator before they go live, while still requiring a human to approve the advertiser's account itself. This is aimed at the internal Freebuff team that builds and runs the advertising marketplace, not at regular users of the coding assistant. It is in place but not wired into anything yet, so it has no visible effect today; campaigns are still approved the same way until the team connects it to the submission flow.

7b1bde13e85e50fb7f0ca7675ebf8c29788ec464.text: The model selection screen now shows separate usage counts when a model has its own daily limit that differs from the main group, instead of mixing it into one shared count. This affects Freebuff users who see the model picker. If you use DeepSeek models, you now see their own "1 of 1 used" label when that specific daily limit is spent, rather than the label being taken over by the main group's count.

b378f994a87f43adea2fa4fed651663f2b89b08e.text: Running ads are now capped at a one-week campaign length, with a new rule that automatically sets the furthest end date from today and clamps any advertiser-requested end date to that limit. This affects advertisers running self-serve campaigns on the Freebuff marketplace, not developers or end users coding with the assistant. You won't notice this in your daily coding sessions: the change is internal to how ad campaigns are bounded and enforced, and campaigns can still run for up to seven days from when they start. The pricing switch remains off, so no cards are charged yet.

08a8371fb064793ba00624c528e8738489aea268.text: The Trust cost per message is now a flat 1 across all model tiers. Previously, sending a message to a premium or frontier model consumed more Trust than one to a standard model; now every model costs exactly the same. Any user who sends messages across multiple model types will notice that their Trust balance drains at a steady, predictable rate. The change is live today.

8c034b5f9242c0bb48b8021f96eeb2e159096d16.text: When you prove you commented on a LinkedIn ad, the system now requires the actual comment link, not just the post's own link. This catches the same mistake that was already blocked on X and Reddit, so a bare post link no longer sneaks through on LinkedIn. Advertisers who submit a LinkedIn comment permalink with a commentUrn in the URL will pass, while a plain activity link will be rejected as the post itself. If you ran an ad campaign recently and submitted a linked post link instead of your comment link, your evidence will now be refused and you should resubmit using the comment permalink.

2e3e3f6691f3de16b7b0b5ddcb1612c553a382de.text: The point-scoring system that tracks how much free premium access you have earned was restructured so that everyday prompts on free models no longer cost any points at all, while prompts on more powerful or limited models now cost one or two points. The system also now stops your point total from ever dropping below zero, instead of letting it fall as low as negative five hundred. This applies to all end-users of Freebuff, including those using the CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. In daily use, most people will notice that their point score no longer sinks into negative territory when they run out, and that routine conversations on free models no longer deduct any points at all.

ba0e40bacf53a1ffa8dfcf0db6ab7b0da43b139a.text: The Freebuff team updated the fake web browser that the app pretends to be when it asks ad companies for ads, and fixed a mismatch where the browser identity shown to advertisers did not match the one used when the ad was actually served. Freebuff keeps Freebuff users on the free plan (supported by ads) on track to see the right ads without being mistaken for a bot; the change is already live today, and you should not notice anything different except that ads continue to appear reliably in the chat.

5f72959fab4202f5b667112c914282bcc195fb9b.text: The team moved the skill-parsing code into a shared utility location so that hosted environments and internal services can read skill files without dragging in the full SDK's heavy dependencies. This fixes situations where a server-side or cloud-hosted runner would fail when trying to load a custom skill, because it no longer has to load a specific parser library that was breaking in those environments. The change also makes it possible for a cloud-hosted server to load only the skills that belong to the specific user or project it is working on, preventing it from accidentally reading the wrong machine's personal skill files.

8da51dc0eaecae13822690e91ea90a9038bd9dc6.text: Freebuff has changed which AI model you get when you use the free, limited version of the service outside the main supported countries or while using a VPN. Previously, users in limited mode could pick from either DeepSeek V4 Flash or MiMo 2.5, but now MiMo 2.5 is the only model available in that restricted mode. This change happened because the price of the DeepSeek model spiked, so Freebuff paused it for limited users to keep the free service affordable for everyone. If you are in limited mode, your model picker will now show MiMo 2.5 as the only choice, and you will see a notice explaining why DeepSeek Flash is no longer listed there.

d20038cb58001e360bbcfb30960817b202e8993a.text: Maintainers added a new reference list inside Freebuff's shared billing constants that separates a model's creator from the company that actually invoices Freebuff for running it, so future spend reports can stop crediting companies Freebuff has no contract with and instead show the real biller, with helper functions to safely translate stored values back into readable names and to label unknown entries as unattributed. The change is internal to Freebuff's core constants, has no user-facing consumer reading it yet, includes its own tests asserting correct labeling and safe handling of unknown or missing values, and therefore does nothing visible today for users, advertisers, or operators of the service.

7dcb4fb1e09cbd72bb0d86409739ff616bc6d472.text: Freebuff's engineers added two new safety limits in the shared model catalog. One caps how many new web projects a single account can start each day across all regions at five, replacing an older regional-only limit. The other caps how many of a user's sandboxed coding sessions can run at the same time at two. Neither limit is wired into the running app yet, so they sit in place but do nothing until the rest of the service begins reading them. This is internal configuration work for the Freebuff team; you will not notice anything change today.

695a52ed5a16bd3c3482682e2f84b29ac47c5190.text: The team updated the internal notes in the spend-tracking file so that Freebuff's support staff and engineers can read exactly how the two-layer daily free limit works: the main cap that stops new sessions from starting, and the separate 2x safety cut that can still end a live session for accounts the system has already flagged as high-risk. No daily dollar amounts and no cut-off rules changed, so your free allowance is exactly the same today as it was before, and you don't need to change anything to keep using Freebuff.

0ce5fb0b7d299ff3a646c2785016dd3287928df3.text: The Freebuff project added automated checks that run on every contribution: a build-and-test job that confirms the software compiles and starts correctly, and a quick pull-request reviewer that checks the title, description, and whether the change touches code the public repository accepts. This affects only people contributing code changes through pull requests, not the assistant itself. Contributors now get immediate feedback on whether their change builds and whether it follows submission rules, and rejected changes include a clear explanation of what to fix.

ad5815a052e41a708572f75b0f8e23fb3f334e5c.text: The engineering team removed the old standalone server that used to run the assistant's brain, and rewired the command-line tool so it loads its helper agents directly through the new developer toolkit instead. This is internal housekeeping for the Codebuff maintainers who build and test the tool, so you won't notice anything different when you run it today. Your sessions, agent choices, and the way the terminal interface behaves stay exactly the same.

f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.title: Add FutureSearch deep research to the web-search tool
f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.summary: Adds the FutureSearch deep research provider to the web-search tool surface via a new deep-research API facade, `callDeepResearchAPI` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts`, which routes to `/api/v1/deep-research` with research set true and forwards `researchEffort`, `researchDirections`, and `researchContext` from the tool call. The shared contract for the research-effort tiers and provider universe now lives in `common/src/constants/web-search.ts` exporting `RESEARCH_EFFORTS`, `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS`, `WebSearchProvider`, `ResearchEffort`, and `WebSearchEnv`, while the FutureSearch polling wrapper in `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/futuresearch-api.ts` defines `POLL_BUDGET_MS` (25s), `COST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s), and `researchQuery`, which the handler calls when deep research is requested. Latency ceilings are paired so the facade's `DEEP_RESEARCH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (6min) exceeds the endpoint's 5min poll budget plus the cost lookup hop.
f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/web-search.ts` defines `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS`, `RESEARCH_EFFORTS`, `WebSearchProvider`, `ResearchEffort`, and `WebSearchEnv`; new file `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/futuresearch-api.ts` implements `researchQuery` with `POLL_BUDGET_MS`, `COST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `callDeepResearchAPI` and FutureSearch env types; edits to `common/src/tools/params/tool/web-search.ts` add research, `researchEffort`, `researchDirections`, and `researchContext` to the `web_search` zod schema; edits to `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts` export `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MAX_RETRIES`, add `DEEP_RESEARCH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, and add `callDeepResearchAPI` hitting `/api/v1/deep-research`; edits to `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/web-search.ts` route research: true calls to `callDeepResearchAPI`; edits to `agents/researcher/researcher-web.ts` update the researcher agent systemPrompt to mention research: true.
f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.unknowns: The rollout and which consumer activates `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER` selection is not visible in the diff.

changes.what: Defines the web-search provider universe and research-effort tiers as shared constants. Adds `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS` (`['serper', 'futuresearch']`), `RESEARCH_EFFORTS` (`['low', 'medium', 'high']`), the `WebSearchProvider` and `ResearchEffort` types, and the `WebSearchEnv` interface for provider.

Adds the FutureSearch API client that runs asynchronous multi-agent deep research, polling task status within `POLL_BUDGET_MS` (25s) and fetching the cost within `COST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s), and exports `researchQuery`.

Adds `callDeepResearchAPI` for the `/api/v1/deep-research` endpoint with no retries (re-submission bills twice) and a `DEEP_RESEARCH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (6min) timeout, and exports `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` and `MAX_RETRIES` so the latency-pairing test can assert the ceilings stay ordered.

Extends the `web_search` tool input with `research`, `researchEffort`, `researchDirections`, and `researchContext`, importing `RESEARCH_EFFORTS` from the new constants file and describing the paid FutureSearch deep-research flow with `researchCostDollars`.

Branches the web-search handler on `research`, dispatching to `callDeepResearchAPI` with `researchEffort`, `researchDirections`, and `researchContext` when deep research is requested and otherwise to `callWebSearchAPI`.

Updates the researcher-web systemPrompt to tell the model to call `web_search` with `research: true` for hard multi-source questions and to break them into `researchDirections` and pass `researchContext`.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.title: Drop FutureSearch deep research from web search
afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.summary: The web_search tool no longer exposes the research, researchEffort, researchDirections, or researchContext fields, and the agent runtime now calls callWebSearchAPI directly instead of routing a research branch to callDeepResearchAPI. This happened because common/src/constants/web-search.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/futuresearch-api.ts were deleted, removing the provider universe, env types, and the deep research facade. The researcher-web system prompt was also rewritten to drop the research: true path, leaving only standard web_search and read_url.
afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.evidence: Removed `common/src/constants/web-search.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/futuresearch-api.ts`, deleting exports WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS, WebSearchProvider, RESEARCH_EFFORTS, ResearchEffort, WebSearchEnv, FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, MAX_RETRIES, DEEP_RESEARCH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, callDeepResearchAPI, FutureSearchEnv, POLL_BUDGET_MS, COST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS. The web_search inputSchema in `common/src/tools/params/tool/web-search.ts` no longer accepts research, researchEffort, researchDirections, or researchContext, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/web-search.ts` only calls callWebSearchAPI instead of branching on research.

161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.title: Sponsored proposal channel logic added to common
161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.summary: A new `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts` module adds the channel logic that turns a sponsored proposal row into a rendering-agnostic view model, defining `SponsoredProposalState`, `SPONSORED_STATE_TITLE`, `sponsoredProposalViewModel`, and the gated helpers `sponsoredPullRequestHref`, `sponsoredLogoToken`, and `sponsoredLogoSrc`. f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.text: The web search tool now has an optional deep-research mode that runs a team of AI agents to research a question and return a written answer with sources, instead of just listing search results. When you ask a research question, the assistant can choose to run this deeper search, which takes longer (tens of seconds to minutes) and costs more to run, but returns a synthesized answer with citations rather than raw links. The assistant shows the cost of deep research in its reply so you know what it spent. This feature is now available to developers using the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app, but the assistant controls when to use it rather than running automatically.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model you get when you start a new chat or write a new app, and adds a new /dashboard command that opens your account page so you can check streaks, tokens, and settings across the web, desktop, and command-line versions. The release also adds the /reasoning command so you can set how deeply Freebuff thinks about your request, and it withdraws DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiniMax M3 from the free model picker, leaving GLM 5.3 Flash, Solar Pro 4, and the remaining unlimited rows as the available free choices. For daily use, upgrading means your next session starts on GLM 5.3 Flash by default, a new /dashboard slash command gives you one-click access to your account hub, and the model picker now leads with the new default so you always reach the recommended free model first. Note: some items in the changelog mention models and caps that the final catalog at the end of the release says are not in the picker, so treat those as superseded by the final state.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new Export command so you can save your entire conversation to a file, and it makes Freebucks the main way the CLI talks about usage, showing your credit balance and prices right in the model picker. Solar Pro 4 is now available to limited users and no longer capped, while GLM 5.3 Flash is back in the default picker lead and Muse Spark 1.3 is added to every surface. Sponsored proposal ads now run in their own worktree in your terminal with a one-sentence consent prompt before they start, and the CLI landing screen shows upgrade prompts when you hit session limits instead of a dead end. You also get better month-scale wait-time display on rate limits, a once-only Freebucks intro card, and clearer model switching so the planner falls back to MiMo for limited builds. Upgrading gives you the Export shortcut plus visible credit balances, the Muse Spark and Solar Pro 4 model updates, the consent-gated local ad runs, and a smoother path from a walled free session to a paid plan when you run out of sessions.

1470aa4e189c2d0347843109e5ec86dbab395402.text: Freebuff's internal database monitoring system used to go completely dark whenever it lacked a specific database permission, reporting false all-clears instead of real problems. Now it runs anyway, clearly reporting exactly which database sessions and statements it could and could not see, and surfaces hidden activity as anonymous buckets so it can still detect a runaway query without naming it. This affects only the Freebuff engineering team, who now get accurate alerts instead of silent blind spots. You, as a user, will not notice this change in your daily use.

6c1591f8a5caf4b189e75bea718139d506c0b121.text: Freebuff quietly switched the model new sessions start on from GPT-5.6 Luna back to DeepSeek V4 Flash, and it also made MiniMax M3 count as an unlimited model instead of one of the rate-limited slots. Anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK sees these two models behave differently the next time they start a new coding session, with no restart or command needed on your part. Freebuff V4 Flash is now the recommended default that every surface points to, and MiniMax M3 no longer uses up a shared daily allowance, so it stays available regardless of how many sessions you have left. This is live today.

ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.text: When you start an AI coding run through the SDK, the assistant has to make two quick checks before it begins: confirming your account details and registering the run with the service. Previously, if you cancelled the run while those checks were waiting on a slow or unresponsive server, nothing would stop the requests in flight. The retry logic would keep waiting, the connection would hang, and you would be stuck there until the full timeout played out, unable to escape. Now, those checks listen for your cancellation command, so aborting will cut the request short and return right away instead of forcing you to wait. This means cancelling a run, especially when a server is sluggish, now actually works the moment you ask it to instead of leaving you stranded in limbo.

35eec19e84f06cc0bfef213d204165ac1e9867a4.text: When the AI model provider charges higher rates during busy hours, your free daily usage limit is automatically lowered during those same hours, so the same amount of money buys fewer tasks. A new message now tells you the limit is temporary, shows the reduced amount you still have, and says exactly when your full limit returns instead of making you wait until the next day. This only affects free-tier usage during the defined peak windows and does not change anything about your account, your paid work, or any ad placement.

2fa82f2e26c68a2e750dcdd3515855e661d05577.text: The team replaced several copies of the same day-counting logic with a single shared helper used by their billing and reporting scripts and dashboards. It only affects Freebuff's internal engineering team; the helper is now in place and wired into the rollup jobs and dashboards, but the remaining consumers still need to be migrated to import from it. You will not notice anything different in your terminal or account today, since this is plumbing that keeps the numbers consistent behind the scenes rather than a change to how you use the assistant.

161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.text: The assistant gained a shared rulebook that decides exactly which buttons, messages, and links a sponsored task card can show at each stage of its life, such as when a task is running, finished, or when a pull request exists. This rulebook lives in the central code so both the web app and any future terminal version stay in sync, and it keeps dangerous raw addresses from being turned into clickable links by quietly refusing anything that isn't a safe web address or recognized logo. It also makes each stage report its own result rather than suggesting the next action, so the wording is consistent everywhere. This is internal infrastructure: nothing new is visible to users yet, because no part of the app reads these new rules today.

c200e2d4f1c2dbc77bdd889971d83fb755fb0f53.text: The Freebuff team added a shared set of database health checks that watch for four specific problems the database had run into before: transaction IDs getting too close to a dangerous limit, a long-running query holding back cleanup, a broken or stuck index build, and one slow query hogging too many database connections at once. Each check only triggers an alert once a problem passes a conservative safety threshold, so routine database activity does not set off false alarms. This is internal tooling used only by the engineers who keep Freebuff's infrastructure running. You do not need to do anything, and you will not see any difference in how the assistant behaves.

6c49e12dc09c72d510ee13940ea543ef19b418e5.text: The Freebuff Desktop auto-run feature, which silently picks what a tab does next during idle moments on Auto mode, has been formally recognized as an official free-mode root agent in the system, ending a previous gap where it was incorrectly routed through metered billing and would either fail or show an out-of-credits error to free users. This change applies to Freebuff Desktop users on the free tier (most of them). When you leave Auto mode idle, the assistant now reliably produces a next step instead of silently doing nothing or erroring out.

2afc2b2dfac9a0bcb48e18ccc0c1f720f6f2e6a7.text: The assistant used to be forced to talk to one specific company for a certain AI model, and now it can pick from that company first but still fall back to others safely. Because that company blocked Freebuff's account on August 16, 2026, the system now makes sure you are never charged too much by refusing to use the model if any provider tries to charge more than the set price cap. You do not need to do anything different, and your coding sessions should now better tell you when a model provider refuses to answer rather than stopping quietly like it did before.

f97ca5511b01eba2552e9be7d7332194f5118ca3.text: Freebuff's abuse-detection system used to treat popular privacy-focused email addresses such as ProtonMail, Tutanota, Apple Hide My Email, DuckDuckGo Email Protection, and Firefox Relay as suspicious signals that could trigger a spending limit, even though they are mainstream primary inboxes. As of August 14, 2026, the system reclassified those big-brand privacy mailboxes into a new category so they are still visible to fraud and trust-scoring tools, but no longer cause the spending ceiling to be applied to them. This change only affects how the Freebuff service detects and scores referral abuse internally. You will not notice this in your day-to-day use of Freebuff.

ae35b542f1b2cc0e6e455ef9effa1cdb9ad4c818.text: Freebuff, the free coding assistant, stopped treating Singapore as a high-risk country that gets a tiny daily budget, and now gives Singapore users the normal daily allowance that most users in supported regions receive. This applies only to free-tier accounts whose requests are identified as coming from Singapore, and nothing else about their account changed. If you are a free user in Singapore, you may now be able to start more coding sessions in a day before hitting the daily limit, instead of running out after just one small session.

7c219be7ef6d60e088fcfa9fcd566a798153d57b.text: When you use Freebuff for free and the system has already spent its daily budget on your account, you used to get a generic message saying capacity was limited. You now get a clearer message that explains in plain terms whether the limit was hit because of VPN or proxy use, a restricted location, or an email provider often linked with automated traffic. It only affects free users on the restricted caps, not paid sessions, and it is live today, so no action is needed on your part.

5db7a544be7c5ec414b833a4cb295fa8511b1b8c.text: Free mode now applies a stricter daily spending cap that can cut off an active session, but only for accounts already being closely watched because of their country, internet connection, or email domain. It affects the engineering team that runs and maintains Freebuff, since the change only adds internal limits and session-tracking fields. You will not notice anything new in your daily use, because the code that actually enforces this cap is not turned on yet; the limits are defined but not yet wired into the sessions.

79d6a9de6e44b00e4d484725b74991122ae257ab.text: Freebuff has switched the default and Lite modes in the CLI to run a newer base3 harness for every model in the free picker. This applies to developers using the Freebuff CLI on the free tier, and the change is live today. You may notice faster, single-loop runs instead of the previous multi-step base2 process when working within your free daily allowance, with no action required from you.

871d75810e6732f65067d4bd6faec927c529332d.text: Freebuff used to give every free user the same daily budget, but now it sets different limits based on the region a user is in, with users in certain regions (SG and CN) getting a smaller allowance. Users whose email comes from disposable domains, who use third-party clients, or whose trust level is low also get a smaller allowance. The new limits are lower than the old flat limit, so some users may see their daily usage run out faster than before, but existing sessions are never cut off, only new ones are blocked once the limit is hit.

a0a9a4c80ae8b8aba38b449aa29ad9e214633c43.text: Freebuff has added wiring for three new extended-context model variants - deepseek-v4-pro-max, deepseek-v4-flash-max, and gpt-5.6-luna-max - into its internal root-agent and model-id tables. These entries register the new roots so the orchestrator recognises them as top-level free-mode agents (instead of treating them as subagents that fail the hierarchy check), and map each root to exactly one matching model id. The change is internal configuration only: nothing in this commit reads these constants yet, so there is no new command, picker row, or quota visible today. It affects only Freebuff maintainers preparing per-account provisioned-tier support; end users and the public model picker are deliberately untouched, per the inline comments.

0029f0a29f01837307120b1212694ffaa2899474.text: Freebuff now applies a stricter daily limit of fifty cents (previously one dollar) to any account that appears to be masking its real location or using an anonymizing network like a VPN or Tor. This lower ceiling joins the same cap already applied to traffic from certain regions and disposable email domains, and because the rulebook picks the lowest applicable limit, a masked account can only ever get a cheaper allowance, never a higher one. Live coding sessions are never cut off mid-use; the limit only decides whether a new session can be started that day, so an account that hit the half-dollar cap just cannot open another session until the daily reset. The new rule is live now for free-tier users who connect through anonymizing services or VPNs.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.text: The assistant can no longer run deep, agent-powered web research: the web search tool dropped its research mode, and now always returns a standard keyword search powered by Serper. If you previously asked the assistant to research a hard, multi-source question, it will now give you quick search results instead of a synthesized, cited deep answer. This is live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web, desktop, or SDK, and there's nothing to change on your end except stop sending the now-unsupported research options.

a29a854c99017a698e7c8c673e870465919ec957.text: A new 'agents' command lets Freebuff users browse, create, and switch between custom AI assistants directly from the terminal, guided by an interactive menu that walks you through naming your agent, choosing its role, and assigning its skills. You can also edit existing custom agents or hand off a task to a specialist helper agent you or another Freebuff user has built. This is live today for Freebuff CLI users who work in the terminal; no configuration or update is needed beyond using the new menu.

01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.title: Free tier shows three usage windows in picker
01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.summary: The Freebuff model picker now renders a free-tier usage line (`FREE · today/week/month`) when a non-subscriber's session response carries a `freeWindows` block, reusing the shared `freebuffPlanSummary` layout so free users see the same three-ring shape subscribers already do. The `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` interface and `getFreeWindowsInfo` accessor were added to `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, wired onto the pre-join, active, and ended response variants, alongside `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` in `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts`, which maps `dayUsed/dayLimit`, `weekUsed/weekLimit`, and `monthUsed/monthLimit` onto the plan's `FreebuffPlanWindow` shape. A new `getZonedMonthBounds` helper in `common/src/util/zoned-time.ts` computes the calendar-month boundaries that drive the free tier's monthly window reset. The block is absent for quota-exempt accounts, limited-access users, and older servers, in which case callers fall back to the daily ring alone, and the week/month counts are display-only today with no enforcement.

In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, the new `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` interface and `getFreeWindowsInfo` accessor are defined, and `freeWindows?: FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` is added to the pre-join, active, and ended response variants. In `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts`, `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` is added, mapping `info.dayUsed/dayLimit`, `weekUsed/weekLimit`, and `monthUsed/monthLimit` to the shared `FreebuffPlanWindow` shape with `dayResetAt`. In `common/src/util/zoned-time.ts`, `getZonedMonthBounds` is added to compute calendar-month boundaries in a time zone for the free tier's monthly window.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.title: Subscription tracking, legacy rewrites, write-in classification
bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.summary: The post-signup onboarding questionnaire adds a subscriptions question that records competitive products (Claude Code, Cursor, opencode, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Gemini, Lovable / Replit), with the `none` row flagged exclusive so validation rejects it alongside other picks. New exports `ONBOARDING_LEGACY_OPTION_IDS`, `ONBOARDING_OTHER_TEXT_RULES`, and `classifyOnboardingOtherText` reclassify retired option ids and raw write-in text at read time during the admin tally, keeping stored answers intact while folding Discord/blog/newsletter write-ins into `other` and Instagram/AI-assistant text into their real options. Validation now enforces the exclusive flag and the `kind` field (introducing `scale` rendering for the proficiency question) without rewriting stored data.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.title: Add Human Behavior session replay env vars to client schema
4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.summary: Two optional environment variables were added to the shared client env schema: `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_API_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_INGESTION_URL`. The API key authorizes ingestion for Freebuff Web session replay and the ingestion URL overrides the SDK default host to point a deployment at a non-default Human Behavior endpoint. Both default to undefined, so a dev checkout without them boots with replay switched off.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 becomes Freebuff Web default and Muse Spark
e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 now replaces GPT-5.6 Luna as the default model for Freebuff Web, Cloud, and Chat sessions, set via `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. The same `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` is wired into `MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID`, so rate-limited Muse Spark turns now reroute to Pro instead of Luna, and `MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE` and the picker copy in both READMEs were updated to name Pro. GPT-5.6 Luna stays fully selectable in the picker but gains a `supersededBy` notice steering users to Pro, and it is deliberately excluded from `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` because the per-token price comparison between Luna and Pro does not cleanly favor either side. The shared daily premium pool is counted in sessions, so quota limits for end-users do not move as a result of the reroute target changing.

In `README.md` and `README.zh-CN.md`, the 'Best for' cells for DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 and GPT-5.6 Luna are swapped so Pro is described as the default for Web, Cloud, and Chat. In `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS`'s doc comment, Luna is explicitly called superseded but NOT muted.

The Pro default (`DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID`) was left unchanged, but its docblock now records that the repricing flipped Pro from cheaper-than-Luna to dearer-than-Luna on cache reads, and notes the cost argument behind Pro being the browser default no longer holds and should be revisited. `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` was left empty and the docblock explicitly states muting is a product-steering decision the repricing alone should not silently overturn.

The comment above `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` (around line 1279) was likewise updated to state that the repricing inverted the cache-read cost comparison versus GPT-5.6 Luna and to leave the default on Pro while flagging the cost half of the argument as no longer holding.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.title: Add Cloudflare Worker egress detector for resold free capacity
90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.summary: A new module in `common/src/constants/cf-worker-signals.ts` defines a pure `detectCfWorker` function that keys on the `cf-worker` header stamped by the Cloudflare edge, requiring the companion `cf-ray` header to corroborate that the request traversed Freebuff's own edge before flagging a zone. The verdict type, `CfWorkerEvidence` record shape, `parseAllowedWorkerZones` allowlist parser, and `looksLikeProxyClientId` helper are defined and exported, along with the `CfWorkerMode` action ladder of `off`, `observe`, `block`, and `ban`, but no reader imports or enforces them in this commit. The detector exists to catch third-party Workers like `pingmike2/freebuff2api-wokers` that pool harvested tokens and resell free-mode capacity, while the zone allowlist is meant to spare Freebuff's own Workers such as `app-preview-proxy`.

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.title: Onboarding requirement gate for Freebuff accounts
fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.summary: Freebuff now enforces a blocking onboarding requirement for new accounts, surfaced to non-web clients as the `onboarding_required` error after a 403 response, with `getFreebuffOnboardingRequiredMessage` falling back to `ONBOARDING_REQUIRED_MESSAGE` when the server omits one. The gate is scoped by a cutover instant parsed from `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED_AFTER` via `parseOnboardingCutover`, so only accounts created at or after that moment are ever required, and the roughly 203,000 pre-existing accounts remain permanently exempt. The four-question questionnaire is defined in `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_QUESTIONS` with append-only option ids and validation that rejects unknown ids, while `common/src/env-schema.ts` adds `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` to the client schema. The later commit [b07e38d9] removes this gate and simplifies validation.

44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.title: Freebuff surfaces shared provider usage error copy
44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.summary: A new common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts module exports a shared provider usage error pattern and a user-facing message that makes clear the provider, not the user, is responsible for billing failures. The CLI's cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts adds isFreebuffProviderUsageError, which matches a 402 status code or the wording of CrofAI, OpenRouter, and similar provider errors. cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts now checks that error in both handleRunCompletion and handleRunError and shows FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_USAGE_MESSAGE, so free users no longer see credit-purchase wording for provider-side billing issues.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.title: Clickable title box makes composer and queue titles clickable

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.title: SDK reports incomplete usage receipts and reasoning tokens
a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.summary: The SDK now exposes an `onUsageIncomplete` callback on `RunOptions`, called whenever a model request ends before an exact provider usage receipt arrives. `promptAiSdkStream` invokes `onUsageIncomplete` on stream abort, thrown response-body recovery, or when the finish part lacks usage data, instead of silently dropping the event; the agent runtime forwards it through `runAgentStep` as `onAgentUsageIncomplete`, and the agent-stream adapter passes it from `getAgentStreamFromTemplate`. `CacheDebugUsageData` also gains an optional `reasoningOutputTokens` field, populated from `outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens` in `emitCacheDebugUsage`. The change spans Shared/Core, Agent Runtime, and SDK across five files.

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.migration: No action required; existing SDK consumers that do not set `onUsageIncomplete` continue to work unchanged.
a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads `onUsageIncomplete` to act on incomplete receipts (e.g. a billing or billing-proration host).

d0c7b069051a45044d107598a2ce98ef80d63100.text: A developer updated the internal notes that describe how much the assistant's main model costs, after DeepSeek changed its pricing on August 16, 2026, splitting it into cheaper off-peak hours and pricier peak hours. This is an internal documentation change only, aimed at Freebuff's engineering maintainers, so nothing about the assistant or your experience changes today. Your sessions, model defaults, and available choices are exactly as they were before, since no live pricing or behavior was altered in this change.

01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.text: The Freebuff model picker now shows free-tier users a three-part usage line labeled FREE that tracks their daily, weekly, and monthly usage in the same layout subscribers already see. It applies to users on full-access free accounts, and does not appear for quota-exempt accounts, limited-access users, or older servers. If you are on the free tier, you will now see your three usage windows displayed together; if this data is missing from your session response, the picker falls back to showing the daily ring alone.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: Freebuff 1.0.687 ships a new model picker and billing meter for free users, adds a /export slash command to save conversations, and tightens sponsorship sandboxing with worktree isolation and consent prompts. The free model picker now shows Muse Spark 1.3 across CLI, desktop, web and cloud while GLM 5.3 Flash returns as the default model, and Solar Pro 4 gains limited-access availability with a per-day spend cap. You can export any conversation to a markdown file or raw JSON with the new /export command. The CLI now routes free-tier sessions through a Freebucks credit meter that displays per-model prices and remaining balance instead of a legacy session counter. Sponsored proposal runs now execute in an isolated worktree with a one-sentence consent screen and per-model campaign allowlists gating compute. Upgrading to this version lets free users track credit-style pricing, pick from Muse Spark 1.3 on every surface, and keep conversations portable via /export, while sponsorship runs stay sandboxed.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This Freebuff release brings a new default AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, to the free model picker across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, replacing the previous default. It adds a new /reasoning slash command so Freebuff users can read or set how deeply the selected model thinks per model, with the choice saved in your settings. A new /dashboard slash command opens your account hub showing streaks, activity, tokens, sessions and settings across surfaces, and the desktop product row is no longer labeled Beta. The ad rail moves to first-party delivery planes that serve real advertiser inventory with sanitized creatives, and CLI copy now falls back to OSC 52 rendering when native clipboard tools are unavailable, aborting stale copy operations so broken display servers cannot freeze the terminal. Upgrading gives you the new GLM 5.3 Flash default model and per-model reasoning control, a one-click account hub, safer copy-and-paste in the terminal, and real first-party ad inventory served in the chat.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.text: Freebuff has switched the AI model that new browser sessions (on the Web, Cloud, and Chat products) start on from GPT-5.6 Luna to DeepSeek V4 Pro, and this is live today for all new threads. The change affects anyone who just starts a new session in the browser-based products, who will now be using Pro unless they pick another model. In daily use, you should notice the strongest model available now powering your first project in the browser, while GPT-5.6 Luna remains a fully usable pick in the model menu, just no longer the first one selected.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.text: A switch was added to Freebuff's web settings that lets the service turn on real-user session replay, powered by a provider called Human Behavior. Only operators running the Freebuff service see or use this, since it is just deployment configuration tucked into the shared settings file. Nothing changes for you today: the new settings default to off, so a dev copy without them still boots normally and no recording happens.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.text: The sign-up questionnaire now asks which AI coding tools you already use, so Freebuff can see who it competes with. If you pick 'None', you cannot also pick other tools at the same time. You can still type a channel or tool that is missing, and the system will quietly count your spelling under the closest existing option without changing what you actually typed. This is live for anyone filling out the questionnaire today.

44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.text: Freebuff now recognizes when the third-party AI provider running a free coding session runs out of money or compute credits and tells you in plain language that the problem is on Freebuff's side, not yours. You are a developer using Freebuff for free coding help. When this kind of billing error happens, you will see the message instead of confusing wording that tries to sell you paid credits, so you know no action is needed on your account.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.text: The title bar at the top of your message queue panel and the composer area where you type can now be clicked to open the queue panel directly, rather than needing a keyboard shortcut. If you already had messages waiting or running, you can click the preview text at the top to expand and review your queued messages. The composer area shows a clickable label when there are items queued, and clicking it opens the queue panel for you to edit or reorder your messages.

00e5fa83a7e86d744e826cef0021ee41b4ccce17.text: The assistant now quietly tracks and reports how much computing power each request uses and whenever it shrinks a long conversation to fit within limits. Developers who embed the assistant into their own tools can now receive these usage and conversation-shrinking events as they happen, without the reporting ever slowing down the work. Nothing looks different in the normal chat experience, but hosts using the SDK can now display token usage or respond to conversation trimming, and any error in their custom handlers is logged rather than crashing the run.

b9810f1556b1ad235441f5bea1278b948d119973.text: A new, well-explained set of plain-language messages was added so that when someone's attempt to create an account is turned away, they are told exactly why and how to fix it, rather than just seeing a generic failure. It affects developers and other people signing up for the Freebuff coding assistant through the login pages. When you try to sign up and are blocked, you will see a clear, non-blaming reason (such as an account already existing for that email, or a VPN being detected) and a next step to retry or contact support, instead of an unhelpful error.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.text: Freebuff has added a new internal check that detects when someone is using a Cloudflare Worker to secretly pool free accounts and resell access to Freebuff's free-tier capacity. This check looks at headers that Cloudflare itself stamps on worker-generated requests, which third parties can't fake or remove. The system is designed so Freebuff's own workers are never flagged, and it only applies to the free tier, not paid accounts. This detection is now in the code and ready, but it does nothing yet since no part of the system is actually using it to block anything today.

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.text: The assistant now tells you when it didn't get a final, exact usage report from the AI model after a response finished. When a response ends abruptly - like a dropped connection, the assistant stops mid-thought, or you cancel - the software lets whatever host is running it know that the usage numbers it can share afterward are incomplete rather than silently guessing. It also now separately tracks 'reasoning tokens' (the behind-the-scenes thinking effort) so those are reported alongside regular input and output counts. If you build on top of the Freebuff tools, your code can opt into a new callback that fires for each incomplete receipt, while existing integrations that don't use it keep working unchanged.

85fe163fd7843afe7dc3d07df57d2ac8eade07c4.text: The internal list of experimental models that only Freebuff staff can test with has been cleaned up: two old test models (Ling 3.0 Flash and Greg 2 Ultra/Super) were fully removed from the system, and a new test-only model called Kimi K3 Eco (from CrofAI) was added in their place, metered like the other internal-only models. This affects internal staff who test new AI models before any public release; it is not a change to the models free or paid users can pick. You will notice nothing different in your daily use of Freebuff, Codebuff, the web app, or the desktop app, because this change only touches a catalog used exclusively for behind-the-scenes testing by the engineering team.

f7d35db5a5e064e98c9f12739e68f1583ced9c5d.title: Admission counting and per-model pool labels land in session quota

The same admission-counted semantics flow through `FREEBUFF_TIER_CHANGE_NOTICE` and the CLI release FAQ, which now describe GLM 5.3 Flash's limit as 2 starts a day. A new test 'an admission-counted chip says starts' pins the rendering path. Together these let the shared CLI/Desktop/Web pickers report per-model caps without each client hardcoding a row's unit type.

e5d41741aeca4ae11989042f2af1647b94c11e41.title: GLM 5.3 Flash gains a reasoning effort ladder of low, high, max
e5d41741aeca4ae11989042f2af1647b94c11e41.summary: GLM 5.3 Flash, already an unmetered Freebuff free model, now declares a native reasoning-effort ladder: 'low', 'high', 'max', with 'max' as both the wire default (reasoningEffort) and the picker starting rung (defaultEffort). The row previously omitted any effort setting because of a mistaken reading that OpenRouter exposed no reasoning parameters; re-checking found z-ai/glm-5.3-flash supports reasoning_effort and the Merge Gateway declares effort_values ["low","high","max"], which measure monotonically (low 107 < high 175 < max 590 < unset 708 thinking chars on 2026-08-27). The FreebuffModelOption interface's reasoningEffort union was extended from 'minimal'|'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh' to add 'max', and MiMo, MiniMax M3, and Solar Pro 4 were confirmed bare.
