68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.title: Foreign client signal now derives signature tool set from tool names
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.summary: The Freebuff signature-tool discriminator is rebuilt in `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts`: `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` is now derived from the shared `toolNames` list, minus the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion set, plus `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES` (set to `['decide']`). The `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type are removed from `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, so `foreign_toolset` is always enforced and `sampling_params` is always reported but never acted upon. This moves the signature from a brittle hand-maintained list to one that updates automatically whenever a new tool is added to `toolNames` or forgotten in `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES`, with the `decide` tool covering Freebuff Desktop's autorun agent.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.evidence: Modified `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts` (commit 68d9a88c): the hand-maintained `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` literal array is replaced with a derived set built from the imported `toolNames` in `common/src/tools/constants`, filtered to remove the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion list and combined with the new `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES = ['decide']`; the `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type on `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` are removed, so the function now always enforces `foreign_toolset` and always reports `sampling_params` without acting on it.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.migration: Requests to the Freebuff free endpoint that do not carry a distinctive Freebuff tool name will now always be served `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` instead of the originally requested model.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` updating to the new parameterless signature, or how the `mode` removal is reconciled downstream.

6ace1d00c9409518218bbf90225391e9002a5b21.text: A new timing rule has been added to the ad delivery system that spaces out how often promoted posts appear to a user during an hour, turning big bursts into a steadier drip. This is internal machinery for the advertising side of the service, not something that touches your coding assistant sessions or Freebucks credits. You won't notice it directly, and there's no action needed from you.

e5d41741aeca4ae11989042f2af1647b94c11e41.text: The assistant's built-in way of thinking before it replies can now be tuned for one model (an AI called GLM 5.3 Flash that's free to use): you can ask it to think less for faster, simpler answers, or more for deeper, more careful ones. This affects anyone using the free version of the assistant. If you choose that model, a new set of depth options appears automatically, with the deeper setting matching how the model already worked, so most people won't notice day-to-day unless they explicitly pick a different level.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model across the Freebuff CLI, web, and desktop, replacing GPT-5.6 Luna, and adds Solar Pro 4 as a new option in the free model picker. A new /dashboard slash command lets you open your Freebuff account page to view streaks, activity, tokens, sessions, and settings in one place. The /reasoning slash command lets you control how hard the selected model thinks on a low-to-max scale, persisted per model in your settings. DeepSeek V4 Flash is now available all day instead of pausing during peak hours, and Luna sessions can run up to 3 per day instead of 2. Time-gated model refusals now show a named timezone label and the exact local return time rather than a bare wall-clock string. The ad rail now fills Freebuff slots with first-party inventory when no paid campaign is active, and GLM 5.3 Flash gains a reasoning-effort ladder you can dial in from the picker.

105640d21d124ff1dd6a7ccd7df06fffb9a5c34f.text: When you ask the assistant to help you sign up for a third-party service like a database or email provider, it can now create the account for you directly and hand back the login credentials, as long as you explicitly approve it first. Previously the assistant could only recommend a service and give you a signup link to visit yourself. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app who asks the assistant to integrate a supported service. You will notice that after a recommended service, the assistant can offer to set up the account in place and write the credentials straight into your project's environment file instead of making you copy them from another page; if the service does not support this, the assistant will still fall back to the signup link as before.

a5b6b0cf4ef9fbf7f6cf529e803601f243cd1b0f.text: Freebuff has raised the daily project-creation limits for outer-region Freebuff Web users and blank Cloud projects to 10, up from 3 and 5 respectively. The new limits apply to users who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app or SDK, particularly those on limited-tier plans. In daily use, you can now create up to 10 projects per day on both Web and Cloud platforms without hitting a cap, with failed builds not counting against the quota.

d9ee7bfc3e52b9156522bc86250fc7376f9fe955.text: The assistant now uses DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 as the recommended starting model across the CLI, desktop, web, and SDK surfaces (taking effect today, 2026-08-12), replacing the previous default of DeepSeek V4 Flash. This affects Freebuff users, who will see Pro selected automatically in the model picker unless they had already chosen another model. In everyday use, the picker now highlights Pro as the recommended hero, and when your daily premium sessions are spent it automatically switches the recommendation to the unlimited DeepSeek V4 Flash so the highlighted option is always one you can actually start. The documentation across the English, Chinese, and release README files was also updated to match.

b07e38d987cc4aa41a1c0fea1a2502a462f0f50f.text: The new-account setup step is no longer a hard stop inside the command-line tool. Instead, it now appears only as a single, skippable form once when you sign in through the website, and only if the team has turned the step on (an unset switch means nobody sees it). If you use the app in your terminal, nothing changes for you and you will not see any new prompt; the step is being tried out on the website only.

190ac96c3428bfbd1ea3ffbdeaf77659f088a902.text: The Freebuff CLI now stops an old clipboard copy whenever you select new text, so a slow or stuck copy can no longer overwrite the newer one with stale content, and over remote sessions any transcript too large for the standard remote-copy method is automatically trimmed before sending. A 5-second safety net also kills any clipboard helper that hangs, so a broken display server can no longer freeze the editor. If you use /copy over SSH with a very long conversation, the largest tool outputs are removed first with a clear note until it fits, and the smallest summary you'd still want is kept. You don't need to change anything. The fix is live now.

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.text: Freebuff has added a new step that some new accounts must complete before they can use the service. If you try to use the assistant and haven't finished this setup, it will tell you to complete it first rather than retrying automatically. Only Freebuff user accounts created after the activation date are asked to do this, so if your account already existed before then, you will not be affected. About 203,000 pre-existing accounts remain permanently exempt. In daily use, eligible new accounts will see a brief multi-question form pop up the first time they try to run an assistant task. Once each question has been answered, the assistant proceeds normally, with no further action required.

702b43bf6fbd41be7405bc3e02773f21a7888d37.text: The Freebuff team decided which of two possible ways the assistant can plan and run tasks should be the default for its free users. One way (base2) coordinates a team of helper agents and double-checks the work, the other (base3) does everything itself in a single pass. In tests over 10 small coding tasks, the single-pass version finished faster but left more of the work undone on Freebuff's weakest (free) model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, so the multi-agent way won and is now locked in as the default for both the normal free experience and the lightweight free mode.

bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.text: The team added a new, more precise way to notice when someone is routing Freebuff's free service through their own tool instead of using an official Freebuff app. This is for Freebuff's operators, the people who run the service itself. You do not see any change in your daily use, and nothing is blocked or limited as a result of this update.

fe7b8fad52fa2ea67a8d2cbb86638e7e0cbb7cf8.text: The launcher now recognizes a specific Windows startup crash pattern (NTSTATUS 0xC0000409) as a likely sign of a CPU missing AVX2 support, applying this check only within the first 10 seconds of launch so that crashes during normal operation are not misclassified. Affected users on x64 Windows who encounter the baseline fallback will see a tailored diagnostic message, and if the baseline build also crashes on startup, they are prompted to include the captured stderr output in their bug report. There is no user action required; the baseline fallback is triggered automatically when the heuristic matches, and the persistent CPU limitation is only recorded for confirmed illegal instruction exits.

da1f340a36ff033086086da3fe1411e796af2bc3.text: The assistant now offers a single, shared 'reasoning effort' ladder (low, medium, high, and so on) that every model picker uses, so the CLI, web, and desktop app all speak the same language when you ask for a quicker or slower response. It affects you if you pick which model the assistant uses - for example, the DeepSeek V4 models and GPT-5.6 Luna now expose a pickable ladder, capped at the effort the model already runs at, so you can spend less thinking time but never more than the model was built to do. Today, when you switch a model in the picker you will see the effort levels line up across surfaces, and if a turn gets rerouted to a different model it drops down to that model's ceiling instead of jumping up to a rung it was never meant to reach.

68b34fa74dd1efa2451b9a4a6df7f5a15ba2a2b3.text: The assistant used to look for instructions in a file named knowledge.md first, but now it prioritizes AGENTS.md instead, falling back to CLAUDE.md. This affects anyone who uses the /init command to set up project documentation or who maintains their own instructions files. If you have an existing knowledge.md file, rename it to AGENTS.md so the assistant continues to read your project instructions automatically.

68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.text: Freebuff now figures out whether an incoming request is genuinely from one of its own tools by starting from the full list of tools the assistant defines, and only excluding the handful of names that competing tools also use, so the protection stays accurate as new tools are added. This detection runs on requests made to the free tier of the service, where developers use the CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK to get code completion and agentic coding for no charge. You will not notice anything different in your daily use: the system now enforces the protection consistently on tool-based traffic and stops serving it for borderline cases, while continuing to report (but not act on) the separate measurement about sampling parameters. The change is live today as part of the shipped code.

9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.text: On August 10, 2026, the team that runs the Freebuff service quietly retuned the alarm that watches database speed, so it stops phoning engineers about everyday traffic spikes. Who it affects: the small on-call group that keeps Freebuff's servers humming (not you, the end user). What you notice: nothing, unless you happen to be on call, in which case your phone finally stops buzzing at 3 a.m. over noise that was not actually a problem.

d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.text: Freebuff's internal monitoring system keeps two separate scorecards when checking database performance: one that tracks whether a metric simply exceeds a target budget (which is always reported but never triggers an alert), and another that tracks whether that same metric got materially worse than usual compared to its normal baseline (which is the only thing that actually triggers a paging alert). Because the budget targets were set aspirationally and every operation was already running above them, mixing the two signals previously meant an alert fired constantly even when performance was stable.

f7d35db5a5e064e98c9f12739e68f1583ced9c5d.text: Each model's usage limit now reports how many separate sessions you started ("starts") versus how much total time you consumed ("used"), so the row for a capped model reads "2 of 2 starts" instead of "2 of 2 used". This only affects free-tier users who see per-model caps in the model picker; if you do not use Freebuff or do not hit a capped model, nothing changes for you. No action is needed: your client fetches the new label automatically on its next session, and the FAQ now describes caps as starts per day rather than sessions per day.

204d98237e29a1004f52c2d7d6beac9cfbb9f694.text: The SDK's chat message converter now correctly handles image data that is already in a usable form, so it no longer wraps an existing web address or self-contained image string inside another data prefix that the receiving provider would reject as malformed base64. This keeps image-bearing messages flowing through OpenAI-compatible provider paths without error when the upstream AI SDK passes tagged file data shaped for version 4 of its protocol. This is an internal SDK fix for maintainers of the Freebuff engineering team; it changes only how provider request payloads are assembled and adds no new behavior you can see or act on. You will notice nothing different in daily use, and no action is required.

21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.title: GLM 5.2 referral reward moved to GLM 5.3 Flash, now tier-shaped
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.summary: The GLM 5.2 daily referral-reward pool is repurposed as a tier-shaped reward: at limited access it unlocks the reward model (now FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID, aliased to FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID), and at full access it adds one extra session to the shared daily premium pool instead of a model. The grid selector no longer filters the reward model out, the referral banner's unlocked card is limited-tier only, and every GLM 5.2 predicate (isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId, isGlmRedeemableAtLimitedTier, getFreebuffStreakGlmWeeklyUnits) is renamed to its reward counterpart. Because the reward model is now an ordinary unmetered full-access row, full access no longer launches it from the banner; GLM 5.2 (FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID) is added to FREEBUFF_PAUSED_FREE_MODEL_IDS so it is only remembered by already-running sessions. README drops the 'GLM 5.2 is available through earned sessions' line, and the streak utilities drop their GLM-specific wording.
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.evidence: Diff hunks in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts rename the GLM 5.2 referral-reward machinery to a tier-shaped reward: FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_IDS becomes FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_IDS, FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID is aliased to FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID (which equals FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID), isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId becomes isFreebuffRewardModelId, getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier no longer filters the reward model out of the grid, and the referral banner now keys its unlocked card on the limited tier only. README.md and README.zh-CN.md swap the 'GLM 5.2 is available through earned sessions' line for a generic referrals/bounties note. freebuff-streak.ts and freebuff-streak-line.ts rename the GLM 5.2 references to reward references.
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.unknowns: The exact server-side wiring that resolves the earned balance into an extra premium session at full access is not shown in the diff; the diff only carries the client-side rename and gating.

changes.what: Renamed the GLM 5.2 referral-reward constants and predicates to reward counterparts and made FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID alias the GLM 5.3 Flash id, then paused GLM 5.2 from free mode.
Stopped filtering the reward model out of the grid and renamed the banner's startable-selection check to isFreebuffRewardModelId.

Keyed the unlocked referral card on the limited tier only and rewrote its copy to offer the reward model instead of naming GLM 5.2, importing FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_DISPLAY_NAME and FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID.
Updated the referral-info docs so the full tier is described as an extra premium session rather than GLM 5.2, and clarified the rate-limit comment to read 'reward referral pool'.
Renamed the GLM 5.2 stint constants and predicate to reward stint counterparts.
Renamed the GLM 5.2 bonus wording to reward bonus wording.

6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.title: CLI ads:enable and ads:disable commands show and rotate Gravity ads
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.summary: Adds the /ads:enable and /ads:disable slash commands, backed by handleAdsEnable, handleAdsDisable, and getAdsEnabled in cli/src/commands/ads.ts, which persist an adsEnabled setting to settings.json. The chat UI now renders an AdBanner when an ad is available and ads are enabled, using useGravityAd to rotate ads every 60 seconds, pre-fetch the next ad 5 seconds ahead, stop after 3 ads without activity, and report activity on input and submit. The usage banner now shows ad-derived credits alongside free and paid balances. The web layer gains Next.js route handlers that serve ads from the Gravity API and grant credits on impression, with server-side storage in a new ad_impression table and a serverEnvSchema entry for GRAVITY_API_KEY.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.evidence: New file cli/src/commands/ads.ts exports handleAdsEnable, handleAdsDisable, getAdsEnabled; command-registry.ts imports and registers ads:enable and ads:disable commands; slash-commands.ts adds 'ads:enable' and 'ads:disable' entries to SLASH_COMMANDS; chat.tsx imports getAdsEnabled and AdBanner, filters slash commands based on adsEnabled, calls useGravityAd and reportActivity on input and submit; cli/package.json adds @gravity/api dependency; web/src/app/api/v1/ads/route.ts and web/src/app/api/v1/ads/impression/route.ts postAds, postAdImpression handlers added.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.migration: No migration is required, but existing users can run /ads:enable to start seeing contextual ads and earning credits from impressions.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.unknowns: The diff does not show the Gravity API response shape details or how the ad revenue share is configured server-side.

changes.what: Added ads:enable and ads:disable slash commands with handlers that toggle the adsEnabled setting, register them in command-registry.ts, list them in slash-commands.ts, and filter the suggested command list based on current ads state.
Introduced useGravityAd hook and AdBanner component to fetch, rotate, and render ads above the input, including activity-based pausing and credit display.
Added Next.js route handlers postAds and postAdImpression to serve Gravity ads and grant user credits on impression via processAndGrantCredit.
Added ad_impression table and migration to log served ads with payout and credit tracking.
Added 'ad' grant type and priority plus AnalyticsEvent for ad auth errors and usage display support.
Added required GRAVITY_API_KEY to serverEnvSchema and serverProcessEnv for ad serving.

851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.title: Freebuff GLM 5.2 referral reward now selectable on both full
851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.summary: The `freebuffCliOfferedModelIds` export in the CLI model selector now appends `FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID` to the offered model list regardless of `accessTier`, where it previously only appeared for the 'full' tier. The companion validity guard in the landing-screen `useEffect` lost its `accessTier === 'full'` guard too, so a limited-tier user who pressed the banner's earned-GLM action is no longer judged invalid and swapped for the recommended model on the next render. The comment attributes the change to bounty grants being redeemable at limited access, making the referral balance - not the tier - what gates the row.
851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, the `freebuffCliOfferedModelIds` function now returns GLM 5.2 (`FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID`) for both 'full' and 'limited' access tiers, removing the previous `accessTier === 'full'` guard. The `selectionIsValid` check in the landing-screen `useEffect` likewise dropped its `accessTier === 'full'` condition so a limited-tier user who selected GLM via the referral banner is no longer silently swapped to the recommended model.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.title: Freebuff model picker shows reasoning effort per row
fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.summary: The FreebuffModelOption interface gains a `reasoningEffort` field, plus a `getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort` helper in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, so the CLI picker can read the same effort level the completions layer sends. The catalog rows for DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and GPT-5.6 Luna now set `reasoningEffort: 'high'`, sourced from the shared FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_REASONING_EFFORT constant so the bundled base2-free-luna agent and the picker cannot drift. The CLI picker in cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx appends a ' · Reasoning: <level>' suffix to matching rows and includes it in the card width math, so the effort a model runs at is visible before a user commits to it.
fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.evidence: Added reasoningEffort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' to the FreebuffModelOption interface in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, along with the getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort helper; set the field on the DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and GPT-5.6 Luna catalog rows; and cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx now appends a reasoning effort suffix to picker rows and accounts for it in the card width math. The base2-free-luna.ts agent definition reads FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_REASONING_EFFORT for the bundled agent. A new test 'says the reasoning effort on rows whose catalog entry carries one' asserts the suffix renders on Flash, Pro, and Luna rows but not on MiniMax.

changes.what: Added a reasoningEffort field to FreebuffModelOption, a getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort resolver, and set effort on the DeepSeek V4 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and GPT-5.6 Luna catalog rows.
Append a reasoning effort suffix to picker rows and include it in the card width math so the rendered width matches the content.
Fixed a stale comment name from applyOpenRouterReasoningDefaults to applyFreebuffReasoningDefaults to match the shared constant's documented consumer.

55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.title: Windows terminal watchdog opt-in env var and gating logic
55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.summary: Added the `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` env var to `CliEnv` and `getCliEnv()`, and `terminal-watchdog.ts` now refuses to spawn the PowerShell watchdog on Windows unless that variable is truthy, after still honoring `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. The previous behavior on Windows was to always avoid the watchdog unless `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` was unset, relying on EDR/AV avoidance; the change makes the opt-in explicit so targeted CI and debugging can enable it while keeping the default off. `startTerminalWatchdog`'s `isOptedOut` helper was generalized to `isTruthy` and now checks both flags, and the Windows smoke test no longer injects `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG: '1'`, instead deleting both watchdog flags to inherit the parent environment.
55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.evidence: cli/src/types/env.ts adds `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG?: string` with a comment to opt into the Windows PowerShell watchdog; cli/src/utils/env.ts mirrors it in `getCliEnv()` reading `process.env.CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`; cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts renames `isOptedOut` to `isTruthy` and gates `spawnWindowsWatchdog` behind `isTruthy(env.CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG)` on win32; smoke test cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-broker-windows.ts now deletes `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` and `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` from the spawned env and clears the previous hardcoded `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG: '1'` override.
55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer first reads the renamed `isTruthy` helper outside the watchdog file or whether the smoke test change affects existing CI expectations.

6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.title: Freebuff takeover retry logic widened and landing screen buttons
6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.summary: The session retry classifier in `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` now returns `retry` for POST failures on HTTP 408, 429, and 503 (previously only 503 with code `service_overloaded`), expanding the set of failures the CLI can safely retry. `TakeoverPrompt` in `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` removes the retry and outcomeUnknown guards on the Take over action so users can explicitly retry a takeover instead of being forced to restart. This is accompanied by `README.md` adding local development prerequisites (Docker and `.env.local`) and `common/src/constants/openrouter-attribution.ts` gaining clarifying comments about OpenRouter header requirements.
6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.evidence: cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts: `classifyFreebuffSessionRequestFailure` now treats HTTP 408, 429, and 503 POST responses as safe 'retry' (previously only 503 with errorCode service_overloaded), and cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx: the TakeoverPrompt component drops the retry/outcomeUnknown block on the Take over button so users can explicitly retry.

changes.what: Widened POST failure retry classification to include HTTP 408 and 429 alongside 503, returning 'retry' for each.
Removed retry and outcomeUnknown guards on the TakeoverPrompt Take over button, adding a Try takeover again label.
Documented Docker and .env.local requirements for local development.
Added comments documenting OpenRouter header requirements for HTTP-Referer and category limits.

e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.title: Terminal broker replaces Windows stdio pipes with temp file
e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.summary: The terminal command broker on Windows no longer relies on Bun's custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes, which could crash the CLI as an unhandled rejection when their node:net handshake failed, and instead writes the broker result to a one-shot temp file (PROTOCOL_FILE_PREFIX='freebuff-terminal-command-broker-') read back by the parent after child close. Parent liveness is now detected by polling the parent PID instead of holding another private socket, and the broker failure message trimmed to 'Restart Freebuff and try again.'. The Windows smoke test doubles its acceptance deadline to 120_000 ms and exercises 64 repeated packaged-broker spawns after the time-sensitive report injection, while docs/agents-and-tools.md documents the console-free, file-based completion protocol.
e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.evidence: cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts: writeProtocol, waitForParentDisconnect, and createTerminalCommandBroker were rewritten to drop the custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes; instead the broker now writes a one-shot JSON response to a constrained temp file (PROTOCOL_FILE_PREFIX='freebuff-terminal-command-broker-', via protocolPathFromEnv and writeFileSync with flag 'wx') and polls the parent PID; cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-broker-windows.ts: TIMEOUT_MS 60_000->120_000 and added a 64-iteration repeated-broker-spawn loop; cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts: added repeatedCommands result field, the 64-iteration repeated command loop, and relaxed the broker-failure assertion to check only 'Restart Freebuff'; docs/agents-and-tools.md: documented the console-free, file-based completion protocol.
e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout to non-Windows platforms or whether the old fd 3/4 code path was removed entirely versus kept behind a platform check.

changes.what: Removed the custom fd 3/4 stdio pipes and replaced writeProtocol, waitForParentDisconnect, and the completion path with a one-shot temp file written with flag 'wx' and a parent-PID polling loop.
Added a repeatedCommands result field and a 64-iteration repeated-broker-spawn loop, and relaxed the broker-failure assertion to require only 'Restart Freebuff' in the message.
Raised the acceptance deadline from TIMEOUT_MS 60_000 to 120_000 and tightened the OK log line to mention repeated broker spawns.

e93edfe8d2d61a6b285ed4e7614d50a8c9de8e29.summary: The Freebuff session GET now sends the 'x-freebuff-compact-session' header on the CLI's recurring active-session poll so the server can return authoritative session state while omitting quota snapshots the CLI already holds from admission. mergeCompactActiveSession in cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts keeps the prior rateLimit and rateLimitsByModel only when the session identity matches, returning null to signal that the next tick must fetch a full response before compacting again. 76020951df33514036c99751ccb03abd92b47274.title: Add bounded user-agent normalizer for analytics

80bc9c895dd73f9996ae18af67432e9ae1b09181.text: The assistant used to keep tool calls that never got an answer, which could make strict providers reject the whole conversation later. It now drops any unanswered tool call when the conversation reaches a new user message or system message, keeping the history clean and valid. This is internal maintenance for the engineering team; it does not add a visible feature for users. Nothing changes in your daily use today, though it quietly prevents certain errors from stacking up in agent conversations.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds the ability to export your conversations to a file with a new /export command, makes DeepSeek V4 Flash the default model for new sessions, and gives you clearer Freebucks pricing and limits directly in the CLI model picker. The Freebucks system now shows prices and your wallet balance when choosing an AI model, so you can see exactly what a session will cost before you start. The /export command lets you save a full conversation as Markdown or JSON, and the landing screen now offers an upgrade path when you run out of free sessions. Several advertiser and billing controls were added or tightened behind the scenes, and the CLI now shows day-scale wait times for rate limits plus a one-time Freebucks intro card on first metered launch.

21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.text: The referral reward you earn by inviting friends is no longer tied to a single older model. At full access, inviting friends now grants you one extra session in your regular daily pool, and at limited access it unlocks a newer, better model as your reward. The old model is withdrawn from free use, and the on-screen banners and picker now use your earned balance to decide what the reward actually is. This is live today, and it applies to Freebuff users everywhere regardless of region. You will notice a different label and a different reward in the referral banner, but you do not need to do anything.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 makes it easier to see how much of your free allowance you have used and adds a new default AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, across the CLI, Web, and Desktop. A new /dashboard slash command opens your account page so you can check your streaks, activity, tokens, sessions, and settings, while onboarding no longer traps you in redirect loops after a failed save. The model picker leads with GLM 5.3 Flash and removes MiniMax M3 from the free models, and the /reasoning command lets you set how hard the selected model thinks before each turn. For users in restricted regions or on VPNs, spend limits now apply per region with clearer refusal messages, and clipboard copies abort stale operations so a broken display server no longer freezes the terminal. Upgrading gives you a working usage dashboard, a fresh default model that is unmetered, and steadier behavior when network or region limits kick in.

92a6961b894204c5620f9dd77cd2606e54b9a397.text: The command palette now reads directly from what you're typing instead of a slightly delayed copy of it. Developers using the assistant in the terminal, web app, or desktop app who type slash commands or mentions will no longer have the highlighted suggestion jump to the wrong spot when the screen is busy. No action is needed from you, and nothing is renamed or removed. This fix is live today.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.text: The model picker now shows how thoroughly each AI model thinks before answering, displayed as a 'Reasoning: high' label next to models like DeepSeek V4 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna. Developers using the Freebuff CLI will see this extra line when choosing a model, helping them pick one that matches how much detail they want. The web and desktop apps already use the same reasoning settings internally, so this mainly just makes what's already happening visible in the terminal picker.

851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.text: When you look at the list of AI models you can pick in Freebuff, the GLM 5.2 model earned through referrals is now offered to you no matter which access tier you are on (free or full), instead of only being available on the full tier. This change affects Freebuff users at the limited access tier, who previously could not select their earned GLM 5.2 reward from the model picker. If you are a limited-tier user who earned GLM 5.2 through a bounty referral, you will now be able to choose it directly from the model list instead of having your selection silently switched to the recommended model.

6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.text: The Freebuff assistant will now automatically retry starting a session when it hit certain network or capacity errors (timeouts, being rate-limited, or the service being temporarily busy), instead of giving up. You are a Freebuff developer who runs the assistant from the terminal, uses the web or desktop app, or integrates via the SDK. You'll notice that when a takeover was interrupted by one of these transient errors, you now get a 'Retry now' option on the screen and can start again right away rather than being told to restart or being blocked until a scheduled retry.

55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.text: The Freebuff CLI gained a new hidden switch that lets operators explicitly choose whether a background safety net runs on Windows machines. That safety net is a helper program that cleans up the terminal if the CLI crashes without shutting down properly; on Windows it was previously always turned off to avoid tripping antivirus software, and now it stays off by default but can be turned on with a simple on/off flag. If you are a Freebuff service operator running the CLI on Windows, you can now enable that helper for targeted CI runs and debugging sessions by setting the new flag to on. If you are not such an operator, this setting does nothing for you: you will not see this option, you do not need to touch it, and nothing about how your sessions behave changes.

3a8cc3135b1201b6403abb26762a309b269c8119.text: The Freebuff CLI now remembers exactly why a session failed and whether it will try again on its own, instead of just showing a vague error. This affects Freebuff developers who use the terminal or desktop app with a free account. You will see clearer, more specific messages when a session request times out or hits a server issue, plus a countdown when the app is retrying for you, and the assistant will no longer repeatedly try the same action when it is not allowed to.

e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.text: The CLI used special hidden data pipes to talk between its own processes on Windows, but those pipes could fail silently and crash the whole terminal session. The change replaces those pipes with a small temporary file the parent process reads after the child command finishes, which is far more reliable. This affects Freebuff CLI users, especially on Windows, who run terminal commands through the assistant. You should notice fewer sudden crashes when the assistant runs shell commands for your project, and no action is needed because the change happens automatically as part of the upgrade.

d62db1eebd81b366812817ac479860ba7ab066e9.text: The release notes that come with Freebuff were rewritten to list the AI models you can pick from right now, including GPT-5.6 Luna and a refreshed DeepSeek V4 Flash, and to mention GLM 5.2 as something you can unlock. This is a plain documentation update for the public release README, so it doesn't change what the assistant does or what any model can do. You won't notice any difference while coding; the only effect is that the printed list of available models is now accurate.

95f7ba2869aed9e0bd0ef259d86becf75a4ac23e.text: Freebuff's engineers added a new internal safety system that watches how long the assistant's database lookups take and whether they ever cross pre-set speed limits. It only affects Freebuff's own operations team, who use it to spot slowdowns before you notice them, so there is nothing new to click or configure on your end today. These limits are intentionally generous launch guardrails, meant to be tightened later once the team has seen a week of real-world traffic patterns.

372bcb13336cfa7eb8060b1b80208c8a9884fb9f.text: Freebuff has added a new AI model, Meta Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor, that is only available through the Freebuff web app, not the command-line or desktop versions. This model is capped at 60 requests per minute across all Freebuff users, so it requires a special queue to manage access fairly. Nothing you do in your coding sessions is affected unless you use the web app, and even then, you will only see it if the service has it turned on for your account.

e93edfe8d2d61a6b285ed4e7614d50a8c9de8e29.text: The Freebuff CLI's background check for keeping your session alive now asks the server for a slimmer update when you're already actively coding, so it doesn't needlessly re-download information about your usage limits that it already knows. This reduces unnecessary network traffic while your session is active, and if a compact response ever comes back for a different session (like after a model switch), the CLI will automatically fetch a full update next time to make sure your usage counts stay accurate. You get a smoother, less chatty experience while a session is in progress, with no visible action required on your part. Live today.

956dcf938814d5da8af5f2c1c1216f14d1bcd769.text: A new AI model called GLM 5.2 can now be used by people in restricted regions. If you live somewhere where Freebuff limits which models you can pick, and you earned a special reward (like from referring friends), you can finally spend that reward on GLM 5.2 instead of being forced to use the default model. Nothing changes for people who don't have that reward, and you only see this option if you're in one of those limited areas and actually unlocked the model through a bounty grant.

76020951df33514036c99751ccb03abd92b47274.text: Freebuff added a small piece of analytics plumbing that turns each incoming web request's browser/device label into a single, safe, short token before it is recorded. It is aimed at the Freebuff engineering team only, since it only feeds internal dashboards and is not yet attached to any user-facing event. You will not see it behave any differently today; the code sits in place and does nothing until a later step wires it into an analytics call, so there is no visible effect or action for you right now.

7005d45cc1116a842069903738371fc3c64f2c92.text: Freebuff consolidated the logic that decides which configuration files its assistant is allowed to look at into shared, reusable pieces. Instead of each part of the app having its own copy of the rules, the CLI and the developer kit (SDK) now both use the exact same checklist to figure out if a file is a real secret file, a harmless template that shows the format, or something it should ignore completely. This means the assistant is now much less likely to accidentally treat an example file like `.env.example` as if it were your actual credentials file. This is internal maintenance work for Freebuff's engineering team.

a47be121a650358f747794cf743870e75d35e6b3.text: Two helper scripts that run the assistant on sample browser and repository-analysis tasks were renamed so the test-runner no longer mistakes them for actual tests; previously, running the project's tests could crash because those scripts tried to connect to a real assistant account and then quit early when it was missing. This only affects the engineering team's local development tools: everyday users, subscribers, and free-tier users will notice nothing different in how the assistant works. Nothing in this update changes what you can do with the assistant today.

60dd01fe109f976b0e1e7eea23b9bd0e3ba67b6e.text: Limited-tier users can now launch GLM 5.2 sessions, but only when they have a bounty grant that is redeemable across every region, so the unlock is keyed on their session balance rather than their access tier. In daily use, a limited-tier user who earned a bounty grant sees the GLM card as usable and can start a session, while everyone else without a grant still sees the regular referral bonus line. This is live today for anyone whose account holds a bounty-eligible GLM grant, and no action is required from other users.

f28ecce37f526a75beecd2e0c8d82da50630abba.text: Freebuff removed the older, pricier MiMo 2.5 Pro option from its free helper lineup, so the assistant no longer spins up that model automatically when helping you for free. You might notice it's no longer offered as an automatic choice in the free list of helpers, though if you were already mid-task with it, that session finishes as normal. New free requests simply skip it and use the other free models instead.

6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.text: The CLI now has two new slash commands, /ads:enable and /ads:disable, that let you turn on or off contextual ads shown above your input box. When ads are enabled, a small ad banner appears with a link to an advertiser's site, rotates to a new ad roughly every minute, and quietly pre-loads the next one just before it's needed so there is no delay. Each time an ad is shown to you, the system records an impression and credits a small number of free compute credits to your account, which you can see listed separately on the usage banner. The feature is now live, requires no setup beyond running /ads:enable once, and you can turn it off at any time with /ads:disable.

c799255a7afc9de583e6fed26712c5a5ec2c48fd.text: The default AI model offered to people using the Freebuff web and Cloud versions has been switched from DeepSeek V4 Flash to GPT-5.6 Luna. This affects Freebuff users who start new conversations in their browser, not those using the desktop or command-line apps, which still default to Flash. For most users this is a no-action update: GPT-5.6 Luna loads automatically on the next page load, though it draws on a shared daily pool so heavy demand could steer you back to Flash.

a6571b01b1383c6806b1344375d38525846701ac.text: Freebuff removed the 'Beta' tag from its Cloud product, showing it is ready for everyday use, and added a new Enterprise row for organizations that want a custom setup. These updates appear in the Freebuff product list you see when deciding which version to use. If you are evaluating Freebuff for your team or company, you can now see Cloud as a stable option and contact the team about Enterprise plans.

25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.title: Muse Spark fallback to GPT-5.6 Luna and tagged Queue model
25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.summary: Three new constants in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts define the runtime fallback path for a rate-limited Muse Spark request: MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID reroutes to FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS = 10_000 caps the wait before rerouting, and MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE carries the picker copy. The Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor model row is retitled with tagline 'Queue' and gains a taglineTooltip field on FreebuffModelOption so the picker can carry that promise without adding a second line, and the isNew flag is dropped. Because the fallback must be a model the caller is already entitled to, Luna is chosen as it shares the same shared daily premium pool as Muse Spark.
25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.evidence: The diff adds four new exports and a new interface field in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts: MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID = FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS = 10_000, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE = 'Falls back to GPT-5.6 Luna if the queue is too long.', and taglineTooltip?: string on FreebuffModelOption. The Muse Spark Contributor model row changes its tagline from '1M context' to 'Queue' and sets taglineTooltip to MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE, and isNew is removed.
25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.unknowns: The diff adds the constants and the tooltip field plus retags the picker row, but does not show the code that reads MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS, or MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE to actually perform the reroute, nor the client/server sync that must keep the notice. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.title: Windows terminal health reporting and watchdog arming telemetry
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.summary: The CLI introduces a new windows-terminal-health module that centralizes Windows terminal-failure reporting for both the command broker and the terminal watchdog, routing events through PostHog when analytics is initialized and otherwise queuing them directly into the Axiom shipper before draining. cli/src/index.tsx now drains queued client logs right after the APP_LAUNCHED event on Freebuff Windows launches, so a health row ships before the PowerShell watchdog is armed and survives an endpoint-security kill of that spawn for rapid-resume on the next --continue launch. The watchdog is no longer opt-in via CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG on Windows; it is armed by default and suppressed only by the existing CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG escape hatch, with a 10-second WINDOWS_ARM_TIMEOUT_MS arming monitor reporting a timeout if the armed marker is never written. A new TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED event joins TERMINAL_BROKER_SPAWN_FAILED in the always-track analytics set, and the broker's old sanitizeTerminalBrokerVersion helper is replaced by sanitizeWindowsCliVersion in the shared health module.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.evidence: The diff adds cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-health.ts, which defines `reportWindowsTerminalFailure`, `deliverWindowsTerminalFailure`, `sanitizeWindowsCliVersion`, and the `WindowsTerminalHealthDeliveryDeps`/`WindowsTerminalFailure` types, and is imported by cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts and cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts (both replacing their old inline reporting). cli/src/index.tsx now calls `drainClientLogs()` for IS_FREEBUFF on win32 after APP_LAUNCHED. cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts drop `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts adds `TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED = 'cli.terminal_watchdog_failed'`, and common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts adds it to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS`.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.migration: No action is required; Freebuff Windows users now get the watchdog armed by default instead of needing CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG, and those who rely on the opt-in variable to avoid it should keep setting CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads the new always-track TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED events in dashboards, or the rollout state of arming the watchdog by default for all Freebuff Windows users.

changes.what: New module consolidating Windows terminal-failure reporting for the broker and watchdog, with a fallback Axiam queue path when analytics is not initialized.
Broker failure reporting delegates to reportWindowsTerminalFailure and its old sanitizeTerminalBrokerVersion helper is removed.
Watchdog now reports spawn, bootstrap, and arming-stage failures via reportWindowsTerminalFailure and tracks a 10s arming timeout.
getCliEnv stops reading CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG from process.env.
CliEnv type drops the CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG opt-in member.
After APP_LAUNCHED, Freebuff on Windows now drains queued client logs before the watchdog is armed.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.title: Block 30 throwaway email domains flagged as referral farm activity
81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.summary: Thirty new domains are appended to `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` in `common/src/util/disposable-email.ts`, the array consumed by referral-abuse detection. The list was compiled from prod on 2026-08-03, with each domain meeting a threshold of >=20 Freebuff accounts and >=75% already banned, covering 7,129 accounts of which 6,699 were banned before the list existed. Matching is by exact domain or any subdomain, and the comment notes many new entries are deliberate Gmail lookalikes or single-day mints like gmito.my.id's 288 accounts.
81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.evidence: The diff adds 30 new domain entries to the `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` array in `common/src/util/disposable-email.ts`, accompanied by a comment block compiled 2026-08-03 from prod data showing each new domain has >=20 Freebuff accounts and >=75% banned.
81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer calls `classifyEmailDomain` or how referral-abuse detection gates a referred account on a `disposable` classification. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.title: Terminal broker performs bounded self-cleanup instead of waiting
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.summary: The terminal command broker now reaps its own process group immediately after writing the protocol result, rather than waiting for the parent CLI to disconnect first, which prevents Windows taskkill from blocking the parent renderer thread after every successful command. defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves the CLI entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') instead of reading process.argv[1], and createTerminalCommandBroker accepts an injectable terminate function plus wraps spawn and pipe failures in brokerFailure with the new TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_RECOVERY guidance. The SDK's direct spawn path replaced its infinite cleanup loop with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper (KILL_ESCALATION_MS) for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL, so detached background descendants from SYNC commands are reaped within a capped window instead of risking an infinite wait, and the abort/timeout path now finishes tracking after the same bounded post-kill observation.
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.evidence: In cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker no longer waits for parentDisconnected before calling reapOwnProcessGroup() after writeProtocol; instead it immediately runs its own cleanup, and defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves its own entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') rather than process.argv[1]. In sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts, the infinite while-loop in spawnDirectTerminalCommand was replaced with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper, and the abort/timeout cleanup now stops tracking after a KILL_ESCALATION_MS post-kill window. In cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker-failure smoke path now constructs a real broker via createTerminalCommandBroker({ invocation }) that points at a missing exe and asserts the resulting 'Failed to start terminal command broker' / 'Restart Freebuff' guidance.
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.unknowns: Whether the smoke-test harness fully exercises the new entrypoint resolution across non-binary and binary builds.

changes.what: Broker runs its own reapOwnProcessGroup immediately after writeProtocol instead of awaiting parentDisconnected, and broker startup/spawn failures are routed through brokerFailure with TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_RECOVERY; defaultBrokerInvocation resolves entry.ts via import.meta.dir.

Direct spawn path uses bounded waitForProcessExit (KILL_ESCALATION_MS) for SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation instead of an infinite loop, and abort/timeout cleanup stops tracking after the bounded post-kill window.
Broker-failure smoke path now builds a real broker with createTerminalCommandBroker pointing at a missing exe and asserts the Restart Freebuff recovery guidance.

17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.title: Self-update test script and freebuff CLI 0.0.137
17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.summary: A new `test-published-self-update.ts` Bun script exercises the published self-update flow end to end. The script installs a prior freebuff npm launcher via npm install --global --no-audit --no-fund, seeds the prior binary from a GitHub release asset, writes a `freebuff-metadata.json` record, launches the old binary, then polls that metadata file until it reports the new version, asserting a successful handoff and a Tree-sitter smoke run; the CLI release package in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.0.136` to `0.0.137`. The script is a maintainer-facing release verification tool covering the npm-to-binary update handoff, not a runtime path change. It validates the launcher's update-detection, relaunch message, and Tree-sitter smoke path after an in-place binary swap.
17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.evidence: New file `cli/scripts/test-published-self-update.ts` adds a Bun script that installs a prior Freebuff npm launcher, seeds the binary from a GitHub release asset, launches it, and polls `freebuff-metadata.json` for the updated version; `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` version field moved from `0.0.136` to `0.0.137`.

changes.what: Added `test-published-self-update.ts`, a Bun script that installs a prior `freebuff` npm launcher, seeds the matching binary from a GitHub release asset, writes `freebuff-metadata.json`, launches the old binary, and polls the metadata file until it reports the new version while asserting.
Bumped the CLI release package version from `0.0.136` to `0.0.137`.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.title: Windows terminal command guard toggles focus reporting around child
f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.summary: A new `installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard` in the CLI disables the TUI's mouse and focus reporting before a Windows terminal command spawns and restores them only after the last overlapping command exits, so descendants that open CONIN$/CONOUT$ directly cannot paint sequences like `^[[<35;187;32M` over the alternate screen. The guard subscribes to terminal command state, which the SDK now publishes via `subscribeToTerminalCommandState` and the `runTerminalCommand.subscribeToState` property added in `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`. State listeners run synchronously before spawn and a listener may abort the run, closing the re-entrant gap that would otherwise miss the abort event. The CLI installs the guard after renderer creation and removes it on renderer destroy.
f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-command-guard.ts` exports `installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard`, which listens to terminal command state and toggles focus reporting via `ENABLE_FOCUS_REPORTING`/`DISABLE_FOCUS_REPORTING` sequences; `cli/src/index.tsx` imports and wires it to the renderer's destroy event. In `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`, `runTerminalCommand` now calls `beginTerminalCommandTracking()` before spawn and exposes `runTerminalCommand.subscribeToState` (the `subscribeToTerminalCommandState` export).
f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.unknowns: The rollout plan and whether the guard becomes default on all platforms rather than win32-only, given the later broker refactor referenced in sibling commits.

changes.what: Adds the Windows terminal command guard that consumes terminal command state and toggles focus/mouse reporting around child processes.
Introduces terminal command state tracking, a synchronous subscriber API, and exposes it via `runTerminalCommand.subscribeToState`.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.title: Terminal isolation becomes a synchronous lease controller
32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.summary: Interactive hosts now pass a `terminalCommandIsolation` capability into `runTerminalCommand`, which acquires isolation synchronously before `spawn` and releases it only after the command's whole process group exits. The CLI's new `TerminalProtocolController` (replacing the former `windows-terminal-command-guard`) disables mouse and focus reporting during any active command lease, keeps focus detection live, and restores the protocols exactly once after the final process exits, while headless SDK consumers can omit the option entirely.
32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/terminal-protocol-controller.ts` defines `TerminalProtocolController`, exports `terminalCommandIsolation` and `installTerminalProtocolController`; deleted `cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-command-guard.ts`; `cli/src/index.tsx` imports and installs the controller via `installTerminalProtocolController(renderer, ...)`; `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts`, and `sdk/src/run.ts` pass `terminalCommandIsolation` into `runTerminalCommand`.
32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added `cli/src/utils/terminal-protocol-controller.ts` with `TerminalProtocolController`, `terminalCommandIsolation`, and `installTerminalProtocolController`; `cli/src/index.tsx` installs the controller on the renderer and disposes it on destroy; removed.
Added `terminalCommandIsolation` parameter to `runTerminalCommand` and threaded it through `CodebuffClientOptions` and the tool-call path so hosts can pass a pre-spawn isolation lease.
Routed the CLI's `terminalCommandIsolation` into both `codebuff-client.ts` and the bash command path in `commands/router.ts`.
Redirected `use-terminal-focus.ts` to subscribe to the new controller's parsed focus state instead of owning its own stdin focus listener.
Documented the new terminal command isolation boundary and the `acquire()` lease contract in `docs/agents-and-tools.md`.

Added a packaged `--smoke-terminal-isolation` gate in `cli/src/index.tsx` driven by `cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-isolation-windows.ts` and `cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-isolation.ts` to verify protocol isolation over a real console under winpty.

13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.title: GPT-5.6 cache-aware step prompt placement
13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.summary: A new `ephemeralTrailingMessageBreaksCache` gate in `common/src/constants/model-config.ts` returns true for `gpt-5.6` models, whose OpenAI prompt cache is destroyed when a trailing message is deleted on the next step. When the gate is true, `run-agent-step.ts` stops appending a per-step ephemeral step prompt and instead places a single resident STEP_PROMPT once at the turn's start via `loopAgentSteps`; for all other models only the ephemeral form is appended per step as before. The shared `stepPromptMessage` builder in `util/messages.ts` distinguishes the two forms by omitting `timeToLive` for resident prompts and keeping `timeToLive: 'agentStep'` for ephemeral ones. `agents/context-pruner.ts` was updated alongside to carry a resident STEP_PROMPT through summarization instead of dropping it. The change keeps GPT-5.6 history append-only so its prefix cache stays warm, at the cost of one extra persistent system-style message per turn for those models only.

6e1168a960e83d3c2651c6765b504f45f0d091b9.title: Cloud planner routes on DeepSeek V4 Flash instead of MiniMax M3
6e1168a960e83d3c2651c6765b504f45f0d091b9.summary: The Freebuff Cloud custom-stack planner now pins `CLOUD_PLANNER_MODEL_ID` to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID` in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, replacing the previous `FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_M3_MODEL_ID` used for full access (limited tiers already ran `CLOUD_PLANNER_LIMITED_MODEL_ID`). Accordingly, `cloudPlannerAgentIdForModel` now ignores its model argument and always returns `CLOUD_PLANNER_AGENT_ID`, since both planner variants resolve to the same model and the model can no longer distinguish limited from full access. This follows the V4-Flash-0731 GA build becoming both the strongest coding/tool-use model served and the cheapest, collapsing the previous planner-vs-build cost argument that kept planning on MiniMax M3.

31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.title: CLI lands IP-capped sessions on the model picker and stops polling
31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.summary: When too many distinct users share a free session on one egress IP, the server returns the `ip_capped` status, and the CLI now routes it to the Freebuff landing screen instead of looping through the chat surface. The poll loop treats `ip_capped` as terminal (no further ticks), the session API accepts it on a 429 POST, and a new landing branch shows how many other users are ahead and a short retry time. Separately, the shared core exports `FREEBUFF_ROOT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_OPENINGS` and `hasFreebuffRootSystemPromptOpening` as a byte-exact prefix gate so only root requests opening with a canonical freebuff system prompt admit to free mode, with a legacy pre-2026-07-07 opening kept for stuck older installs.

25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.text: When you pick the Muse Spark assistant and it is momentarily full, the assistant now silently switches you to the GPT-5.6 Luna assistant within ten seconds instead of making you wait in line. The Muse Spark line in the model picker is now labeled Queue, with a small explanation that it can send you to GPT-5.6 Luna if the line gets too long. This affects Freebuff users who choose Muse Spark, and they will see the new Queue label and tooltip in the model picker. Nothing needs to be done on your end; if Muse Spark is busy, you simply continue with GPT-5.6 Luna without any action from you.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release introduces new AI model options including GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Flash as the recommended free model, shifts several models between free and premium tiers, and adds a built-in Cloud project planner tool that lets the assistant design and hand off project plans for your approval before any code is written. The installer now resumes interrupted downloads and works behind HTTP proxies, the agent loop automatically retries when a model response stream is cut off mid-output, and chat sessions properly abort in-flight runs so switching conversations can no longer overwrite transcripts. Users hitting daily usage caps now land on a clear waiting screen that reports the session limit instead of looping, streak bonuses now refill weekly with increasing rewards, and the free model picker hides retired models like Kimi K2.7 Code while surfacing superseded-model replacement nudges directly on the selected row. Upgrading gives you access to the new model lineup, a plan-first Cloud workflow, more resilient downloads and streaming, and clearer messaging around usage limits and plan recommendations.

405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.text: The Freebuff assistant now automatically resets the terminal on Windows when the program crashes (hard kill, crash, or force-quit) without any setup, instead of requiring an extra setting to be turned on first. If the watchdog that performs this reset fails to start or times out, a bounded telemetry event (TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED) is now reliably sent through your analytics pipeline rather than being silently dropped, and the existing broker failure event follows the same reliable delivery path. Who this affects: Freebuff Windows users, with the watchdog on by default; anyone whose endpoint security conflicts with the watchdog can keep using the existing suppression flag.

b5111f885a8e3b737cffff102f353444ea860ada.text: The system that tracks whether an advertiser's promoted post is allowed, blocked, or being reviewed now records a fourth outcome: when a post is outright rejected, it is marked as 'flagged', not just 'rejected'. This status and its label are now defined in the same list the rest of the system reads from, so dashboards and moderation tools can display and filter by it instead of leaving the 'flagged' posts unrepresented. The change is live today and requires no action from you; it only makes the internal tracking of rejected advertiser posts accurate in the places Freebuff operators look at.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.text: When you run a command through the assistant inside the terminal on Windows, stray mouse and keyboard focus signals that the program prints to the screen can now be blocked while that command is running, so they no longer get painted over the interface as garbage text. This only affects the Windows desktop or terminal version of the product; Mac and Linux users see no difference. You do not need to do anything, and there is no visible change for most people, but Windows users who run shell commands inside the assistant will no longer see flickering or garbled mouse/focus output appearing over the chat while those commands execute.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.text: When you run a command in the terminal through Freebuff, the CLI now uses a new terminal-protocol controller (the old Windows terminal command guard was removed) that turns off mouse and focus reports before the command starts and restores them only after the whole command process tree has fully exited, so those reports stay isolated from your interactive session. This also applies to any code using the SDK to run terminal commands. You may notice the terminal no longer shows stray focus or mouse sequences painted over the interface while a command is running. Developers using the removed `subscribeToTerminalCommandState` or `installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard` should migrate to `terminalCommandIsolation` via CodebuffClientOptions; headless SDK users can omit it.

ae8c38c6a145ee540ec48aea9027714917d9da36.text: The engineering team reorganized how the list of AI models shown in the Freebuff command-line interface is built, so the referral bonus model is added in exactly one place rather than being mixed into the main grid. This is an internal test and build change, it does not add or remove any model you can pick from. You will not see anything new or different in your daily use of Freebuff.

612e2a39e0355c12169f3dd37ce5e3bf09942e02.text: A new helper was added that turns your first message in a conversation into a short, clean title for the tab or chat window, so each chat can be labeled with a quick summary like "Update README file" instead of a long snippet. It is built as a shared piece of code that the desktop app, the web version, and the server can all use, but no part of the app is actually using it yet, so you will not see any new behavior today. The helper also cleans up common mistakes the assistant makes when writing titles, like extra quotes or a trailing period, and shortens anything that is too long to fit in a tab label. This is internal preparation work that does nothing visible until a future update connects it to the actual chat windows.

6e1168a960e83d3c2651c6765b504f45f0d091b9.text: The free project-planning helper that runs behind the Freebuff Cloud interface now uses DeepSeek V4 Flash instead of the previous model, MiniMax M3, and both limited-access and full-access plans use that same model now. Who it affects: Freebuff Cloud users (the web-based AI coding assistant on the free tier). Everyday impact: You don't need to do anything or notice anything different - your free planning sessions keep working the same way, but the assistant now runs its planning step on a different, cheaper, and stronger model. Existing sessions are unaffected, and no action is required.

3e5be71544b2879899a0dea5162bf6f7e8195bcb.text: Freebuff has added a new AI model called Claude Fable 5 as a limited-time trial in the model picker. The picker now shows a new "LIMITED TRIAL" section with a count of how many sessions remain globally and per user; when the shared pool runs out or your personal quota is spent, the row disappears or shows a reset countdown. This is live today for Freebuff users on any plan; if you do not see the trial row yet, the server has not opened the pool, and no action is needed from you since the model is pinned to a dedicated agent that only runs while the offer is active.

a5cb80f3d735b96b63f2fc075689ab4ed9955056.text: When the assistant loads your saved model choice, it now silently swaps any model we no longer recommend for the one we do, every single time, instead of doing it just once. This affects you if you previously selected a model like MiMo 2.5 or MiniMax M3; you will notice that each new session opens on DeepSeek V4 Flash instead, even if you manually re-picked the older one in a prior session. Picking a superseded model mid-session still works for that session, it just will not be remembered as your default next time. No action needed from you; the change is live today.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.text: The team added 30 new throwaway email providers to a watchlist used to catch fake sign-ups that try to claim referral rewards. This only affects the system that detects abusive account creation, not your own email, and you will not see or need to do anything different in the app. The change is already live, and it quietly stops new accounts created on those domains from being treated as legitimate referrals.

31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.text: When too many people on the same internet network try to use Freebuff at once, you now see a clear message telling you how many others are ahead of you and how long to wait, rather than the app silently retrying or acting confused. Anyone who has hit the Freebuff model picker recently (and anyone running an older client that already learned the new status code on a 429 response) will see this landing message the moment their network is too busy. The change is live today in the Freebuff CLI/web/desktop clients: picking a model that returns the new ip_capped condition stops the assistant from polling the server every few seconds and instead shows your spot in line with a short retry timer, so you aren't left staring at a frozen or looping screen.

8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.title: OpenTUI native bundle install gets recovery and staging logic
8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.summary: The CLI build now sources its OpenTUI native bundle from a staging directory written to by ensureOpenTuiNativeBundle, which seals the bundle with a .freebuff-native-bundle.json receipt of sha256 file hashes and swaps it atomically so a stale split install fails before the binary step. prepareOpenTuiNativeBundle resolves both @opentui/core and @opentui/react up front, runs bun install with --os and --cpu flags into the staging root, and replaces the old patchOpenTuiAssetPaths and tar-based fetch path in build-binary.ts.

8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer or release flow relies on the new receipt file or how the recovery directory cleanup is scheduled across builds.

ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.title: Streak bonus note gates on earned streak and model picker reorders

Separately, `FREEBUFF_MODELS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` was reordered so `GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL` sorts before `MINIMAX_M3_MODEL`, and the Mimo 2.5 Pro retirement note was dated 2026-07-31, matching the earlier staged-removal pattern used for Kimi K2.7 Code. The test suite asserts this ordering with 'orders Luna above MiniMax while keeping the saved premium model focused'.
