02f42768b0bc73acb01625d4d082a2f6f72d497e.text: Paid Freebuff subscribers now see more AI models listed when they open the model picker in the CLI. If your account has a paid subscription tier, the picker adds the models that come with your plan alongside the usual free list. You don't have to do anything, and if your subscription tier isn't set or you're on the free tier, the picker looks and behaves exactly as before.

389f40a9a9a113232c22a5e93ee40d01a4ee7b08.text: When the assistant needs to run a command on a Windows computer, it looks for a program called Git Bash to do the talking. This update moves all the logic for finding Git Bash into a single shared spot, so the main app, the desktop window, and the startup script all agree on where to look. The big fix is for people who installed Git without having administrator rights - the old search only checked a few hard-coded folders, so it missed per-user installs, Scoop installs, and Git installed onto a drive other than C:. Now it checks every location Windows uses for programs, including where Scoop, Chocolatey, and portable Git put their files, and only falls back to the Windows registry if nothing on disk is found.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model for both the command-line tool and the web app, followed by Solar Pro 4 in the model picker. New slash commands /dashboard and /reasoning let you check your account usage and control how much the model thinks before responding. A new subscription system offers Starter, Plus, and Pro paid tiers that add to your free sessions instead of replacing them, with per-region daily spend caps and a hard 2x ceiling on live sessions for safety. The CLI clipboard now times out and aborts stale copies, and ad delivery moves to real first-party inventory with creative sanitization. Upgrading gives you a new default model, account dashboard, reasoning controls, paid plans that top up free usage, and steadier spending limits.

21e20ab6257f3141ddca47ec45624e70688a4bc1.text: Engineers removed a technical tag that used to tell the assistant apart between two reasons you might be blocked from starting a coding session: running too many tabs at once versus using up your daily quota. Now, any time the assistant blocks a new session it always means the daily session quota is exhausted, so the message you see will only ever be about your free-session allowance. This is internal bookkeeping only, no visible change for users.

c731787cd02fea9b5d37c9e5e6fb06c0e3897045.text: The assistant's free session (Freebuff) no longer retries to connect at a fixed, identical pace when something goes wrong. Instead it now waits a little longer each time and adds a small random timing offset to each retry and regular check so many copies of the app do not all ask the server at exactly the same moments. It also honors a "retry-after" instruction from the server when one is provided, to wait the right amount of time before the next attempt. You as a free-tier user won't notice the timing change, but during a service problem you are less likely to pile onto the very moment the service is struggling to recover. This is live today.

31731d4b275ad637ad19e9531442b3f5acaa8d7f.text: Freebuff engineers added a way to track, in their internal logging system called Axiom, the exact moments when a long AI response gets interrupted (for example, the network drops mid-message, or the model runs out of output tokens while thinking). The tracking now records not just that an interruption happened, but how many such interruptions stacked up in a row and what type it was (interruption vs output limit), giving the team better diagnostic data. This is internal observability work for the Freebuff team; you as a user do not need to take any action and will not notice any difference in your daily use.

6741ac4a35ff3d5b290540a363ae19c6c5c485cf.text: The Freebuff service now reports first-time usage and follow-up activity to Reddit Ads more carefully. It waits to fire retention reports until the exact calendar-mark anniversaries (1 day, 7 days, 24 days after a user's first day), instead of firing them the first time any threshold is crossed. Delivery of each report now retries once on temporary network-style errors and tells callers whether it succeeded or was intentionally turned off, rather than silently failing. This is internal advertising-attribution plumbing operated by whoever runs the Freebuff service (via configuration and tokens set at deployment); it does not change anything you can see or do in Freebuff today.

74ee22bd83306ec1e06b515b52e03e43a31b41cd.text: Free sessions per day went from 5 to 6, so you get one extra hourly session of premium models like MiniMax M3 each day. This affects Freebuff users on the free tier in full-access regions such as the US, Canada, UK, and EU. Starting today, the dashboard and help text show 6 daily sessions instead of 5, but there's nothing you need to do for the change to take effect.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff 1.0.685 adds new models, raises the daily free session limit, and makes the installer work behind HTTP proxies. GPT-5.6 Luna is a new free model you can pick, DeepSeek V4 Pro becomes the CLI's recommended default, and MiniMax M3 moves into a shared premium pool so the picker can flip to Flash when it runs out. The daily free session quota goes up from 5 to 6, and the landing screen now shows the counter inside the model selector scrollbox. The installer adds retry/timeout handling, HTTP proxy support, and safe resume for partial downloads, while chat switches abort in-flight runs to stop transcripts getting overwritten. Telemetry now tracks desktop event-loop health, turn stalls, and background waits to help diagnose slowness.

9262d077baa57360516b372dae789cd193f7a15a.text: A new cap of six daily sessions has been added for fresh users starting on Freebuff's web and cloud versions when they use standard, non-premium models. Only the browser-based version enforces this limit to prevent bots from signing up and immediately creating many projects; the desktop and command-line apps remain unlimited. This cap applies today to standard free models, not to premium ones you reach after referring friends. No action is required, however, Freebuff engineers have not yet flipped the switch that puts this cap into effect, so your daily limit will not change yet.

8785289028f63c9a6d0f34de8380e3de400c1f3c.text: The assistant now treats the MiniMax M3 model as a premium option that counts against your small daily allowance of five sessions, rather than letting you use it without limit. If you usually start conversations on MiniMax M3 and run out of those five daily slots, the assistant will automatically switch you to the unlimited DeepSeek V4 Flash model so you can keep going instead of getting stuck on a rate-limited screen. You, as a Freebuff user, will notice the counter showing how many of your five premium sessions you've used and, once they're gone, the recommended starting model will flip to the always-available fallback. This change is live today across the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app.

380909638150bde314b3d4eb96bcd7664fa07529.text: The Freebuff CLI now uses a single, shared routine that every quit path calls: pressing Ctrl+C, running /exit, hitting Escape on the exit button, or closing the login picker and takeover prompt. That routine stops any in-progress run, ends the Freebuff session seat, stops the engagement timer, then flushes pending analytics and client-side logs with a one-second timeout before exiting, guaranteeing the same tidy cleanup happens no matter how you quit. The launcher also passes its process id onward, so a package subprocess can detect when the parent wrapper has vanished and shut itself down cleanly, which fixes silent hangs when a tool like taskkill or pkill kills the launcher mid-session.

4b03dcbd2a7791366306ab976dba52fd9659b6d6.text: Freebuff has added a new behind-the-scenes connection that lets its advertising partners tell when someone sends their very first message to the assistant, so those partners can measure how well their ads bring in new users. This is part of the internal systems that power the free, ad-supported tier of the service, and it runs automatically on Freebuff's servers. You do not need to do anything and will not see any difference in your experience, but it helps explain why Freebuff can offer coding help at no charge.

0b35949fad7bbaf605afbd048ca912c14d4a3173.text: The Freebuff coding assistant can now mark a cloud project plan as ready for your approval during a planning session. This only affects you when you are setting up a blank Freebuff Cloud project and have finished discussing the product, stack, and build approach with the assistant. When the assistant finishes a planning discussion and confirms the details with you, it can now flip the project into a ready state so a Start building button appears for you to approve.

9ac3cfaccbda1e5eefac4a136587406f1bf5fe83.text: The assistant's file-ignoring logic now starts with a strict, lexical path-containment check before merging gitignore rules. The audience is the Freebuff engineering team, since this is a core refactor in the shared project-file-tree utilities. In daily use, you should not notice any difference, since the behavior change is internal and no user-facing feature is altered.

This only touches how ad requests are tagged for targeting and fraud checks, not what you see or how you use the assistant. No action is needed from you and you should not notice any difference in daily use.

1328a3f288ed36e8ee37a3aac1b8ca1efff52cd6.text: Engineers pulled the two most commonly referenced AI model names out of the big shared configuration file and put them into a tiny, standalone file that any part of the app, including the desktop version, can read without loading all the heavy server-side setup. Only the Freebuff engineering team sees any effect, since this is an internal housekeeping move. You, as a user, will not notice anything change in your daily use of the assistant.

94f0f052111d7430d1cc973c9653333d045e5f6d.text: The assistant now sends picture messages only to models that can actually read them. The free MiMo 2.5 model can still view images, but the paid MiMo 2.5 Pro version cannot, so images are no longer forwarded to it, which prevents upload failures. The list of picture-friendly models is now generated automatically from the model catalog instead of being kept by hand, so it stays accurate when new models are added or removed. This change is live today for anyone using the assistant through the terminal app, browser, or desktop app, and there is nothing you need to change; if you pick the MiMo 2.5 Pro model, you will just have to describe images in words instead of sending them directly.

5b05edcad1c49dbfae18bb40a3a8026b8b5673c6.text: If you keep using Freebuff every day for a week or more, you now get an extra premium coding session every single day, instead of just once on the exact day you hit a multiple of seven. Full-access users on a seven-day-or-longer streak also earn one GLM 5.2 session each week, and that weekly GLM allotment refreshes every Monday while your streak stays alive. The assistant interface now shows a short note explaining this perk only when your streak has reached seven days and the GLM reward is actually enabled, so it never advertises something you can't receive. The perk turns off the moment your daily streak breaks. This is live today for active Freebuff users.

ef2019f26ece398825b6dbe8451e9b5aec3be563.text: If you run out of the free daily budget that pays for the models running your coding sessions, starting a new session now quietly stops instead of crashing your terminal, and a small message appears asking you to come back once the daily reset finishes. The new screen reuses the same plain countdown that already appears for rate-limited sessions, so it reads “in ~2h 30m” instead of leaving you at a blank prompt. Only fresh session starts are blocked, so a chat already running keeps going until you close it. Live today for anyone on the Freebuff free tier whose new session request hits that provider spend cap.

191fd58e6fbdcd4f428da59d556490c152d2361f.text: When the assistant's conversation gets too long and it has to shrink it down to keep working, it now quietly sends a summary of that cleanup to Freebuff's internal diagnostics system (Axiom). This summary includes things like how much it cut, which parts it kept, and whether it had to drop your latest message, but it no longer shows up in the product analytics tool (PostHog) that tracks general usage. This is purely an internal change for the Freebuff engineering team to monitor how well the conversation shrinking works; you won't notice any difference in how the assistant behaves or performs your coding tasks today.

7dbf452bebddc6dd0ea8d46809d425a182a44753.text: Freebuff removed an experimental AI coding model called KAT Coder Pro V2 from its systems, deleting all references to it including its agent, web lists, and validation entries. This is an internal cleanup for the Freebuff engineering team, not something you as a user would see or need to act on. Since the model was experimental and never shown in the default free model list, there's no change to your daily experience or any model you can pick.

9ef7e7f28943c8ab971309b595bafd08d00d7b3a.text: The release process for installing the coding assistant on your computer has been rebuilt. Instead of downloading the program directly into the place it runs from (which could leave a broken program if the download was interrupted), it now downloads to a temporary holding spot first and is only swapped in once the whole thing is verified complete. If anything goes wrong during that swap-in, your old, working program is automatically put back. This affects anyone installing or updating the assistant through the package manager. You should see fewer failed or partially installed copies of the assistant, and when a download is interrupted it will resume where it left off instead of starting over; if it does fail, a clearer message tells you what happened and what to retry.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff 1.0.685 updates the free AI model lineup and how daily session limits work, retires some older models, and fixes error recovery when connections drop. DeepSeek V4 Flash (07/31) is now the recommended default model and GPT-5.6 Luna was added to the free picker, while MiniMax M3 and Kimi K2.7 Code were retired or demoted. Daily free sessions for both full and limited tiers grew from 5 to 6, the GLM 5.2 referral reward became a daily reset (capped at 4) instead of weekly, and the streak bonus now adds a weekly extra GLM session when your streak reaches 7 days. When a network connection interrupts an AI response, the client now detects the silent ending and retries automatically instead of stopping mid-answer. The model picker also shows a new badge and note when your previously selected model is no longer recommended, nudging you toward the updated default.

a793b16ecd43ca8d61e002222b2c9f8f8614880b.text: The referral/reward banner now renders inside the model picker's scrollable area instead of taking up fixed space above it, and the old shared focus-state helper that coordinated keyboard navigation between the two has been removed in favor of local coordination handled directly by the picker. It affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who are on the free tier and see the referral banner on the model-selection screen. In daily use you may notice the model list scrolls as one combined block (models plus your referral reward card) and that arrow-key navigation flows smoothly from the model rows into the banner's buttons without the layout jumping or the banner being clipped on narrow or short terminals. It is live today.

75c94becef9f223a3266bab4840d4594ae3e8fe8.text: Ads in streamed responses now wait two nodes before the first placement, then space subsequent ads every three nodes, up from every two. This affects advertisers buying placements in Freebuff interfaces, not Freebuff users' coding sessions. You notice nothing in daily use: this is an internal ad interspersion change with no visible effect on how the assistant responds or how many ads appear overall.

908988675e48fa01e64a50b5f9ac2410d06900dd.text: The assistant's internal helper that tidies up long conversations has been improved so it better hides behind-the-scenes work that isn't useful to see. When you're using the assistant in your terminal, it sometimes quietly brings in little helper tools behind the scenes to do things like clean up before responding to you; this change makes sure those moments no longer appear as empty, confusing gaps in your conversation history that might linger on screen. Anyone using the Freebuff assistant in the terminal will notice their chat stays cleaner and less cluttered, especially after restarting the program, without having to do anything themselves.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release updates the Freebuff AI coding assistant with several model and usability changes. A new Flash-dated version of the DeepSeek V4 model is introduced as the recommended default, while other models like MiniMax M3 and GPT-5.6 Luna are reorganized or retired from the free tier. The landing screen now shows weekly session usage instead of daily, and the referral system switched from a weekly to a daily reset for GLM 5.2 reward sessions. The model picker interface was redesigned for better layout stability when the access tier loads, and saved model preferences are now automatically migrated on every startup if your pick has been superseded. The CLI also now stops silently reverting a deliberate model choice by reclaiming a locked session, and it displays an IP-capped message when too many users share one connection. Additionally, the installer was changed to download binaries on first launch with rollback safety, and various telemetry and desktop lifecycle tracking events were added to aid debugging.

383fb0ceededb4056d40b1f6db984a321b7feb21.text: The assistant now shows your free-coding streak (days you've used it) next to the title at the top of the welcome screen, using simple bullet and dot symbols that display correctly in any terminal font. If your streak is long or your terminal window is narrow, the streak moves to its own line below the title so it never squishes against the title text. If you have no streak yet, that space stays blank until you earn your first day, and the layout no longer shifts around when you do. This only affects the Freebuff CLI landing screen; Freebuff Desktop keeps its original symbols and no action is required from you.

e78563f1e523d46e46a3234eeb84bb3e77cb9b4b.text: The CLI no longer tears down and rebuilds the entire chat interface every time you switch between conversations or open chat history; instead, it now resets only the active conversation session while keeping the surrounding chat state intact. This is an internal change for Freebuff engineering maintainers (the diff contains no user-facing features, only a refactor of how chat state is scoped and shared). You should notice no difference in daily use today - the chat still loads, streams, and switches conversations the same way it did before.

464115e810f97affdcebc6f7e5485d3664c6956c.text: When you start a new chat or go back to an old one, the assistant now stops any work it was still doing in the previous conversation first. Previously, background saves from the old chat could accidentally overwrite or bleed into the new conversation's transcript, potentially corrupting or hiding history. This affects everyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app when switching between chats. In daily use, you may not notice anything different, but your chat history will now be cleaner and less likely to get mixed up or lost when you rapidly switch conversations.

10fb028c168f112636f95dc76cc992a67819940e.text: When you ask the assistant to read multiple files at once, it now shares a single budget across all of them rather than giving each file its own allowance. The combined text it pulls back is capped at 100,000 characters and roughly 20,000 tokens, and if a file or the whole batch hits that ceiling, the excess is cut off with a plain note telling you what happened. This applies to anyone using the Freebuff assistant or SDK to read files through their tools. You will not see a new feature, only more predictable trimming when a read request is large, so smaller reads behave exactly as before.

739b605e24c6307c71c81c8323b3f38563a76ec1.text: The assistant's helper agents now use the finalized, stable version of Google's lightweight Gemini model instead of the earlier test version. If you use the free tier of Freebuff (or build custom agents with the SDK), you might not notice any difference in how these helpers behave today. This is an internal update that keeps the model references consistent, and it does not require any action from you.

8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.text: The Freebuff CLI build system was changed to install the OpenTUI native terminal interface in a safer, more reliable way. Instead of fetching it directly during the build, it now prepares the package in a temporary staging area first, checks that all required files are intact using a checksum receipt, and only then swaps it into place atomically - so an interrupted or partial install no longer leaves the CLI in a broken state. Who it affects: Freebuff maintainers who build and release the CLI binary (internal engineering team). Everyday impact: You as an end user should notice nothing directly, but the build process that produces your CLI download is now more robust and less likely to fail or produce a corrupted install if something goes wrong mid-build.

33192e18252182b6f101ffe9191d2da5fb230c57.text: The AI coding assistant that powers Freebuff has upgraded the Kimi model it offers from version 2.6 to a newer, faster-coding version called 2.7 Code. This affects you if you use or pick the Kimi model when coding with Freebuff in your terminal or browser. You will see the model listed as a different name and it should start more reliably, since the old version could stall on its very first response.

c4c5dcd66aaa42cd023a0ad0c146feacf180ebc9.text: If you keep using Freebuff every day for at least a week and your streak stays at seven days or more, you now get a bonus session every single day you keep it up, instead of only on the 7th, 14th, 21st and so on. The weekly model session is still handed out only once per week, on those milestone days. This applies to anyone using the free Freebuff assistant on a computer or the web, and what you'll notice is that your daily session credit now refreshes each day while your streak is seven or higher.

a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.title: Add Strong subscription backend with Stripe webhooks and DB migrations
a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.summary: This adds a subscription billing backend spanning packages/billing, web Stripe API routes, the internal DB layer, and the operator env schema. The new common/src/constants/subscription-plans.ts file defines SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS (100, 200, 500), DEFAULT_TIER as SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS[200], and SUBSCRIPTION_DISPLAY_NAME = 'Strong', while packages/billing/src/subscription.ts implements block-grant creation, weekly usage windows, rate limiting, and credit migration via handleSubscribe. packages/billing/src/subscription-webhooks.ts wires Stripe invoice and subscription events to handleSubscriptionInvoicePaid, handleSubscriptionInvoicePaymentFailed, handleSubscriptionUpdated, and handleSubscriptionDeleted, using createSubscriptionPriceMappings against STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_100_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_200_PRICE_ID, and STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_500_PRICE_ID to resolve the tier.
a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.evidence: New files packages/billing/src/subscription.ts and packages/billing/src/subscription-webhooks.ts define tier logic and Stripe webhook handlers; common/src/constants/subscription-plans.ts defines SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS with tiers 100, 200, 500 and DEFAULT_TIER as SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS[200]; migrations 0036_handy_silver_sable.sql, 0037_many_millenium_guard.sql, and 0038_legal_jimmy_woo.sql (referenced by meta/0036_snapshot.json, 0037_snapshot.json, 0038_snapshot.json) create the subscription, limit_override, and subscription_status enum tables plus tier and scheduled_tier columns.
a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.migration: If you run the Freebuff service, you must set STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_100_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_200_PRICE_ID, and STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_500_PRICE_ID and apply migrations 0036, 0037, and 0038 before Stripe webhooks can be processed.
a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that invokes handleSubscribe on first payment or whether the web routes are wired behind the Freebuff product surface rather than Codebuff.

changes.what: Added subscription block-grant engine, limit resolution, weekly usage tracking, rate limiting, credit migration, and Stripe webhook handlers; exported them from the billing package index.
Added tier plan constants, the SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS table keyed by price 100/200/500, DEFAULT_TIER, and a 'subscription' entry to GRANT_PRIORITIES and GrantType to support subscription-credit grants.

Added STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_*_PRICE_ID vars to the operator env schema, created the subscription_status enum, subscription and limit_override tables, tier and scheduled_tier columns, and a stripe_subscription_id column plus index on credit_ledger.
Added Stripe subscription create, change-tier, cancel, and user subscription status routes, and wired invoice/subscription webhooks to separate organization and user subscription handlers.
Added a 'subscription' grant type to the usage display breakdown so subscription credits render with a teal Zap icon alongside free, referral, purchase, admin, and ad credits.

e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.title: SDK adds session state clone helper for checkpoint snapshots
e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.summary: The SDK added cloneSessionState, a helper that copies SessionState for checkpoint and cancellation snapshots. It JSON round-trips mainAgentState instead of running the expensive lodash cloneDeep over the whole session, falling back to cloneDeep only if JSON stringify throws. The cancellation handler in run-once now calls this helper and appends an interruption message to the copy without disturbing the live session.
e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.evidence: sdk/src/run.ts adds exported function cloneSessionState(state, logger) and a try/catch block that JSON.round-trips state.mainAgentState, falling back to cloneDeep on failure; getCancelledSessionState now calls cloneSessionState(sessionState, logger) instead of cloneDeep(sessionState).
e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

d0de3f5b1cbd70534b9d6c36f0dfc9c77ae8f92b.title: Cloud connect repo analytics event and experimental model badge field
d0de3f5b1cbd70534b9d6c36f0dfc9c77ae8f92b.summary: The AnalyticsEvent enum in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts gains FREEBUFF_CLOUD_CONNECT_REPO_CLICKED, which fires when a logged-out visitor clicks a Continue with GitHub or Connect your repo CTA on the Freebuff /cloud landing page and carries a location property to distinguish hero, migration/lovable, and final CTA clicks. Separately, common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds an experimental?: boolean field to the FreebuffModelOption interface and sets experimental: true on the HY3, HY3 Atlas, and KAT Coder Pro V2 model option objects, marking them with a TEST badge in the picker so users know they are still being trialed.

bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.title: SDK terminal command detaches on all platforms
bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.summary: The `spawn` call in `runTerminalCommand` now sets detached: true unconditionally, replacing the previous `detached: !isWindows`. The updated comment states that on POSIX a negative pid kills the process group and that on Windows detached: true maps to `DETACHED_PROCESS`, which with `windowsHide` fully detaches the child from the parent's console.
bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.evidence: In `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`, the `spawn` options block changes `detached: !isWindows` to detached: true and rewrites the adjacent comment to describe a process group on POSIX using a negative pid kill and detached: true mapping to `DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows. The `killProcessGroup` helper and `liveChildren`/`installExitSweep` exit sweep logic are unchanged in the hunk.

9e48fc62b994946fb6f5412439bc458c0c222904.title: KAT Coder Pro V2 added as Freebuff Web premium model
9e48fc62b994946fb6f5412439bc458c0c222904.summary: KAT Coder Pro V2 (kwaipilot/kat-coder-pro-v2) is introduced as a Web-only premium model option, registered through the `openrouter_kwaipilot_kat_coder_pro_v2` provider entry, gated behind `FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS` and `FREEBUFF_WEB_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS`, with test assertions confirming it is treated as a premium Web test model.

0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.title: Intersperse inline ads within assistant responses instead of anchoring
0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.summary: Replaced the legacy single-ad-per-anchor placement model (`placedAds`, `InlineAdBanner`, `computeInlineAdAdditions`, `isCompletedAnswer`) with a per-prompt batch model: `useGravityAd` now auctions `ADS_PER_PROMPT` ads per genuine user prompt and computes `responseAds` keyed by assistant message id via `computeResponseAds`. `blocks-renderer.tsx` reads `responseAds` from `useMessageBlockStore` and intersperses `AdCard` nodes between rendered response nodes using `responseAdNodePositions`, which places an ad after every `RESPONSE_AD_NODE_STEP` node only when a following node exists, so short responses show fewer ads. `chat.tsx` passes `responseAds` into the message-block context and routes ad click/impression callbacks through `handleAdClick`/`handleAdImpression`, while the rotating above-input `SingleAdBanner` now auctions separately via `slotPlacementId` for reporting continuity.
0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.evidence: Commit 0a6df576 adds `cli/src/utils/response-ad-positions.ts` (defining `RESPONSE_AD_NODE_STEP` and `responseAdNodePositions`) and replaces the prior `placedAds`/`InlineAdBanner`/`computeInlineAdAdditions`/`isCompletedAnswer`/`AdPacing`/`inlineAdAnchorIds` exports in `use-gravity-ad.ts`, now exposing `responseAds` keyed by assistant message id computed via `computeResponseAds` from messages and `PromptAdBatch[]`; `blocks-renderer.tsx` reads `state.context.responseAds[messageId]` from `useMessageBlockStore` and intersperses `AdCard` nodes between render via `responseAdNodePositions`
0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.migration: Because the inline ad placement API changed, any custom ad-rendering component that consumed the removed `placedAds`, `PlaceAd`, `isCompletedAnswer`, `AdPacing`, `inlineAdAnchorIds`, or `computeInlineAdAdditions` exports must migrate to reading `responseAds` keyed by message id and interspersing `AdCard` nodes via `responseAdNodePositions`.

f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.title: Freebuff runner package removed
f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.summary: The `@codebuff/freebuff-runner` package at `freebuff/runner/` has been fully deleted, removing the Render-hosted Bun worker that offloaded Freebuff agent turns from Convex action compute. This eliminates the long-lived runner process (`src/main.ts`), the HTTP/WS `RunnerCtx` bridge (`src/convexBridge.ts`), the batched event flush (`src/eventBatcher.ts`), the Codex/Claude Code executors, the ported harness logic, and structured logging glue. Dispatch therefore reverts to the legacy Convex action and workflow paths; the `freebuff_runner_enabled` flag and the `runner_bridge` Convex helpers it depended on are no longer consumed by any runner-side code here, and the README's deploy-order warning about bringing the Render worker up before flipping the flag no longer applies.
f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.evidence: The diff deletes the entire `freebuff/runner/` package directory: `freebuff/runner/README.md`, `freebuff/runner/package.json`, `freebuff/runner/tsconfig.json`, and every source file under `freebuff/runner/src/` (`main.ts`, `convexBridge.ts`, `eventBatcher.ts`, `executeClaudeCode.ts`, `executeCodex.ts`, `harness.ts`, `logger.ts`, `runCliTurn.ts`, `runTurn.ts`, `webcontainerTools.ts`). The analysis notes confirm the package was added in an earlier commit [f7828c2c] and structured facts list the exports removed (`RunnerCtx`, `createRunnerCtx`, `createSubscriptionClient`, `createEventBatcher`, etc.).
f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.unknowns: Whether the `freebuff_runner_enabled` flag is also flipped back off and the `runner_bridge` Convex helpers are deleted in adjacent commits, and whether the sweep cron and requeue behavior the README described are being cleaned up elsewhere.

changes.what: Removed the entire `freebuff/runner/` package, including its manifest, tsconfig, and all source modules.

07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.title: Freebuff Runner adds structured logger and logging wiring
07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.summary: The Freebuff Runner (@codebuff/freebuff-runner, the Bun worker that claims queued freebuff_agent_runs from Convex and runs the codebuff SDK harness in-process) gains a structured logger via a new freebuff/runner/src/logger.ts that builds @codebuff/common LogRow payloads tagged service=freebuff-runner and re-exports flushLogSink from @codebuff/logging. package.json adds the @codebuff/logging workspace dependency and main.ts sets FREEBUFF_RUNNER_ID and calls flushLogSink on graceful shutdown; every console.log/warn/error call in main.ts, eventBatcher.ts, and runTurn.ts is replaced with logger.info/warn/error calls that include runId context. The eventBatcher and runTurn modules now route flush, heartbeat, and error diagnostics through the logger instead of raw console output, so runner lifecycle and crash logs ship into the unified freebuff dataset.
07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.evidence: New file freebuff/runner/src/logger.ts defines LOG_SERVICE = 'freebuff-runner', re-exports flushLogSink from @codebuff/logging, and builds LogRow payloads; freebuff/runner/package.json adds "@codebuff/logging": "workspace:*"; main.ts sets process.env.FREEBUFF_RUNNER_ID = RUNNER_ID and calls flushLogSink on shutdown; eventBatcher.ts and runTurn.ts import { logger } from './logger' and replace console.log/warn/error calls with logger.info/warn/error.

4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.title: Add HY3 model constants and Freebuff Web-only model sets
4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.summary: Adds HY3_MODEL and HY3_ATLAS_MODEL option objects plus the constants FREEBUFF_HY3_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_HY3_ATLAS_MODEL_ID and FREEBUFF_HY3_OPENROUTER_FREE_MODEL_ID in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, and wires the matching model-config.ts identifiers openrouter_tencent_hy3_free and atlasCloudModels.tencentHy3 into the provider catalogs and the 'tencent' allowlist so the new ids resolve to real provider entries. Exports the Web-only picker sets FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_GOD_ONLY_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_ALL_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS and their id variants so Freebuff Web can surface HY3 while CLI/Desktop surfaces keep it out, because HY3 is intentionally excluded from FREEBUFF_MODELS and SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS during the initial web rollout. The detail: FREEBUFF_HY3_MODEL_ID equals FREEBUFF_HY3_OPENROUTER_FREE_MODEL_ID, so the free id is reused as the canonical HY3 id within the Web set.
4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts adds the HY3_MODEL and HY3_ATLAS_MODEL option objects and the constants FREEBUFF_HY3_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_HY3_ATLAS_MODEL_ID, FREEBUFF_HY3_OPENROUTER_FREE_MODEL_ID, plus the Web-only export sets FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_GOD_ONLY_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_ALL_MODELS, FREEBUFF_WEB_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS and the predicate/resolver exports isFreebuffWebModelId, isFreebuffWebGodOnlyModelId, resolveFreebuffWebModel, isFreebuffWebPremiumModelId, isFreebuffWebMultimodalModelId, FreebuffWebModelId and FreebuffWebPremiumModelId; model-config.ts adds openrouter_tencent_hy3_free, atlasCloudModels.tencentHy3 and the 'tencent' entry to ALLOWED_MODEL_PREFIXES.

2f0296cf9937bb0bc0256849868e81c193f0f472.text: The Freebuff CLI's inline response ads now appear more frequently within assistant answers. What changed: ads intersperse after every second rendered section (previously every fourth), and they're served from a small, lazily-filled pool of four ads that get reused for longer conversations, instead of fetching a fresh batch of eight on every turn. Who it affects: Freebuff CLI users on the free tier, as well as Codebuff users with ads enabled (subscribers see no ads). Everyday impact: you may notice more inline ads appearing throughout longer conversations, presented in a more compact one-line format.

e1ce92184215843f83e268d758011594a4a0c8a5.text: The SDK now makes a faster, safer copy of the current session when saving checkpoints while a run is in progress. This makes the periodic 'snapshot' saves that guard against losing work if your terminal closes or crashes noticeably smoother on larger sessions. It only affects code that uses the Freebuff SDK to embed the assistant, so there is no visible change for people using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app. No action is needed from you.

bd3b19ed76cf17a16e45df2e329ee5e84b7b6883.text: The terminal command runner now starts every command fully detached from the parent process on both Mac/Linux and Windows, where it previously only did so on Mac/Linux. Developers who embed the SDK can now rely on timeouts and aborts cleaning up the whole command tree, including any extra programs the command spawned, instead of leaving stuck background work behind. You will not see this in the app today, but if you drive Codebuff from your own scripts or tools, your kill switches behave the same way on every operating system now.

ea226cb387463c614ad636bf2fa368cca721099c.text: The assistant's built-in research tool, which pulls up-to-date documentation from Context7 for libraries like React or MongoDB, has been upgraded to use Context7's newer v2 API endpoint. This endpoint uses a different URL path structure that the assistant now routes searches through a dedicated /libs/search path with the library name and topic as parameters. The tool also now enforces stricter input checks, requiring non-empty library names and topics (which get stripped of extra spaces), and the default amount of documentation returned has been lowered from 20,000 tokens to 10,000, with any extra content trimmed locally by the assistant itself rather than requested from the server.

d0de3f5b1cbd70534b9d6c36f0dfc9c77ae8f92b.text: The Freebuff team added tracking so that when someone who is not signed in clicks a button on the cloud sign-up page to connect their code repository, that click is now recorded. They also added a way to mark certain experimental AI models in the model picker, and they applied that mark to the HY3, HY3 Atlas and KAT Coder Pro V2 models, which users will now see labeled as a test version when choosing a model. These changes are live today and affect anyone using the web version of Freebuff to pick a model, as well as the company's internal analytics. Users do not need to do anything. The cloud click tracking helps the company understand which buttons are attracting sign-ups, while the test badge warns that the marked models may be less reliable than the rest.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release updates Freebuff's CLI with better session handling, new model options, and protections for when free quotas fill up. When your daily free limit is reached, the landing screen now explains the limit and shows a countdown to when you can try again, instead of looping or failing silently. The model picker now defaults to DeepSeek V4 Pro, nudges you toward DeepSeek V4 Flash, and stops offering retired models like Kimi K2.7 Code and KAT Coder Pro V2. Stream recovery now retries interrupted AI responses instead of cutting off mid-sentence, and context pruning now preserves recent messages more fairly. These changes mean fewer stuck sessions, clearer messaging when limits hit, and better handling of model switches and network interruptions.

4afa065433a1f7c99574755052324ab24fc7bd1c.text: A new AI model called HY3 has been added to the list of models you can choose from when using Freebuff on the web, making it available both as a free option and as a premium 'god-only' option through a different provider. This change only affects Freebuff Web users - the command-line and desktop versions of Freebuff do not get access to HY3 during this initial rollout. If you use freebuff.com in your browser, you might now see HY3 as an option in the model picker when starting a new session. The premium HY3 Atlas variant is currently restricted to select users only.

f0d966458519ffa59de0fbce27fad27f0ac7a047.text: Freebuff removed a small, separate worker program it had added the same day to run Freebuff coding sessions; that worker never became the main way sessions run, so Freebuff is now dispatching coding sessions the same way it did before, through its standard internal pathways. The change is for maintainers only; no advertiser budgets, placements, or self-serve ad limits were modified by this removal. For you, nothing changes in daily use right now, because the feature flag that would have routed sessions to the removed worker was never flipped on for anyone, so your coding sessions were never going to be handled by it in the first place.

0a6df5765585fe3da17d92272fbce28be74bc127.text: The assistant now shows up to eight small sponsor cards directly inside its answers, mixed in between the text and tool results instead of only sitting in one fixed spot above the box where you type. The cards appear only for Freebuff users, who get the free tier of the service, and they are picked based on each new prompt you send. What you will notice is a few labelled sponsor messages tucked into longer answers, with the number growing as a response gets more complex; very short answers show none at all.

d2ae8a0dc59e09d6a13717590ebdd0fd9e2b3dfa.text: The animated shimmer effect that runs across the Freebuff/Codebuff logo in your chat window now pauses automatically whenever you scroll the logo out of view, so it only animates while the header is actually visible. This change only affects the visual behavior of the chat header for developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, or desktop app. If you use Freebuff or Codebuff in a terminal or browser tab, you won't notice this beyond the logo shimmer being a bit more battery-friendly when it's scrolled out of sight.

07ab1c6445e0e36697f749f10d34eccea254b5e5.text: The team that operates the Freebuff background workers added a centralized, structured logging system to the worker that runs Freebuff agent turns, replacing scattered direct print statements across the runner's startup, run-claiming, turn execution, and shutdown paths (main.ts, eventBatcher.ts, runTurn.ts) with a single logger module (logger.ts) that emits tagged log rows and flushes them cleanly on shutdown. This is internal tooling for the Freebuff engineering team only (it lands in the freebuff/runner package, an internal Bun worker that claims queued runs off Convex), so it does not change anything you see or do in the Freebuff web app, CLI, or desktop client.

9e48fc62b994946fb6f5412439bc458c0c222904.text: A new premium AI model called KAT Coder Pro V2 was added as an option when using Freebuff from a web browser. It is only available to people signed up for the Freebuff web experience, not to those using the desktop app or command-line tool. If you use Freebuff in your browser, you will see this new model listed as a paid upgrade choice, but the default free model and your existing credits are unchanged. It is live now for web users who select premium models.

a207ad23c2e11b4963b3c78bb4b961eab5e182ca.text: The Freebuff service operators have added a new paid subscription tier called 'Strong' that connects to Stripe for recurring payments, with three price levels. Operators must now configure three new Stripe price identifiers and run three database updates before the subscription system will accept payments. For users, this prepares the ground for a new monthly billing option that will offer larger packs of compute credits and weekly usage limits, though the actual purchase flow for end users is not yet wired up and will arrive in a follow-up.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.title: Freebuff Runner package added to offload agent turns from Convex
f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.summary: The `@codebuff/freebuff-runner` Bun worker is added under `freebuff/runner/` so Freebuff, Codex, and Claude Code agent turns run off Convex action compute. It subscribes over websocket to runner-dispatched `queued` rows in `freebuff_agent_runs`, claims them with a CAS mutation, and streams batched events through `recordRunEventBatch`. Dispatch is gated by the `freebuff_runner_enabled` feature flag, which now defaults ON for those send types, with the legacy Convex action and workflow paths remaining as fallback. The event batcher ships every buffered delta in one mutation per ~2s and sends a 30000ms heartbeat to keep the run alive during long tool calls with no streamed output.

Their accompanying comments describe `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEM_FAILED` as a one-shot guard signal for redemption blockers (signup_too_old, user_banned, self_referral, etc.) and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SOCK_SIGNAL` as a non-verdict attribution signal that a referred user shares an IP/browser with the referrer, to be weighed by the referral sweep jobs against farming signals. These events extend the server-side referral lifecycle funnel documented in the same enum, but no reader in this diff emits them, so the change seeds telemetry infrastructure rather than shipping tracked behavior.
bfaad48713d14b4e948a6ad49a2c6f79d6cb250c.evidence: Added `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEM_FAILED` and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SOCK_SIGNAL` enum members to `AnalyticsEvent` in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, placing them between `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_REDEEMED` and `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_COMPLETED` with explanatory comments describing their one-shot guard and sock-signal semantics.
bfaad48713d14b4e948a6ad49a2c6f79d6cb250c.unknowns: No emitting code or consumer of the new events is present in this revision; only the enum definitions and their documentation comments.

b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.title: Merge consecutive assistant messages into one wire message
b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat message converter now merges consecutive assistant messages into a single wire message, concatenating `text`, `reasoningContent`, and `toolCalls` in order and unioning provider metadata onto the prior message via `Object.assign`. This addresses thinking models like DeepSeek V4 that require `reasoning_content` to sit on the message carrying `tool_calls`, since a separate adjacent assistant message fails the request. New tests assert merging runs of consecutive assistant messages while preserving separation when another role intervenes.
b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.evidence: In `packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts, the assistant case now checks messages[messages.length - 1]`; when `previous?.role === 'assistant', it appends text`, `reasoningContent`, and `toolCalls to that prior message and calls Object.assign(previous, metadata)` before breaking, instead of pushing a new assistant message.

454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.title: Add optional steering hook to agent runtime loop and SDK run
454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.summary: An optional steering hook (`drainSteeringMessages`) was added to the agent runtime loop and SDK run path, letting a host inject free-text messages into a running agent turn. In `loopAgentSteps`, the hook is drained at each step boundary after a step's LLM call and tools complete; returned strings are appended to `messageHistory` as `USER_PROMPT` user messages and `shouldEndTurn` is forced to false so the agent runs another step. The SDK threads the same option through `RunOptions` into `runOnce` and forwards it to `callMainPrompt`. New tests verify a message appended at the boundary keeps the turn going and that empty returns do not extend the turn.
454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.evidence: Added the optional `drainSteeringMessages?: () => string[]` parameter to `loopAgentSteps` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` (added to the params type and drained inside the main loop after each `runAgentStep`), and threaded the same option through `RunOptions` into `runOnce` then `callMainPrompt` in `sdk/src/run.ts`, where returned texts are appended to the message history as `USER_PROMPT` user messages and `shouldEndTurn` is forced to false; new tests in `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts` assert the step boundary message injection and turn continuation.
454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.unknowns: Which host (CLI or web app) currently supplies `drainSteeringMessages` to exercise the hook in practice.

changes.what: Added optional `drainSteeringMessages` parameter to `loopAgentSteps`, drained at step boundaries to append injected user messages and keep the turn going.
Exposed `drainSteeringMessages` on `RunOptions`, destructured it in `runOnce`, and forwarded it to `callMainPrompt`.
Added tests asserting steering messages are appended at the step boundary and continue the turn.

effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.title: SDK checkpoints in-flight runs and CLI persists them to survive
effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.summary: `run()` in `sdk/src/run.ts` gains an `onStateSnapshot` hook fired once at start and every `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS` (5000 ms) while in flight, yielding a `RunState` whose output carries `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE`; a `settled` guard and cleared `snapshotTimer` ensure snapshots never overwrite the final state, and an owner check stops a late snapshot from clobbering a newer run. The CLI wires that hook in `createRunConfig` and calls `saveChatState` from `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` at turn start, on each snapshot, and on error, so a killed terminal or crash keeps the last turn on disk, while `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` invokes `flushLiveChatState()` during process exit to persist any in-flight checkpoint. Supporting storage helpers in `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` (`setLiveChatStateProvider`, `clearLiveChatStateProvider`, `flushLiveChatState`, `setChatDirOverrideForTesting`) make the provider owner-guarded and best-effort, and `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts` adds `sanitizeRestoredMessages` to mark an interrupted `AI_MESSAGE_ID_PREFIX` AI response as complete with an interruption notice and cancel its running agent blocks.
effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.evidence: The diff adds an `onStateSnapshot` callback to `RunOptions` in `sdk/src/run.ts` (with `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000` and `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE` exports), threads it through `createRunConfig` in `cli/src/utils/create-run-config.ts`, and calls `saveChatState` from `useSendMessage` in `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` both at turn start and on each in-flight snapshot plus on error; `sdk/src/index.ts` now re-exports `STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE`; `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` calls `flushLiveChatState()` in `cleanup()`; `cli/src/utils/run-state-storage.ts` adds `setLiveChatStateProvider`, `clearLiveChatStateProvider`, `flushLiveChatState`, and `setChatDirOverrideForTesting`; `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts` adds `AI_MESSAGE_ID_PREFIX`, `sanitizeRestoredMessages`, and imports `appendInterruptionNotice` and `markRunningAgentsAsCancelled`.
effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.migration: If you embed the CLI or SDK and relied on `run()` never calling back with a `RunState` before completion, you must now handle the optional `onStateSnapshot` snapshots in your host persistence layer.
effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the checkpoint snapshot is consumed by any downstream autosave or sync service beyond the CLI's `saveChatState`.

changes.what: `run()` accepts `onStateSnapshot` and emits a `RunState` snapshot immediately and every 5000 ms while in flight, stopping once the run settles.
`STATE_SNAPSHOT_INTERRUPTION_MESSAGE` is now re-exported from the public SDK entry point.
`CreateRunConfigParams` and the returned config object now include `onStateSnapshot`.
Registers a live state provider, saves chat state at turn start and on each snapshot, saves the last checkpoint on error, and clears the provider in `finally`.
`cleanup()` now calls `flushLiveChatState()` first to persist any in-flight checkpoint before terminal reset.
Adds owner-guarded `setLiveChatStateProvider`/`clearLiveChatStateProvider`, best-effort `flushLiveChatState`, and a `setChatDirOverrideForTesting` escape hatch for tests.

55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.title: Referral banner shows daily bonus for limited tier and reserves rows
55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.summary: The `FreebuffReferralBanner` component in the waiting-room screen now branches on the session's `accessTier`: the LIMITED tier renders a quiet one-line daily free-session bonus (capped at `REFERRAL_CLI_DAILY_SESSION_BONUS_CAP`) with a copy-invite-link button instead of hiding the banner entirely, while the FULL tier keeps its GLM 5.2 card and launch button. The waiting room's `referralBannerRows` height budget now adds an `accessTier === 'limited'` case so the scrollbox shrinks correctly for the new branch, and both branches share the existing `flexShrink: 0` guard to prevent the bordered copy button from overlapping the line above it in height-starved landing columns. In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` the `FreebuffReferralInfo` type makes `weeklySessionsRemaining` and `resetAt` optional (documented as full-tier-only, omitted for the limited daily-bonus variant) and updates the `none` status doc comment to describe both tier-specific reward presentations.
55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-referral-banner.tsx`, the `FreebuffReferralBanner` component now gates on `accessTier`: the LIMITED branch renders the daily-session-bonus line and shares the same `flexShrink: 0` defensive layout as the FULL tier. In `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx`, `referralBannerRows` now branches on `accessTier === 'limited'` to reserve the correct row budget. In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, `FreebuffReferralInfo.weeklySessionsRemaining` and `resetAt` change from required to optional, and the `none` status doc comment now mentions the limited-tier daily-bonus variant.
55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side change that begins emitting `referral` blocks on limited-tier `none` responses, only the client handling of them. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Adds a LIMITED tier branch rendering a daily free-session bonus line plus a copy-invite-link button, sharing the existing flexShrink and focus-guard logic.
Adds an accessTier === 'limited' case to the referralBannerRows height-reservation math so the picker scrollbox accounts for the new branch.
Makes weeklySessionsRemaining and resetAt optional on FreebuffReferralInfo and redocs the none status referral field as tier-dependent.

8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.title: CLI free-tier engaged-time heartbeat via shared EngagementTracker
8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.summary: Adds a Freebuff-only engaged-time heartbeat in the CLI, reusing `./activity-tracker` as the presence signal and emitting one `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` per active minute with `surface` set to `cli` (no tab/visibility concept in a terminal, so idleness alone gates the count). The tracking lives in a new shared `EngagementTracker` in `common/src/util/engagement-tracker.ts` that fires every `ENGAGEMENT_INTERVAL_MS` (1 minute) and skips ticks where the user has been idle past `ENGAGEMENT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (5 minutes); the CLI wraps its timers with `.unref()` so the heartbeat never keeps the process alive on exit, and `exitFreebuffCleanly()` stops it before flushing analytics. `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` is added to `AnalyticsEvent` and to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` (never sampled), and `product_active_minute` is placed on the Axiom denylist so PostHog remains the system of record for this high-volume metric. This is the most user-relevant of several changes: two new modules, the engine wiring in `index.tsx`, exit cleanup in `exitFreebuffCleanly`, one new enum entry, sampling guard, and the Axiom denylist; tests cover tick/visibility/idle/idempotency behavior.
8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.evidence: New files `cli/src/utils/engagement.ts` and `common/src/util/engagement-tracker.ts`; `cli/src/index.tsx` calls `startEngagementTracking()` after renderer creation gated on `IS_FREEBUFF`; `cli/src/utils/freebuff-exit.ts` calls `stopEngagementTracking()` before flushing analytics in `exitFreebuffCleanly()`.
8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.unknowns: The diff does not show the web/desktop shell consuming `EngagementTracker` yet, even though the module doc describes browser and desktop wiring.

changes.what: CLI heartbeat that starts an `EngagementTracker` emitting `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` with `surface: 'cli'`, driven by `./activity-tracker`'s activity signal and unref'd timers.
Framework-agnostic `EngagementTracker` class plus `ENGAGEMENT_INTERVAL_MS` (60_000) and `ENGAGEMENT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` (300_000), with injectable `emit`, clock, and scheduler for tests.
Imports and calls `startEngagementTracking()` only when `IS_FREEBUFF` is true, after `createCliRenderer` and before rendering the app.
Calls `stopEngagementTracking()` at the start of `exitFreebuffCleanly()` so no engaged-minute fires mid-teardown before analytics flush.
Adds the `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` enum entry with documentation tying it to per-minute event counting and the `engagement-tracker` module.
Adds `AnalyticsEvent.PRODUCT_ACTIVE_MINUTE` to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` so engaged-time minutes are never sampled.

ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.title: Referral banner now links to /get-started with referrer name
ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.summary: The referral share link now points at the /get-started CLI install walkthrough instead of the bare landing page, passing the inviter's display name as an optional ?referrer= query parameter so the page can greet the friend with "X invited you to try Freebuff!", per the referrerName field newly added to FreebuffReferralInfo. freebuff-referral-banner.tsx introduces a CopyInviteLinkButton that wraps copyTextToClipboard and flips to a 'Copied!' confirmation for COPIED_RESET_DELAY_MS milliseconds, replacing the previous CopyButton usage. The FreebuffReferralBanner is also reordered to render after the streak line in the waiting-room landing layout, keeping it visually anchored to the model picker.
ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.evidence: In cli/src/components/freebuff-referral-banner.tsx, referralLink now takes a referrerName argument and builds a /get-started link with ?ref= and optional ?referrer=, and a new CopyInviteLinkButton component replaces CopyButton for clipboard feedback. In common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts, FreebuffReferralInfo gains a referrerName: string | null field. In cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx, the FreebuffReferralBanner render slot is moved to the bottom of the landing picker column
ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.migration: No action required; existing referral links continue to work and the new referrer personalization is applied automatically.

changes.what: Reworked referral link generation and clipboard button to target /get-started with an optional referrer name parameter, adding a CopyInviteLinkButton with copied-state feedback.
Added referrerName: string | null to FreebuffReferralInfo, sourced from user.name, for landing-page personalization.
Moved the FreebuffReferralBanner render slot below the streak row in the landing picker column.

99f8bdf7238772049723aee6d133b9e2af05e10c.text: When you ask the Freebuff Chat bot to recommend a third-party service like a database, email provider, or payment API, it now resolves tracked setup links (the exact signup/credential URLs) before showing them to you, rather than risking a wrong or guessed URL. This affects users interacting with the Freebuff Chat web interface and the CLI's UI rendering, ensuring the links you click to create accounts or get API keys are verified and accurate. You'll experience more reliable "Get your X API key" buttons that point to the correct tracked signup page instead of potentially incorrect fallback URLs.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: Version 1.0.683 adds a /copy command that exports your full chat to the clipboard, adds referral streak rewards that grant bonus sessions for 7-day login milestones, and lowers the unified referral GitHub account-age requirement to 4 months so more users qualify. The free model picker now lists MiniMax M3 first, a new GLM 5.2 referral reward model is served through a dedicated weekly session pool, and the CLI waiting room shows a reset countdown for premium sessions even at zero usage. Desktop users get a one-per-user concurrency cap on premium models, multi-session headers sync server and client tabs, and nine new desktop analytics events are tracked at 100 percent sampling. You also get keyboard navigation that extends into the referral banner, a persistent anonymous analytics ID that aliases cleanly into your account on login, and Windows AVX2 detection cached on disk to speed up launches.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff CLI release adds GPT-5.6 Luna to the free model picker, retires Kimi K2.7 Code from free mode, and moves MiniMax M3 into the daily premium pool so it now draws from a shared 5-per-day limit. The landing screen now shows a weekly-based session counter that adapts its wording and layout to your terminal size, and deliberately picking a model after a model_lock error now reclaims a clean session instead of silently reverting. Stream recovery now yields tagged error chunks and auto-retries interrupted model output up to three times, while the read-files tool enforces a combined 100,000-character and 20,000-token budget across all files in one call. Upgrading gives you a newer free model to choose from, clearer feedback when you hit daily limits or IP sharing caps, and fewer dropped conversations when a model stream is cut mid-response.

f7828c2c4b5a55de46b00f0484ed047e091d0964.text: Freebuff added a separate, always-on worker service that now handles running the AI agents behind the scenes instead of relying on the built-in code-execution capacity tied to the main app. This is an internal infrastructure change for whoever operates the Freebuff service, so it doesn't change any features you use directly today, though it should make agent runs more reliable and resilient if a single worker needs to restart. The new worker is live behind the scenes, but only matters to the people who keep the Freebuff platform running.

c59bde7fe2f90f0e25b0ce36a1d8856ec8ccfa5f.text: Ads now appear directly inside your chat scroll, pinned right after every second completed assistant reply, instead of only one rotating ad sitting at the very bottom of the screen. This affects Freebuff (the free tier of the Codebuff coding assistant) users on desktop and web, and anyone in the CLI who isn't on a paid subscription plan. If you use the free assistant today, you will start seeing these inline, scrollback-anchored ad cards appear between your and the assistant's messages as you work, and they remain in place as you scroll up and down.

3d1a8e68f275183a92cfbb5100a2528bd5ce4c79.text: When the assistant's terminal interface crashes hard - killed by a force-quit command or a system crash that cuts it off without letting it shut down properly - it can leave your terminal in a messy state where things like keyboard shortcuts or screen layout stop behaving normally. To fix this, the CLI now launches a tiny, hidden helper process at startup that quietly watches the main program and, if that sudden crash happens, automatically sends commands to restore your terminal to a clean state. This helper runs on Linux and macOS (the Mac always had a fallback, but now there are three layers of protection), and it stays ready in the background only while you're using the assistant, meaning you are less likely to find a stuck or broken terminal after an unexpected crash.

7f595c4c0634c855c18f0cfb325c173392e3bd61.text: The assistant no longer shows a "waiting room" screen when you start it up, replacing that old language with a message that says your free session is still being set up if there is a brief race condition during admission. This is an internal change to how the CLI boots and how the automated tests check that it launched correctly, so it only affects Freebuff engineering, not end users directly. You will not notice anything different in daily use because the waiting-room state the change removes was already no longer a real boot screen the CLI renders; the update just cleans up the old wording and test signals so the code and tests match what the assistant actually does today.

4f5a72d6b85c9521b28248e359c11719cf6d55c4.text: The engineering team added a single, shared set of helpers that every part of the system uses to turn messy log details (including ones with loops) into clean, size-limited text before sending them to the logging backend. This is internal maintenance only, so it does not change what you see or do in the Freebuff assistant. The same change also updated a design note for the analytics event that tracks daily usage, adding the Cloud interface as another place messages get counted and listing where that count happens across the apps. No action is needed from you, and nothing you currently experience is affected.

671c093077dc5cd74ab2b1892c7c134d84c8fbd8.text: Freebuff now saves a tiny summary file (a few hundred bytes) next to each saved chat transcript instead of forcing the app to open and parse the full transcript every time it needs to display your chat history list. When you open the chat history screen, Freebuff reads these summaries first for speed, and only opens the full transcript if the summary is missing, corrupted, or out of date. Your full chat history is still stored in full, so nothing is lost. This makes the chat history list load faster, especially for long conversations. This is live today for everyone using the Freebuff CLI.

a07d73d1f0bdd5f9c47d64423d3837d59bcb2309.text: The SDK now checks which server address to use at the moment it is needed, rather than fixing it once when the code is packaged. This matters to teams that embed the SDK inside their own server-side code or cloud functions, where a development machine address baked in at packaging time would be unreachable at runtime. These teams can override the address using environment variables on their deployment, so the SDK connects to the correct backend without rebuilding it. If you simply install or use the CLI, you will not notice anything change.

77cfee986c1b3e6fd7fffc5b37bb7c4028a30446.text: The assistant's tools now all listen for a single cancellation signal, so when you or the program stops a task, every running helper (the terminal, the web fetch, and the code search) shuts down together instead of some of them lingering and freezing. Developers who build their own apps on top of the Freebuff assistant can now stop a busy action mid-way, and everything they started stops cleanly without leaving background work behind. If you interrupt the assistant while it is running something, it will stop faster and no longer keep doing hidden work after you stop it. This is already live for anyone using the tools that run in their app or script.

effaebabd70b475f18cd90481cc6cbc88c5ff9e3.text: When you ask the assistant a question and something goes wrong before it finishes replying (like closing the terminal, your computer crashing, or the app freezing), the assistant used to lose everything you asked plus any partial work it had started. Now, while the assistant is still working on your request, it quietly saves your question and whatever progress it has made to your computer every few seconds. So if that happens mid-way through, reopening the app brings the conversation back as-is, with a note that the response was cut off, instead of disappearing entirely. You do not need to turn this on, and there is nothing new to configure or pay extra for. This only affects the Freebuff and Codebuff command-line tools.

b10e9ab1644601375492fa771f2acd2088b27429.text: The app now combines multiple assistant replies into a single message before sending it to the AI model, so models like DeepSeek V4 can correctly replay their internal reasoning alongside tool calls. This matters for you if you use the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK, because it fixes a bug that could cause requests to the model to be rejected. You will not see anything new in the interface, but the assistant is less likely to hit a wall mid-task when working with models that rely on thinking steps.

b88380a4c48c5a1dfe12d788f62d794c5df7db57.text: The app now saves your chat conversations in a safer way, so if the app crashes or closes unexpectedly while saving, your conversation won't be lost or hidden from the chat history list anymore. This change affects Freebuff CLI users who rely on saved chats being available after a crash, and in everyday use, you'll no longer see chats mysteriously disappear from your history due to corrupted files. Starting a new chat now always creates a fresh folder for the new conversation instead of risking overwriting the previous one.

d304465cf1503c0d27dc79e6ffaf252657fe922c.text: Freebuff's engineering team added two new tracking labels that let their analytics system tell when a sponsored ad shown in the Freebuff desktop app is displayed to a user and when that user clicks on it. These labels are purely internal bookkeeping the same way the team already tracks ad views and clicks elsewhere; they affect no one's ad experience or account. You will not notice anything different in the app today, and there is no action for you to take. This is a minor step behind the scenes to keep ad tracking consistent across Freebuff's desktop surface.

454dcd2c72790576154d4ed6cc68d96bf47dad96.text: Freebuff's coding assistant can now accept guidance while it's working, without stopping what it's doing. When a developer uses the SDK to run an agent, they can now optionally provide a way to feed in messages that get delivered at natural pause points between the agent's thinking steps, letting the assistant respond to new directions immediately instead of waiting until its current task finishes. For teams building on the SDK, this means they can steer a running agent in real-time. If no messages are fed in, nothing changes. This arrives today.

55f61ffc60b73ecdfb31f8d649e85e4ff3086c0b.text: The invite-friends message that used to appear only for paid-tier users now also shows up for free-tier users, but in a quieter way. Instead of advertising the premium GLM 5.2 model, it tells you that referring friends can earn you extra free coding sessions per day, and it shows your progress toward a daily cap. If you're on the free tier and you refer a friend today, you'll see a small line with a 'Copy invite link' button rather than a flashy reward card. The screen layout was also adjusted so this new line doesn't overlap or squeeze other text when your terminal window is short.

8a96d48d79d02c951416f047ba4d2b269407b584.text: The Freebuff CLI now sends a gentle, minute-by-minute heartbeat that quietly records how long free-tier users stay actively engaged in the terminal, but only while they're actually interacting with it and not idle, and it turns off the moment you close the app to avoid interfering with shutdown. This is live today for free-tier users of the Freebuff CLI, desktop, or web app, and you won't see or feel it - it's invisible background plumbing that helps the team understand engagement patterns, with no action needed from you.

ec42536f50943a38138d63621738bf4a4e5bfa8f.text: When you click the "copy invite link" button in the referral banner, the copied link now points to the full /get-started sign-up walkthrough instead of the bare landing page. That walkthrough link is personalized: if you have a display name set, the URL includes a ?referrer= parameter so your friend sees "X invited you to try Freebuff!" on the page. You don't need to do anything new. The banner itself is reordered to render right after the streak line while keeping its place anchored to the model picker, so the layout shift is purely visual and only affects where the banner appears on screen.

04d67d73b9052e63dead5ad1a6cf6bbe76c4cd2e.text: Freebuff removed the Kimi K2.6 model from the list of models you can freely pick from a drop-down menu in the app. If you had Kimi chosen as your go-to model, it will stop being available to select in the free model picker. However, your existing conversations using Kimi will continue to work, and if you ever upgrade or are part of a special promotion, you will still be able to use it as a premium option.

bfaad48713d14b4e948a6ad49a2c6f79d6cb250c.text: The Freebuff team added two new tracking labels to their internal analytics system: one for noticing when a referral attempt fails because of basic eligibility rules (such as a too-old account or a self-referral), and another for spotting when a referred person appears to share an IP address or browser with the person who invited them. These labels exist now in the shared definition file used by all Freebuff surfaces (the web app, the desktop app, and the command-line tool), so any of them can start recording these situations later, but right now nothing in the product actually logs them. Because the change only adds vocabulary to a catalog and does not wire up any code to emit or read these events, you will not see any difference in your daily use, and no action is required on your part.

c931d187e9c094739c6acc86ec1c583dc9319d51.title: SDK forwards end-user id through agent run, step, and model requests
c931d187e9c094739c6acc86ec1c583dc9319d51.summary: The SDK now accepts an end-user id on agent runs, agent steps, and model provider requests and attaches it to outgoing requests as the `x-freebuff-acting-user-id` header so trusted service accounts can act on behalf of a signed-in user. The id flows from `RunOptions.userId` in `sdk/src/run.ts` into `callMainPrompt`, into `getModelForRequest` and `createCodebuffBackendModel` in `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, and into `startAgentRun`, `finishAgentRun`, and `addAgentStep` in `sdk/src/impl/database.ts`, where each conditionally sets `FREEBUFF_ACTING_USER_HEADER` only when the id is supplied. A matching `GetUserInfoByIdInput` and `GetUserInfoByIdFn` pair was added to `common/src/types/contracts/database.ts`, giving the shared database contract a type-level path for user lookup by id. The new header is omitted entirely when no user id is present, matching ordinary API key behavior that cannot delegate.

c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.title: Release HTTP client adds redirect limit and retry support
c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.summary: The shared release HTTP client now caps redirect chains at 10, follows 303/307/308 in addition to 301/302, rejects redirect responses missing a Location header, and exposes a withRetries helper that retries transient failures with exponential backoff and a maxAttempts cap. The CLI release wrappers for codebuff and freebuff call downloadAndExtract through withRetries(CONFIG.downloadMaxAttempts), pass CONFIG.downloadRequestTimeout to httpGet, and log retry attempts, so flaky downloads and long redirect loops no longer fail upgrades silently. This hardens the binary download path so a transient network error or a misbehaving registry/CDN redirect no longer blocks installs or updates on any tier.

In cli/release/index.js (and identically in the staging and freebuff counterparts), downloadBinary is refactored to call a new downloadAndExtract helper wrapped in withRetries using CONFIG.downloadMaxAttempts, CONFIG.downloadRequestTimeout, isRetryableDownloadStatus, isRetryableDownloadError, retry messaging, and a new pipeline import from stream/promises.
