dc8f236d73ec651b392b4dbb09a8826258f12666.text: Freebuff's team added the ability to tell Reddit's ad system when someone has a genuinely good first experience with the assistant and again at useful intervals afterward, like one day and one week later, so Reddit ads can be measured against real, repeat usage instead of just a single click. This only affects people whose traffic Freebuff tracks for advertising measurement, and only when Freebuff has its own configuration in place. You, as a Freebuff user, will not notice anything different in your daily coding session, no extra prompts or slowdowns.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This Freebuff release adds GPT-5.6 Luna as a new free AI model you can pick in the model menu, and makes the daily free session limit six per day instead of five. The landing screen now handles rate limits and daily spend limits by showing a clear message with a countdown timer instead of leaving you stuck, and the model picker reorders itself to recommend DeepSeek V4 Flash with a one-time migration that switches your old saved pick to the newer model on every login. Ads in streamed responses now wait a few messages before the first one appears and space themselves every three messages afterward, and the CLI downloader retries failed updates three times with redirects and proxy support so half-finished installs roll back to the previous version instead of corrupting your binary. If you deliberately choose a model and the server locks you to a different one, the session now deletes itself and retries your chosen model automatically, and shared subprocess output is capped at 10MB to prevent crashes from huge git diffs. The streak bonus for GLM sessions is now uncapped with a daily reset giving one session per day per qualified referral, while the web referral tier ladder and watermark removal tiers were removed from the config entirely.

c931d187e9c094739c6acc86ec1c583dc9319d51.text: The Freebuff SDK can now forward an end-user id through agent runs, steps, and model requests as a new header so trusted service accounts can act on behalf of a signed-in user. This affects developers and partners embedding the Freebuff SDK in their applications, particularly those using service accounts to run on behalf of end users. For most Freebuff users and CLI users there is no visible change today, since this only activates when a trusted service account supplies a user id; regular API key usage is unchanged and the header is omitted entirely when no user id is provided.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: This release adds a /copy slash command that exports your entire conversation - messages, replies, and tool work - to your clipboard as Markdown, trimming large tool results on SSH connections to stay within size limits. Premium model users now see a reset countdown in the model picker header showing when their daily quota refreshes, and the waiting room display adapts to narrow and tall terminals by promoting the logo and adjusting the streak indicator layout. The CLI no longer keeps you in a queued waiting room, transitioning directly from model selection to active chat, while desktop premium users get a one-per-user concurrency cap on premium models. New analytics events now track the full login and referral signup funnel, and the referral banner links to /get-started with your inviter's name for a personalized welcome. Streak rewards grant bonus sessions after 7-day milestones, with GLM 5.2 weekly sessions added as a referral reward for qualified users.

cee618d4b5a9d00053d9955262595b276fd7ea1e.text: The assistant now holds back queued messages while your free session has fully ended, instead of sending them into a session the server will reject. This affects you if you use the free version of the assistant in the terminal, web app, desktop app, or through the SDK. You no longer see failed messages being sent after your session runs out; they stay queued and automatically resume once you rejoin a new session.

a4f5d94ecbd0e09f41c432abf7115b65eb498f3e.text: The Freebuff service now copies its important usage events (like when someone starts the app or signs up) into a separate debugging log that engineers can search. It still sends everything to PostHog like before, but skips the extremely high-volume noise events (like detailed click tracking and screen recordings) so the debugging log stays readable and affordable. Who this affects: End users of the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app do not see any change. This is an internal observability and logging infrastructure change for the Freebuff team. Everyday impact: There is no visible effect or action needed. The change only affects how Freebuff's own engineering team debugs and troubleshoots the service.

a54b61094c5a8b141e2d1f4dd365e538ffb8529c.text: When you open the Freebuff coding assistant for the first time, the list of AI models you can choose from now opens already collapsed to a single highlighted recommendation, so you can just press Enter to get started without scanning multiple options. The recommended model is MiniMax M3 (or DeepSeek V4 Flash in limited regions), which gives strong performance without depleting your daily premium-model quota. Other models are still available via a 'see all' toggle, now grouped into clear 'Premium' and 'Unlimited' sections, and the session counter is hidden until you've actually used a session.

874c8ec4aabb8c0db77ffe375d5edd248402a83a.text: The team added a new AI model, Kimi K2.7 Code, to the set of models the assistant can use, and it’s now the one the team uses to grade how well the assistant works on server-related coding tasks. This is an internal change that only affects the Freebuff engineering team who build and test the assistant. You won’t see or use this change yourself, and it does not affect which AI models you can pick in the Freebuff app today.

d38aa87d8f52653a6efbd545aba736173cf07a89.text: The assistant behind Freebuff's chat feature can now hand off tricky questions to a specialized reasoning helper, rather than trying to figure everything out itself, so answers to things like math problems or architecture debates come out more thoughtful. The chat interface can now call that helper directly as part of handling a conversation, it identifies itself as Thinker, and it takes a bit more time to work through problems instead of rushing to a quick reply.

f0c65d3132424eafe090f368fc5615f2ced05c62.text: The Freebuff service now collects a second copy of your CLI logs and ships them to a separate server-side log store called Axiom, running alongside the existing analytics tracking. This runs automatically in production for all Freebuff users who are signed in, and developers or service admins can turn it off with an environment toggle. From your daily use you notice nothing: the assistant behaves exactly as before, but behind the scenes Freebuff's operators gain an extra diagnostic view of what happens in your terminal session.

66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.title: CLI logs conversation summaries and adds opt-in trace writer
66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.summary: The CLI now writes a summary-only run config from `use-send-message.ts` and a summary-only agent step log in `run-agent-step.ts`, instead of dumping the full conversation history and attachments into `log.jsonl` on every step. It adds `trimOversizedChatLogs` (invoked via `setTimeout` at startup in `index.tsx`), which reclaims disk by deleting any `log.jsonl` over `MAX_LOG_FILE_BYTES` (10 MB) from chats untouched for more than `MIN_LOG_AGE_MS` (14 days). A new opt-in `TraceWriter` records message histories to `trace.jsonl` only when `CODEBUFF_TRACE` is set (or in dev), and the SDK's `getAgentRuntimeImpl` and `CodebuffClient` now accept a `traceWriter` option threaded through the agent runtime. Together these changes stop multi-GB debug logs while keeping detailed tracing available on demand.

66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.migration: No migration is required; existing debug `log.jsonl` files over 10 MB in chats untouched for 14+ days are deleted the next time the CLI starts.

9d9e3f15ad1e2fd45a3501a73a9ea9d5acc8ed79.text: When you chat with Freebuff's web assistant at freebuff.com/chat, it will start using a built-in research tool to find and recommend third-party developer services, rather than guessing from its own training. The change lets that chat surface tag every product suggestion as coming from the Chat experience, so clicks are tracked as Chat traffic instead of being lumped in with the Freebuff CLI. For you as a Freebuff Chat user, the daily experience is the same: you still chat normally, and when you ask for something like a hosting or payment provider, the assistant will now try to look up and show the right option with a real setup link to click through.

66b39f9ac99af7faa8b610590717bdfa5daeb7f1.text: The assistant now writes a short, plain-English summary to its debug log instead of dumping your entire conversation and every file attachment into the same log file every time it took a step, which used to create multi-gigabyte log files that ate up disk space. Starting today, the CLI also automatically deletes any of those old, oversized log files that belong to conversations left untouched for 14 days or longer, while leaving your actual chat history files alone. If you are a developer who wants the full, message-by-message transcript for troubleshooting a specific run, you can turn on detailed tracing with a single setting that saves it to a separate trace file; by default, that detailed tracing stays off so your disk is not filled with a second copy of your conversation.

35474f6bf77e51e4dbcf3773cbb0ebf5c30d6fe7.text: The CLI now treats each chat session like a tracked task with a clear reason for stopping it. When you interrupt the assistant, start a new chat, resume a previous one, or log out, the system stops the current task specifically and applies the right queue behavior for that reason, rather than just clearing whatever was running. This prevents a late-finishing task from accidentally saving its output into the wrong conversation you already switched away from. If you use the Freebuff or Codebuff CLI, no action is required; the change is internal, but you may notice cleaner handling when switching chats mid-response or logging out during a run.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release introduces GPT-5.6 Luna as a new free AI model you can select in the picker, retires Kimi K2.7 Code from free usage, and raises the default daily free sessions from 5 to 6. The model picker now shows which models are new, deemphasizes older picks, and can automatically guide you to a better model if your saved choice is no longer recommended. Ads in streamed responses wait two nodes before the first placement then appear every three nodes, and the read files tool now shares a 100,000 character and 20,000 token budget across all files in one call. When too many people share one internet address, the app routes you to a landing screen that tells you how many people are ahead instead of spinning forever. The Cloud stack planner now uses DeepSeek V4 Pro for planning and a separate model for building, and stream interruptions recover automatically up to three times without dropping your work.

c4a838fedc84d87b1640d62047cc4aa7bff923b4.text: The downloader that fetches the Codebuff and Freebuff applications to your computer is now more resilient when the server it talks to misbehaves. It caps how many redirects it will follow (at ten), retries failed downloads with increasing wait times between attempts (up to three tries), and recognizes a broader set of redirect statuses, so you are less likely to see a hard "Download failed" error when the release servers are briefly unavailable or returning odd responses. When a download still cannot succeed, it drops the old proxy hint message in favor of pointing you at the same generic internet-connection troubleshooting. Affects anyone installing or updating Codebuff or Freebuff via the CLI today; most users just notice fewer failed downloads.

0a3669024953392e5c7b6171940113766df9c728.text: The assistant now recognizes when a network connection goes quiet for five minutes and shows you a clear, network-focused explanation instead of a confusing server-error message. It affects anyone running a coding agent session through the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK. In daily use, when your connection drops packets silently (like a flaky Wi-Fi, VPN, or proxy), you will see a message telling you to retry, check your network, or switch networks, rather than a generic timeout line that makes it look like the server crashed.

44cbd349993e6f82827d8ca66c2b3dcf6634ce31.text: You now get a code review when you run a task using the MiniMax M3 model in Freebuff's free tier, where there wasn't one before. The change affects only Freebuff users who pick MiniMax M3 as their model, since other free models already reviewed code and MiniMax M3 now joins them in getting that review step. In daily use, you will notice generated code coming back checked over by a reviewer agent that follows the same pattern as every other free model, rather than seeing the review step skipped just for this model.

f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.title: Proactive AVX2 baseline selection and spawn error handling in CLI
f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.summary: The CLI release wrapper now detects CPU AVX2 support up front on Windows (using PowerShell's IsProcessorFeaturePresent) and Linux (/proc/cpuinfo) instead of waiting for the optimized binary to crash with SIGILL, caching the result in `cpu-features.json` and routing to the `-baseline` target proactively. `spawnInstalledBinary` now wraps the spawn call in try/catch to handle synchronous spawn errors like Windows UNKNOWN errno from antivirus or Smart App Control, printing system info and a baseline override hint via the new `printSpawnFailure`/`exitOnSpawnFailure`. The staging banner log lines were removed from `cli/release-staging/index.js`, and `tree-sitter.wasm` ships as a sibling file to the binary during download. These changes span the codebuff, freebuff, and staging CLI release wrappers.
f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.evidence: All three files show the same AVX2 detection refactor: `linuxCpuHasAvx2` changed from a strict platform/arch guard (returning true for any non-linux-x64) to a try/catch reading `/proc/cpuinfo`; new `probeWindowsAvx2`, `machineHasAvx2`, `detectMachineHasAvx2`, `readCachedAvx2`, `writeCachedAvx2`, `getCpuFeatureCachePath`, `printBaselineOverrideHint`, and `printSystemInfo` functions were added to `cli/release-staging/index.js`, `cli/release/index.js`, and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`; `getTargetOverride` now checks for missing spawn targets; `spawnInstalledBinary` wraps the spawn call in try/catch to handle synchronous spawn errors and `printSpawnFailure`/`exitOnSpawnFailure` were added; the staging banner log lines were removed; and `tree-sitter.wasm` is now moved as a sibling file to the binary during download in `cli/release/index.js` and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`.
f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.unknowns: The rollout mechanism and whether the Windows AVX2 detection cache in `cpu-features.json` is cleared on uninstall.

changes.what: Added proactive AVX2 CPU detection on Windows and Linux with disk caching, synchronous spawn error handling, and removed the staging banner log lines.

293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.title: Active session summary shows used quota instead of remaining
293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.summary: The active session summary in cli/src/components/freebuff-active-session-summary.tsx now displays formatSessionUnits(quota.recentCount) of quota.limit with a 'used' label, replacing the prior remaining-count display that subtracted quota.recentCount from quota.limit and labeled it 'left'. 89ef2b771d74e90e173c03c80e5a0b7e1285932f.title: Gravity-index labels and button styling refined with model multimodal
89ef2b771d74e90e173c03c80e5a0b7e1285932f.summary: Gravity Index tool calls now render as verb-first labels like 'Search services' instead of 'Services 烷 Search' in gravity-index.tsx, and the `gravity_index` renderer drops the BRAND/withSubcommand pattern in favor of DEFAULT_NAME. e39f9da8bc239a0b8c08ee3014e7ec7c2a287c41.title: MiniMax M3 premium model and free root agent added

a60a6abccdfcbbe6d3a72c17ed86dbc03810876a.text: The slash menu now lets you press Tab to fill in the command you've highlighted without running it, so you can add extra arguments before sending, while arrow keys move the highlight and Enter runs the chosen command immediately. Freebuff users who use the assistant every day will soon see a weekly streak reward added, where staying active for about a week grants bonus usage credits. No setup is needed today, though the reward feature appears to be configured and waiting to be surfaced in the coming streak-related UI.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: This release adds a new slash command (/copy) that copies your full conversation (including tool calls and reasoning) to the clipboard as Markdown so you can easily save or share chats. The free model list in the picker now puts MiniMax M3 first, with DeepSeek V4 Pro moved to second position, making the recommended starting model easier to spot. The /plan and /review commands no longer require a connected ChatGPT account, and instead run on whichever model you currently have selected. A new persistent anonymous analytics ID means your pre-login activity now correctly links to your account when you sign in, improving measurement consistency. The desktop app now limits premium models to one running at a time per user to prevent concurrency abuse, while Windows AVX2 detection has been improved for better compatibility. Users can now tab-complete slash commands without leaving the chat input, and the streak reward system has been unified across surfaces to consistently grant free GLM 5.2 sessions for qualifying users.

9c8af8c79c36649273421ef43e515b2fffe63be3.text: When you open the Freebuff assistant in a folder that isn't a real project (like your home directory), it now shows you the first few levels of files instead of stopping at a blank list, capping the view at three levels deep, up to 2000 files and 500 folders, followed by a short line explaining that deeper files are hidden unless you open a project folder.

e39f9da8bc239a0b8c08ee3014e7ec7c2a287c41.text: The Freebuff assistant can now run a new, more capable model variant named MiniMax M3, which appears in the model picker as a frontier-tier option and triggers a dedicated free orchestrator agent built for it. This applies to Freebuff users on the free tier who choose to select and use this new model and its paired agent. You will see the new MiniMax M3 option in the model picker and, when selected, the assistant runs the corresponding free orchestrator agent tuned for that model.

89ef2b771d74e90e173c03c80e5a0b7e1285932f.text: The labels that appear when the assistant searches for services or browses integrations now read as plain verb-first phrases like "Search services" or "Browse services" instead of a prefixed "Brand - Verb" format, and the rendered buttons in the terminal are now always outlined (never filled), with the label underlining on hover, dimming briefly on click, and showing a trailing arrow to mark external links. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI and its built-in service-integration lookup tools. For these developers, the service tool labels are clearer, and any button the assistant renders to open an external page now has a consistent outlined look with hover and click feedback. The change is live today for Freebuff CLI users.

293172345e45adda8b4ab9be0546a1b5614ad09c.text: The summary line on your screen now shows how much of your monthly quota you have already used (for example, 3 of 10), instead of flipping it to show how many you have left. This is for people who use the free Freebuff coding assistant in their terminal or on the website or desktop app. If you upgraded to the newest version, you will simply see the numbers worded the opposite way the next time you glance at your session stats, and no other behavior changes.

637bdf14fa0443c9539f6550eeb64ae129fb55c6.text: When you are using the Freebuff command-line assistant (the free version of Codebuff) and you send a prompt, your computer now quietly logs that you sent a message, but only if you are on the Freebuff side, not the paid Codebuff side. This logging happens in the background and helps the team that runs Freebuff count how many people are actively using Freebuff each day, which is a metric they track across their desktop app and website as well. You will not see this happen yourself, and there is no new feature or performance change to notice; the assistant behaves the same as before.

61bbbed7acda7e26413a443b17854e6dfdd359d9.text: The engineering team removed a set of experimental helper agents that were being used in-house to test and evaluate coding assistant features. These agents and their supporting files are no longer present in the codebase, and the project's guide documents have been updated to remove references to that experimental folder. If you are not an internal developer working on the project, you do not interact with these helpers and will not notice any difference in how the assistant behaves.

ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.title: Remove Freebuff waiting-room queued state from session lifecycle
ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.summary: The Freebuff free-tier no longer has a queued state: picking a model POSTs straight to an active session instead of joining a per-model queue. The `queued` branch is deleted from the `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` union in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, and the CLI's `nextDelayMs`, `getFreebuffInstanceId`, `shouldReleaseSlot`, `apply`, and startup-takeover logic in `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` no longer handle it. `cli/src/app.tsx`'s `AuthedSurface` routes only `none` and terminal statuses through the waiting room, while `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx` drops the queued position panel and its `formatWait`/`formatElapsed` helpers. The `committedModelId` in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` is now always `null`, and `useNow` in the waiting room ticks once a minute (not per-second) since the queue timer no longer exists. A secondary change removes the disabled server status and `queueDepthByModel`, collapsing the landing response to quota and referral snapshots only.
ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.evidence: Removed the `queued` session status from the FreebuffSessionServerResponse union and all CLI handling in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts (nextDelayMs, getFreebuffInstanceId, shouldReleaseSlot, apply, startup-takeover branch, and the landing GET), cli/src/app.tsx (AuthedSurface routing in AuthedSurface), cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx (removed queued position panel, formatWait/formatElapsed, and isQueued gating), cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx (committedModelId no longer reads session.status === 'queued'), and common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts (deleted the queued union member, the disabled status, and queueDepthByModel from none).
ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.unknowns: The diff is client-side only; it does not show the server-side removal of queueing or whether the `x-freebuff-model` header now means 'model to admit' rather than 'model to queue for'.

changes.what: Removed the `{ status: 'queued', ... }` and `{ status: 'disabled' }` union members from `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` and dropped `queueDepthByModel` from the `none` status, leaving quota and referral snapshots as the only pre-join metadata.

Deleted all `queued` handling from `nextDelayMs`, `getFreebuffInstanceId`, `shouldReleaseSlot`, `apply`, the startup-takeover branch, and the landing GET; changed `POLL_INTERVAL_QUEUED_MS` removal and the admission bell to fire on `none` to `active`; set `committedModelId` to always null.
Removed `session.status === 'queued'` from the `AuthedSurface` waiting-room routing condition so only `none` and terminal statuses route through the pre-chat screen.

Removed the `isQueued` branch, the queued position panel (`queuedTitleText`, `session.position`/`queueDepth` display), and the `formatWait`/`formatElapsed` helpers; changed `useNow` from per-second to once-a-minute ticking on landing.
Set `committedModelId` to a `null` literal constant since the queued state no longer exists, and updated the doc comment to say the POST admits straight to active.

f1a5a202b3505df7216651ab21560dd053faf148.text: The program that launches the assistant on your computer now checks your processor's capabilities before starting, instead of waiting for a crash. On Windows and Linux it looks for AVX2 support and, if your CPU lacks it, automatically downloads a compatible version of the program rather than throwing an error. If a download or antivirus tool blocks the program from starting, you'll now see a clear explanation of what went wrong and how to fix it. You notice this as fewer startup crashes and clearer error messages when something blocks the program from running.

ca8ddb859a773965c2058c74e401c818650f92d9.text: The Freebuff waiting room no longer queues you. When you pick a free model and press Enter, the assistant starts right away instead of putting you in a virtual line. Affects Freebuff users who use the free (ad-supported) tier of the assistant. You no longer see a queue position or an elapsed-in-line timer. The model picker stays open until you start a session, and your spot in line is gone because there is no line anymore.

6e392721fb79228f970577ee7d957562e282073f.text: This release adds a new /copy command (also /copy-chat or /export) that saves your whole chat - your messages, the AI's replies, thinking, tool usage, and helper agents - as Markdown you can paste anywhere, with smaller versions for SSH sessions so it still works in tight terminals. It introduces a referral reward AI model that you can use by inviting friends, and a new banner in the waiting room that shows your invite link and rewards for bringing people to Freebuff. The premium model selector now always shows how long until your daily reset, moved the session counter to the header, and the streak line shows a progress dot track that adapts to narrow terminals. Other improvements include always-on analytics so Freebuff can measure daily active users across CLI, web, and desktop, plus better error messages when external tools fail to connect and Tab key behavior that completes commands without running them.

cc46321813ab0a89d119f1d808f82355fc43126e.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.1.2 version bump
cc46321813ab0a89d119f1d808f82355fc43126e.summary: The Freebuff CLI release manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` advances the `version` field from `0.1.1` to `0.1.2`. The diff is a release-bump commit with no accompanying source code, launcher, or runtime logic changes.
cc46321813ab0a89d119f1d808f82355fc43126e.evidence: The diff for commit cc463218 touches only `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.1.1` to `0.1.2`; no source, launcher, or runtime logic changes are present in the diff.
cc46321813ab0a89d119f1d808f82355fc43126e.unknowns: The diff does not show any new features, fix, or behavior shipped in this release beyond the version string change.

cc46321813ab0a89d119f1d808f82355fc43126e.text: This release fixes startup crashes on older Windows computers that lack newer processor features. When the launcher detects that Bun (the JavaScript runtime) has crashed due to a missing AVX2 instruction set - now confirmed by reading its error output - it automatically switches to a simpler version of the app built for older hardware. Previously, only specific Windows error codes triggered this fallback, so some pre-AVX2 CPUs would fail to start the app silently. Now, the launcher reliably recognizes the crash pattern in the error text and downloads the compatible version, letting users on older processors launch Freebuff without issues.

47ac2c9063507ddb8a13343548e72527f7a92750.title: First-party decision log keeps L2 ranker counters and drops campaign
47ac2c9063507ddb8a13343548e72527f7a92750.summary: The `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS` allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` now permits `ranker_mode`, `ranker_version`, `ranker_evidence`, `ranker_scored_placements`, and `ranker_disagreements`, so the L2 v0 ranker's shadow-decision metrics survive sanitization into Axiom. Campaign identifiers such as `ranker_lead_campaign_id` and `rankedLeadCampaignId` remain outside the allowlist and are dropped, keeping the campaign handle out of operational telemetry. The change is consumed by the decision contract test asserting the retained-and-dropped shape.
47ac2c9063507ddb8a13343548e72527f7a92750.evidence: The diff to `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` adds five fields to the `ADS_FIRST_PARTY_DECISION_FIELDS` schema: `ranker_mode`, `ranker_version`, `ranker_evidence`, `ranker_scored_placements`, and `ranker_disagreements`. The new test 'keeps the ranker counters and drops its campaign ids' asserts these fields are retained while non-allowlisted identifiers like `ranker_lead_campaign_id` and `rankedLeadCampaignId` are discarded.
47ac2c9063507ddb8a13343548e72527f7a92750.unknowns: The diff does not show which producer emits the new ranker fields or how the `FREEBUFF_FIRST_PARTY_RANKER` switch gates `ranker_mode`.

47ac2c9063507ddb8a13343548e72527f7a92750.text: The internal logging system that Freebuff's operators use to monitor ad delivery now records additional counters from a newer ranking model: it can log the model's mode and version, the state of its evidence, how many ad slots it scored, and how often its top pick differed from the current rotation. Campaign identifiers from those model picks remain excluded, so operational dashboards see only aggregate disagreement counts, not the specific campaigns the model preferred. This is internal telemetry for the Freebuff service team, live today, and changes nothing in your coding sessions or ad experience.

184ef6e63baa3df9926f8fa26c0e8ddbd31568df.title: Home hero surface chosen event and home hero download location
184ef6e63baa3df9926f8fa26c0e8ddbd31568df.summary: A new analytics event `freebuff.home_hero_surface_chosen` is added to `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` to track which product tab a home hero visitor picks when committing to a product. It pairs with the existing `freebuff.desktop_download_clicked` event: a hero Desktop download is instead recorded at the newly exported `HOME_HERO_DOWNLOAD_LOCATION = 'home_hero'`. The companion report `bun scripts/home-hero-funnel.ts` consumes these events.
184ef6e63baa3df9926f8fa26c0e8ddbd31568df.evidence: Added `FREEBUFF_HOME_HERO_SURFACE_CHOSEN = 'freebuff.home_hero_surface_chosen'` to the AnalyticsEvent enum in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, plus the export `HOME_HERO_DOWNLOAD_LOCATION = 'home_hero'`.
184ef6e63baa3df9926f8fa26c0e8ddbd31568df.unknowns: The diff only adds the enum member and export without wiring an emitter, so nothing fires yet.

184ef6e63baa3df9926f8fa26c0e8ddbd31568df.text: The Freebuff team added a new tracking tag and a saved download location to their internal measurement setup. Only the Freebuff engineering team uses these pieces right now, since they are part of the data the report script reads. Nothing you see or do in the app changes today, because the tracking tag has not yet been wired into the buttons that record clicks.

681a5136f9a98fc15eba63723ba983964695953f.title: Onboarding questionnaire adds Desktop surface and shared form logic
681a5136f9a98fc15eba63723ba983964695953f.summary: A new file `freebuff-onboarding-form.ts` holds the pure form logic - option toggling, readiness checks, answer serialization, resume point, and option ordering - shared by the Web form and the Desktop app so they cannot post different answers. `ONBOARDING_SURFACES` in `freebuff-onboarding.ts` gained `desktop` as a third submission surface, recorded on each row for segmentation, alongside its JSDoc clarifying the desktop dialog is asked after sign-in when the app retakes focus. The new module and its exports are covered by `freebuff-onboarding-form.test.ts`, which asserts toggle behavior for single-choice, multi-select, and exclusive options, plus readiness and advance-on-pick rules.
681a5136f9a98fc15eba63723ba983964695953f.evidence: Added `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding-form.ts` exporting `Selections`, `OtherText`, `toggleOption`, `isAnswerReady`, `shouldAdvanceOnPick`, `toAnswerList`, `selectionsFromAnswers`, `resumeIndex`, and `orderOptionsForDisplay`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` changed `ONBOARDING_SURFACES` from `['web', 'cli_login']` to ['web', 'cli_login', 'desktop'] and updated its JSDoc; tests added in `common/src/constants/__tests__/freebuff-onboarding-form.test.ts` cover `toggleOption`, `isAnswerReady`, and `shouldAdvanceOnPick`.

681a5136f9a98fc15eba63723ba983964695953f.text: The signup questionnaire that new Freebuff users fill out has been updated so that the desktop app now asks the same questions as the web version and the log-in screen, and the answers from all three places are processed by one shared set of rules so they can't drift apart. This is an internal correctness and consistency fix for the engineering team, not a new feature users will notice; it keeps the desktop onboarding dialog from recording answers differently than the other two entry points, but there is no change to what you see or any action you need to take.

4f3c8a0aa859cb31d49ad29347bef0743b94a493.title: Freebuff Chat Header Picks Wordmark by Fitted Width
4f3c8a0aa859cb31d49ad29347bef0743b94a493.summary: The chat header in `cli/src/components/freebuff-chat-header.tsx` now selects the Freebuff wordmark variant by measuring each ASCII logo's line width against the panel's padded width budget, replacing the fixed `terminalWidth >= 69` breakpoint. A new `wordmarkVariants` array maps `FREEBUFF_WORDMARK` and `FREEBUFF_WORDMARK_COMPACT` to their computed widths, and the header picks the widest variant that fits, falling back to the plain `Freebuff` text when neither fits.
4f3c8a0aa859cb31d49ad29347bef0743b94a493.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-chat-header.tsx`, a new `wordmarkVariants` array maps `FREEBUFF_WORDMARK` and `FREEBUFF_WORDMARK_COMPACT` to their measured widths, and the header now renders `wordmarkVariants.find((variant) => variant.width <= width)?.text ?? 'Freebuff'` instead of the previous `terminalWidth >= 69 ? FREEBUFF_WORDMARK : FREEBUFF_WORDMARK_COMPACT` ternary.

4f3c8a0aa859cb31d49ad29347bef0743b94a493.text: The banner at the top of your Freebuff chat panel now picks between a wide and a narrow version of the Freebuff logo based on how much horizontal room is available, instead of a single fixed screen-width cutoff. This only affects what you see in the chat header when you resize your terminal, so nothing behaves differently otherwise. Live today. You do not need to do anything, and there is no impact on your conversations, model choices, or Freebucks balance.

d94526c00d428f9267d19bff1d5328200e1dcfe5.title: Steering hook accepts structured messages with images
d94526c00d428f9267d19bff1d5328200e1dcfe5.summary: The `drainSteeringMessages` hook in `loopAgentSteps` and the SDK's `RunOptions` now uses the `DrainSteeringMessages` type from `common/src/types/contracts/steering.ts`, replacing the previous `() => string[]` signature. Drained values can now be plain strings or objects shaped as { prompt: string; content?: Array<TextPart | ImagePart> }, which the runtime maps into `userMessage` content via `buildUserMessageContent(message.prompt, undefined, message.content)`. The draining call in `run-agent-step.ts` is now awaited, so async hosts can load attachment bytes before the batch is handed to the agent. This lets hosts inject image-bearing messages into a running turn without aborting the run. Two changes elsewhere (type import in `sdk/src/run.ts`, new type file) carry the same contract.
d94526c00d428f9267d19bff1d5328200e1dcfe5.evidence: New file `common/src/types/contracts/steering.ts` exports `SteeringMessage` and `DrainSteeringMessages`. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, the `loopAgentSteps` parameter `drainSteeringMessages` type changes from `() => string[]` to `DrainSteeringMessages` and the call site changes from `params.drainSteeringMessages?.()` to `await params.drainSteeringMessages?.()`, with each drained message mapped through `buildUserMessageContent(message.prompt, undefined, message.content)`. In `sdk/src/run.ts`, the `RunOptions` field `drainSteeringMessages` type changes from `() => string[]` to `DrainSteeringMessages`.

changes.what: Added the shared steering contract that lets hosts drain structured user messages, including images, into a running agent step.

Switched the `drainSteeringMessages` parameter of `loopAgentSteps` to the shared `DrainSteeringMessages` type, awaited the drain, and mapped each message through `buildUserMessageContent` so prompt and image content are preserved.
Updated `RunOptions.drainSteeringMessages` to the shared `DrainSteeringMessages` type so SDK hosts can pass structured messages.

d94526c00d428f9267d19bff1d5328200e1dcfe5.text: The assistant can now receive new messages - including photos - from you while it's still working, so you can guide it mid-task instead of waiting until it stops. This works through the SDK and runtime that developers build on top of Freebuff, and it's live today for those builders. When you use an app built with this SDK and send the assistant a photo for reference during a run, it sees the image immediately at the next step without stopping or restarting the turn.

e906480d29aed4b3b158aa77176d245198b9d5aa.title: Freebuff CLI 0.1.3 pins baseline build on evidence not any crash
e906480d29aed4b3b158aa77176d245198b9d5aa.summary: Freebuff CLI 0.1.3 ships the AVX2 baseline-fallback rewrite in `cli/release-core/launcher.js`, where `detectMachineHasAvx2()` now requires evidence before pinning a machine to the slower build. `crashAvx2Verdict()` reads `{ avx2, evidence }` from Bun's `CPU:`/`Features:` report or the OS probe (`parseCpuinfoAvx2`, `parseSysctlAvx2`), `recordMachineLacksAvx2(evidence)` persists the reason, and `knownToHaveAvx2()` feeds `getDownloadTargetKey()` so a baseline install can return to the optimized build on the next update. The pin record now stores an evidence field (`bun-report`, `cpuinfo`, `sysctl`, or `crash`), and `readCpuFeatureRecord()` re-checks older evidence-less pins once against the OS. New tests in `cli/src/__tests__/launcher-avx2-fallback.test.ts` cover pinning on evidence, cpuinfo/sysctl parsing, SIGILL on AVX2 machines not pinning, Apple Silicon never pinning, and old evidence-less pins being dropped or upgraded.
e906480d29aed4b3b158aa77176d245198b9d5aa.evidence: In `cli/release-core/launcher.js`, `detectMachineHasAvx2()` now reads records via `readCpuFeatureRecord()` carrying an evidence field, `recordMachineLacksAvx2(evidence)` accepts an evidence parameter, the new `crashAvx2Verdict()` function resolves `{ avx2, evidence }` from Bun's crash report or the OS probe, and `getDownloadTargetKey()` now calls `knownToHaveAvx2()` to move a baseline install back to the optimized build; new constants `BUN_CPU_LINE`, `parseCpuinfoAvx2`, and `parseSysctlAvx2` are defined and exposed under `__testing`, with platform and `arch` destructured as variables in the test module. Version bumped from 0.1.2 to 0.1.3 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` as a release-bump commit.
e906480d29aed4b3b158aa77176d245198b9d5aa.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Rewrote AVX2 detection so a baseline pin requires evidence and exposes it so a baseline install can return to the optimized build.
Version field bumped from 0.1.2 to 0.1.3 as a release bump.
Removed the 'client_hints_limited' branch comment from FreebuffPrivacyDecision, a doc-only edit to a type union.
Adds test cases asserting baseline pinning only on evidence, OS probe parsing, and old evidence-less pin re-checking.

e906480d29aed4b3b158aa77176d245198b9d5aa.text: The Freebuff CLI now remembers whether your computer can handle the fast version of the assistant, and it only switches to the slower, compatible version when it is sure your machine actually needs it. Previously, a harmless crash or a glitch could trick the launcher into permanently thinking your computer couldn't run the fast version, forcing you onto the slow one for good. Now, if your computer is actually capable, the next update will switch you back to the faster version without any action from you.

5400c18c15a9708b4b3b0e835575c1806c592295.title: Model compaction respects per-model output cap
5400c18c15a9708b4b3b0e835575c1806c592295.summary: BYOK connections set `compactContext.maxOutputTokens` on every local template (sdk/src/run.ts), so a summarizer request that previously asked for 6,000 tokens against a 4,096-token cap is now clamped to the model's real output limit via `compactionOutputTokens` and `compactionSummaryBudget` (half the cap), because a capped connection would run out of output mid-summary. The stream now reports its finish reason through `onFinishReason` and `compactWithModel` throws before installing a summary whose finish reason is `length`, so a truncated handoff is rejected and falls back to mechanical compaction instead of silently dropping the rest of the session.
5400c18c15a9708b4b3b0e835575c1806c592295.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts exports `compactionOutputTokens` (clamp summarizer request to min(16,384, model cap)) and `compactionSummaryBudget` (now bounded by SUMMARY_OUTPUT_SHARE * output cap), with `compactWithModel` passing `maxOutputTokens` through to the stream and throwing when `finishReason === 'length'`; common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts adds `onFinishReason` to `PromptAiSdkStreamFn`, and sdk/src/impl/llm.ts calls it from the finish chunk; sdk/src/run.ts sets `maxOutputTokens: limits.maxOutputTokens` on every BYOK template's `compactContext`; tests assert 'the requested summary fits the output cap the request is clamped to' and 'compaction asks for a summary that fits the connection output cap and refuses one cut off by it'
5400c18c15a9708b4b3b0e835575c1806c592295.migration: If you author an agent with `compactContext`, you can now pass `maxOutputTokens` to cap the summarizer to your model's real output limit; existing agents keep working because the field is optional and defaults to the prior fixed ceiling.

changes.what: Added `compactionOutputTokens` and `compactionSummaryBudget` helpers that clamp the summarizer request to a model's `maxOutputTokens` cap (never above COMPACTION_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=16,384) and bound the summary to half that cap via SUMMARY_OUTPUT_SHARE=0.5; `compactWithModel` now threads.
Added `onFinishReason` callback to `PromptAiSdkStreamFn` so compaction can observe the stream's finish reason.
Threaded `onFinishReason` from `getAgentStreamFromTemplate` into the compaction stream so the summarizer's finish reason reaches the new guard.
Added optional `maxOutputTokens` to the `compactContext` shape on both the user-facing AgentDefinition and the backend AgentTemplate.
Added `maxOutputTokens` to the Zod schema for `compactContext`.
Sets `compactContext.maxOutputTokens` from the BYOK connection's `maxOutputTokens` on every local/published template so the summarizer request is clamped like any other BYOK request.

5400c18c15a9708b4b3b0e835575c1806c592295.text: When the assistant needs to catch up on a long conversation by asking a model to write a summary of everything so far, it now checks how many words that model is actually allowed to produce. If the model can only produce a smaller number of words than the summary needs, the request is automatically shortened to fit, instead of asking for too many words and getting cut off mid-sentence. This matters most for developers who run their own AI providers with smaller output limits than the default. The summary is also checked after it is written: if it was cut off, the system rejects it and falls back to a simpler, no-model-based method so the conversation can continue without losing context.

e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.title: Undici body cut now classified as transient network error
e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.summary: isTransientNetworkError in common/src/util/error.ts now returns true for undici's TypeError('terminated') body-read failure, which Node's fetch throws when the peer closes the socket after SSE headers arrive, by adding isUndiciBodyTerminated and the UND_ERR_SOCKET code to TRANSIENT_NETWORK_ERROR_CODES so an SDK host running on Node no longer ends the turn in an error on a dropped model stream.
e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.evidence: Modified file `common/src/util/error.ts` adds `isUndiciBodyTerminated` and the `UND_ERR_SOCKET` code to `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_ERROR_CODES`, and calls `isUndiciBodyTerminated` inside `isTransientNetworkError`.
e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.unknowns: The consuming code paths for this classification change are not shown in the diff.

changes.what: Added isUndiciBodyTerminated helper and UND_ERR_SOCKET code, and calls isUndiciBodyTerminated inside isTransientNetworkError.

e488d49ce54605dc40c2ec1c84a80ef495083786.text: The assistant now recognizes one more specific way a network connection can drop mid-stream and treats it as a temporary glitch worth retrying, rather than a hard failure. This affects anyone using the assistant through tools or environments built on Node.js (where the underlying fetch library is undici), which is common for developers embedding the assistant in their own apps via the SDK. In daily use, if a model's response gets cut off because the server connection closed unexpectedly, the assistant can now resume the turn instead of stopping with a confusing error, matching behavior Freebuff users already get when running in the terminal.

ba9141ce5a11e1158664e00ccf1f231dd032881a.title: MCP schema and result handling fixes for tool registration and storage
ba9141ce5a11e1158664e00ccf1f231dd032881a.summary: Replaced lodash cloneDeep with zod-safe cloneDeepKeepingZod in agent-runtime tool handling so zod v4 schemas keep their non-enumerable _zod engine during deep copy, fixing the empty inputSchema bug where properties were stripped at registration. Refactored MCP tool result content mapping into common/src/mcp/content-mapping.ts so text resources stay json values and non-image binary resources degrade to descriptive text instead of media, preventing base64 decode failures. Normalized tool inputSchemas to plain JSON Schema before storage in agent state and the subagent path so Zod instances no longer break JSON.stringify across turns. Moved to-json-schema helpers into util/to-json-schema.ts for spawn-agent-inline reuse without an import cycle. Each fix ships with a regression test that fails on pre-fix main.

61f50f7e2be156def198dac02c70318d621c4120.text: Freebuff is now able to offer certain special limited-time AI models to users no matter what subscription tier they are on, instead of only making them available to higher-tier subscribers. This is live today in Freebuff app version 0.0.179.

It only affects Freebuff's internal engineers and the metrics dashboards they maintain; it does not change anything you see or do in the app. You will notice nothing different today - the bookmark screen itself is already gone, and these entries were just leftover labels for events the app no longer sends.

3af5ff1fb34c0c30677e09070c89dcfb5c18d7c4.title: Freebuff CLI release bumped to 0.1.4
3af5ff1fb34c0c30677e09070c89dcfb5c18d7c4.summary: The version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was updated from 0.1.3 to 0.1.4, marking the publish of the Freebuff CLI 0.1.4 release. This is a release-bump commit affecting only the package manifest shipped to npm under the name field, so no runtime code, model, or command behavior changes with it.

3af5ff1fb34c0c30677e09070c89dcfb5c18d7c4.text: Freebuff 0.1.4 improves how the assistant handles long conversations that need to be condensed. When you connect your own AI model, the summarization step now respects that model's actual output limit, so a request that asks for more tokens than the model allows is reduced to fit, and a summary that gets cut off is rejected and replaced with a simpler mechanical summary instead of being used incomplete. The app also stops treating a specific kind of connection drop as a permanent failure, classifying it as a temporary network problem that the agent can retry through, which helps sessions that would otherwise end unexpectedly. Finally, the bookmark gate analytics events that were no longer used have been removed from the tracking list, so the event records only describe flows that are actually happening.

ed7485229b4d8f6492ea393d1c7d64d5e5455b8e.title: Compaction pass gains start/end hooks across SDK and agent runtime
ed7485229b4d8f6492ea393d1c7d64d5e5455b8e.summary: The SDK and agent runtime now expose onCompactionStart and onCompactionEnd callbacks alongside the existing onCompaction hook, so hosts can bracket a compaction pass with start and end events. In run-agent-step.ts the compactWithModelOrFallback call is wrapped in a try/finally so onCompactionEnd always fires after onCompaction, and the isRoot guard that previously wrapped only onCompaction now wraps onCompactionStart, onCompaction, and onCompactionEnd; in sdk/src/run.ts these callbacks are destructured from RunExecutionOptions and forwarded to callMainPrompt via the report/reportSignal wrappers. This lets a host show a continuous 'Compacting...' state without a visible gap between the pass it is showing and the handoff that replaces it.

ed7485229b4d8f6492ea393d1c7d64d5e5455b8e.text: The assistant now signals to its host app when a conversation-summarizing step starts and ends, so the app can cleanly show a loading indicator that disappears right as the summary replaces the old messages, with no blank moment. This matters for developers using the Freebuff SDK or hosts embedding the agent runtime, because the previous callbacks only fired after a summary finished, leaving a visual gap between the work and the handoff. It is live today, but only hosts that actually wire up the new start and end callbacks will see the smoother display; otherwise nothing changes for them.

3af5ff1fb34c0c30677e09070c89dcfb5c18d7c4.text: Freebuff 0.1.4 ships with better handling of AI conversation summaries, fixes for custom model settings when you bring your own provider, and corrections to how external tools (MCP) register and report their data. When the assistant shrinks a long chat down to keep it manageable, it now checks the real token limit of each model you use, so a summary request that asks for more than a model can actually output gets capped to what the model supports, and a summary that gets cut off mid-way is rejected instead of leaving you with an incomplete handoff. Tool registration problems where input fields disappeared have been fixed, so external tools you connect now keep their full settings, text resources from those tools stay usable as readable values, and binary (non-image) resources fall back to plain descriptions instead of breaking. A couple of retired bookmark-screen analytics events were also cleaned out of the system. Upgrading means your long sessions summarize more reliably without losing content, your custom or third-party AI models behave correctly instead of erroring on oversized requests, and connected external tools work without silent setup glitches.

ba9141ce5a11e1158664e00ccf1f231dd032881a.text: A batch of behind-the-scenes reliability fixes went live today so that tools added through plug-in servers register their input fields correctly and their results display properly. If you use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK and rely on MCP plug-in tools, those tools will now show up with their full set of input fields instead of an empty form, and text or binary results from plug-in servers render as readable values instead of erroring out. No action is required from you: existing plug-in servers and tool definitions keep working, only with corrected handling. These changes are live in today's release.

90462035737cade3fe28073b4c1f7a94a49fdb3e.title: Spawn agents results arrive as plain text instead of message arrays
90462035737cade3fe28073b4c1f7a94a49fdb3e.summary: The SDK changelog records that `spawn_agents` results from `last_message` agents now arrive as plain text, with each result's `value` being the child's final answer and a child whose last turn has no text reporting { type: 'error', message: 'No response from agent' }. The runtime enforces this in `outputForParent` within `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/agent-output.ts`, which `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts` calls as `value: outputForParent(output)`. A concrete constraint: the `answerText` helper strips think/reasoning scaffolding via `stripThinkScaffolding` before returning the parent's string, and `agents/file-explorer/file-picker.ts` and `agents/reviewer/multi-prompt/code-reviewer-multi-prompt.ts` drop their old { type: 'lastMessage', value: Message[] } unwrapping code to read the string directly. This change lives in the SDK surface (`sdk/CHANGELOG.md`) and agent-runtime/util layers, which is the area covered here; the changelog contains three other independently-worded bullets covering `run()` abort behavior and the `knowledge.md` to `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` file priority shift, which are not reflected in the diff hunks shown for this commit.

The runtime enforces that via `outputForParent` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/agent-output.ts`, which converts a `lastMessage` output to the answer text and a no-output turn to { type: 'error', message: 'No response from agent' }, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts` calls it as `value: outputForParent(output)`. Tests in `agents/__tests__/code-reviewer-multi-prompt.test.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/spawn-agents-message-history.test.ts`, `agents/__tests__/context-pruner.test.ts`, and `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/compact-history.test.ts` assert the new plain-text and error outcomes.

90462035737cade3fe28073b4c1f7a94a49fdb3e.text: When the coding assistant finishes a task and reports back to the main assistant, it now sends just the final written answer as plain readable text instead of a bulky bundle of raw messages and internal thinking. This matters most to developers who build custom helper workflows using the SDK, where one assistant automatically calls another to review code, search files, or research topics. The plain-text result is easier to read and stitch into reports, and if a helper produced no usable answer, the main assistant is told directly that the child had no response, so it can retry or warn instead of parsing an empty message array.

5a8cac584fae64ffc8de9e422c1b5bebc55b30dd.title: Facebook folded into the Instagram / TikTok referral chip
5a8cac584fae64ffc8de9e422c1b5bebc55b30dd.summary: The `tiktok` referral option's label is extended to `Instagram / TikTok / Facebook` and its write-in pattern now matches Facebook spellings, so Facebook answers are counted under the existing `tiktok` id instead of being split or lost. Because this changes how existing write-in answers would be tallied, `ONBOARDING_TALLY_VERSION` is bumped from 3 to 4, which triggers a full rebuild of the stored aggregate in Convex. The id itself is kept deliberately: renaming it would restart the count from zero for no analytical gain.

This is an internal change to the survey's answer tracking, and the company's internal team is rebuilding the stored survey results so the combined option shows an accurate total. You do not need to take any action, and nothing changes for your experience in the app today.

774b13485d0c5b5d1e44ca41217bf35ab37aae2a.title: Add streak status line showing Freebucks credit and reset time
774b13485d0c5b5d1e44ca41217bf35ab37aae2a.summary: The CLI landing screen and chat header now render a new status line beneath the earned Freebucks streak perk note, reporting whether today's bonus +${bonus} Freebucks with your first message each day has landed in the wallet and when the next streak day starts, in the terminal's local time. The line is produced by `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatusForLayout`, which delegates to `getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus` in `common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts`, itself consuming the new `nextResetAt` and `todayCredited` fields on `FreebuffStreakResponse` so clients never guess the boundary, which is why the change exists. A matching height-budget row (`streakBonusRows`) was added to the landing picker layout, and tests assert the rendering and the zone-aware reset copy, including the case where today's credit is in the wallet and the reset time is `3:00 PM` instead of midnight for Pacific readers.

774b13485d0c5b5d1e44ca41217bf35ab37aae2a.text: The Freebuff CLI now shows a short help line under your streak reward note that tells you whether today's Freebucks streak bonus has already landed in your wallet and when the next streak day resets, displayed in your own local time. This only affects Freebucks-paying users on the free tier whose accounts are on the Freebucks meter, and it appears only on the landing screen and chat header where the streak note already shows. You'll notice the extra status line when your streak is 7 days or longer and your terminal is tall enough to fit it; if you're on the meter, the line clarifies whether today's bonus is already credited or still pending your next message, removing confusion for users in time zones like Singapore where the streak day rolls over at 3 PM local time rather than midnight.

81788ea1e9eac6472badf6cdebc4041ccf77751f.title: Sponsored run funnel metadata gains client version and receiver schema
81788ea1e9eac6472badf6cdebc4041ccf77751f.summary: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-client-version.ts` derives a closed `desktop/<version>` or `cli/<version>` string from `Freebuff-Desktop/<v>` and `Freebuff-CLI/<v>` user agents already sent by clients, so the Postgres funnel can tell whether a failure came from a fixed or predating build. `sponsored-run-funnel-metadata.ts` adds a `client_version` field to the strict `sponsoredRunFunnelMetadataSchema` and a `sponsoredRunFunnelMetadataReceiverSchema` that widens only `failure_code` to `other` for unknown codes while refusing unknown keys, so a newer producer talking to an older receiver during Convex-before-Render deploys does not 400 the bridge or drop the outcome. The receiver schema exists because Convex deploys before Render, meaning a rollback reverts Next before Convex and an unknown code would otherwise be lost from Postgres telemetry.

81788ea1e9eac6472badf6cdebc4041ccf77751f.text: The analytics system that tracks sponsored coding sessions now records which version of the Freebuff desktop or terminal app accepted a task, so the team can tell whether a failure came from a recent build (that already includes the fix) or an older one (that predates it). This is internal telemetry for the Freebuff engineering team, stored as a simple label like "desktop/0.0.151" next to each session outcome. You do not see or interact with this change in your daily use of Freebuff, and no action is required.

423da043a3b507289562a7f4bb37014c77c4bf74.title: Tighten release download origin, add terminal text sanitizer
423da043a3b507289562a7f4bb37014c77c4bf74.summary: The release launcher now accepts a NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL override only over https to a codebuff.com or freebuff.com host (or a loopback) with no credentials or query, and refuses any release version that is not strict semver before a download URL or partial-archive path is built, so a steered or malformed version can no longer rewrite a path or escape a directory. A shared `sanitizeTerminalText`/`sanitizeTerminalStrings` in common/src/util/terminal-safe-text.ts is applied at every site that draws remote text to the terminal (partner ads, the sponsor proposal block, gravity ads, API and session error bodies, sponsored-run copy, ad layout, and safeOpen's scheme gate) to strip OSC 52/8, CSI, C0/C1 controls and invisible Unicode before render. The smoke test proves the binary ignores steering .env files and that a non-first-party override is honoured only with CODEBUFF_ALLOW_CUSTOM_APP_URL=1, while the SDK build now runs bundle-source-guard against its sourcemaps and drops them from the published files.
423da043a3b507289562a7f4bb37014c77c4bf74.evidence: New `cli/release-core/launcher.js` adds `RELEASE_ORIGIN_DOMAINS`, `STRICT_RELEASE_VERSION`, `isStrictReleaseVersion`, and tightens `resolveDownloadOrigin` to accept an https override only to a codebuff.com/freebuff.com host (or loopback) with no credentials or query; tests assert it honours a release-host override, ignores other hosts with warnings that never leak the value, and refuses non-semver versions at `stageBinary`/`getPartialArchivePath` before any request. New `common/src/util/terminal-safe-text.ts` exports `sanitizeTerminalText` and `sanitizeTerminalStrings`, imported and applied at every terminal draw site: partner ads (`cli/src/ads/partner-ads.ts`), the sponsored proposal block, `use-gravity-ad`, `codebuff-api`, `freebuff-session-api`, `sponsored-run`, `open-url` (`isOpenableWebUrl`), and `inline-ad-layout.ts`; tests cover OSC 52/8 stripping, CSI, C0/C1, bidi/invisible chars, and `isOpenableWebUrl` accepting only http(s) with no whitespace controls.

changes.what: resolveDownloadOrigin now accepts an https override only to a codebuff.com or freebuff.com host (or a loopback) with no credentials or query, and stageBinary is gated by isStrictReleaseVersion so a non-semver version is refused before any download URL or path is built.

sanitizeTerminalStrings and sanitizeTerminalText are imported from the new common util and applied to partner ad text, gravity ad responses, sponsored-proposal view model and procedure, user-error banner title/error, session API bodies, sponsored-run advertiser name, ad layout destination label,.

Imports ALLOW_CUSTOM_APP_URL_ENV_VAR and asserts dotenv isolation plus host allowlisting: a non-first-party NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL is honoured only when CODEBUFF_ALLOW_CUSTOM_APP_URL=1 is set and ignored otherwise.
New terminal-safe-text.ts exports sanitizeTerminalText and sanitizeTerminalStrings, which the CLI now imports and applies at every remote-text draw site.

Adds FIRST_PARTY_APP_DOMAINS, ALLOW_CUSTOM_APP_URL_ENV_VAR, isCustomAppUrlOptIn, and isFirstPartyRuntimeAppUrl so the host fence is shared by the SDK and the smoke test rather than duplicating the allowlist.
sanitizeAdText is rewritten to delegate to sanitizeTerminalText(input).trim(), so creative cleaning uses the same terminal-safe rules as every other draw site.

423da043a3b507289562a7f4bb37014c77c4bf74.text: The launcher now only trusts https download locations at codebuff.com or freebuff.com (or your local machine), and any update version that isn't a strict format gets rejected before a single byte downloads. Every string that comes from an ad or a server error and gets shown in your terminal is put through a shared cleaner first, so attacker- or advertiser-written escape sequences can no longer rewrite your terminal, hijack your clipboard, or reprogram your keyboard when an ad or error message renders. This is live today.

46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.title: Sponsored runs gain launch-time in-flight sweep and partial-edit undo
46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.summary: Two new CLI modules, `private-state.ts` and `sponsored-run-inflight.ts`, give a sponsored run one file per project and one in-flight record per run so a process that dies before writing a terminal report is reported `failed` by the next CLI launch from any folder, reading the receipts still on disk. The verdict logic moved into the shared `common/src/ads/sponsored-in-place.ts` helpers (`sponsoredInPlaceVerdict`, `sponsoredPartialEditsDiagnostic`, `SPONSORED_PARTIAL_EDITS_COPY`, `SPONSORED_PARTIAL_EDITS_MARKER`), so an interrupted or errored turn that already changed files is now classified as `partial_edits` and reported with the changes still in place, and the dock renders the changed-file count and an Undo for that case instead of only for delivered. The product User-Agent is now sent on every proposal request so the Accept route can set `acceptance.client_version`, and the funnel metadata classifier learned `never_started_*` and `funding_refused` codes plus the partial-edits marker, because the Postgres funnel must now count and classify the runs this sweep reports from the client side.
46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.evidence: New files `cli/src/utils/private-state.ts` and `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run-inflight.ts`; `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` imports `atomicPrivateWrite`/`privateStateFile` from `private-state.ts` (replacing inline file helpers), adds inflight to `SponsoredRunDeps`, calls `sweepSponsoredInflightRuns` during `flushTerminalReports`, and adds `computeStarted`/`active.running` with `withSponsoredModelEventTap` wired in `use-send-message.ts`; `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` adds `SPONSORED_RUNNING_SWEEP_GRACE_MS`/`sponsoredRunningSweepDeadlineMs` and `common/src/ads/sponsored-in-place.ts` adds `SponsoredTurnEnding`/`SponsoredInPlaceVerdict`/`sponsoredInPlaceVerdict`/`SPONSORED_PARTIAL_EDITS_MARKER`/`sponsoredPartialEditsDiagnostic`/`SPONSORED_PARTIAL_EDITS_COPY`; `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-funnel-metadata.ts` adds never-started/funding-refused codes and `client_version`; `cli/src/components/blocks/sponsored-proposal-block.tsx` switches undo rendering to undoable/`undone` driven by `changedFiles`/`undone` so partial-edit failures still offer undo; tests assert orphaned-run reporting and partial-edit UI.
46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.unknowns: The exact consumer of the new `client_version` funnel field beyond the Accept route is not shown in this diff.

changes.what: Added private-state.ts with per-project atomic JSON write helpers and sponsored-run-inflight.ts implementing the per-run in-flight record plus the boot sweep that reports orphaned runs from receipts.

Wired the inflight port into the default deps, reports running on the first model event via withSponsoredModelEventTap, and sweeps in-flight records at flush so dead runs get a failed report from disk.
Wrapped the sponsored run config with withSponsoredModelEventTap so the turn's first model event reports running.
Added productHeaders sending the CLI User-Agent on every proposal request so the Accept route records acceptance.client_version.
Renders the changed-file count and undo for partial-edit failures, not only delivered runs, using changedFiles and undone from the snapshot.

Added in-place verdict helpers and partial-edits copy/marker to sponsored-in-place.ts, the running-sweep grace deadline to sponsored-compute-contract.ts, and never-started/funding-refused failure codes plus client_version to sponsored-run-funnel-metadata.ts.

46813796ce87abb4b405325a7c3deffa3f6f8509.text: The Freebuff CLI now keeps a small 'in-flight' file on your computer the moment a sponsored run starts spending compute, so if Freebuff is killed or the process dies before it can report a final result, the next time you open Freebuff it finds that file and marks the run as failed. The failed run's record includes how many files it changed and points you to /ads:undo to revert them, and the 'running' status is now sent when the run's first actual model work begins rather than when it was queued. This only affects developers who run sponsored tasks in their own working folder via the Freebuff CLI or web/desktop apps that share the same in-place flow.

40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.title: Referral source chips split Instagram TikTok Facebook
40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.summary: The `referral_source` question in `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts` splits the single `tiktok` chip (Instagram / TikTok / Facebook) into separate instagram, `tiktok_only`, and facebook options, retiring the combined `tiktok` id into `retiredOptions` so pre-split answers still tally under it. This happened because a single combined chip could not read cost per activation per platform, so the options were split on 2026-09-28 while the legacy id is preserved for read-time folding. `ONBOARDING_TALLY_VERSION` is bumped to 5 so Convex rebuilds the stored aggregate under the new mapping, `applyOnboardingAnswersToTally` folds retired ids into their successor, and `onboardingSourceProperties` emits the per-channel detail as PostHog person properties via the new `PERSON_PROPERTIES_SET = '$set'` event.
40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts`, the `referral_source` question replaces the single `tiktok` chip (label `Instagram / TikTok / Facebook`) with three chips: instagram, `tiktok_only`, and facebook; the combined `tiktok` id is moved to a new `retiredOptions` array, the `ONBOARDING_OTHER_TEXT_RULES` patterns are split per platform, `ONBOARDING_SOURCE_PROPERTIES` gains entries for the three new ids plus keeps the `tiktok` mapping for the pre-split combined chip, `ONBOARDING_TALLY_VERSION` is bumped from 4 to 5, `emptyOnboardingTally` now includes retired options, and a new `resumableOnboardingAnswers` function and `OnboardingSourceProperties` type/`onboardingSourceProperties` function are exported. In `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`, `PERSON_PROPERTIES_SET = '$set'` is added with a comment that it is PostHog's own person-update event carrying `onboarding_source`.
40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.migration: The Convex stored onboarding aggregate rebuilds automatically on the next deploy due to the ONBOARDING_TALLY_VERSION bump to 5, requiring no manual intervention.
40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.unknowns: The rollout timing of the Convex aggregate rebuild and whether the PostHog person property backfill runs in the same deployment are not shown in the diff.

40cdfe2fc4c97d351a6efa619960adacd714247e.text: The signup survey where developers say how they found Freebuff used to offer one combined option for Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, and now presents three separate choices, one per social platform. Existing answers picked before this change stay counted under their original combined label, so previous data is not erased or relabeled. If you sign up going forward, you'll see Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook as their own selectable options on the 'Where did you hear about Freebuff?' question. No action is required from you.

cef527925490255bcfcfb2dba4a125ae27f63d38.title: Residential proxy notice names the likely cause
cef527925490255bcfcfb2dba4a125ae27f63d38.summary: A new isResidentialProxyOnly helper checks whether ipPrivacySignals contains only res_proxy and anonymous signals, and when true, getFreebuffModelAvailabilityNotice returns a specialized line under the anonymous_network case. This is because a household line listed as a residential proxy is usually the user's own connection enrolled by a bandwidth-sharing app, not a VPN they chose, so generic VPN advice would be misleading. The change adds one concrete branch: isResidentialProxyOnly gates the return of a residential-proxy-specific explanation.
cef527925490255bcfcfb2dba4a125ae27f63d38.evidence: In common/src/util/freebuff-model-availability.ts, an isResidentialProxyOnly helper is added and a new branch in getFreebuffModelAvailabilityNotice under case 'anonymous_network' returns a residential-proxy-specific line when reason.ipPrivacySignals contains only 'res_proxy' and 'anonymous'. The test in common/src/__tests__/freebuff-model-availability.test.ts asserts the returned string 'a line listed only as a residential proxy names the likely cause, not a VPN'.

cef527925490255bcfcfb2dba4a125ae27f63d38.text: When the assistant checks your internet connection and finds it looks like a residential proxy (typically caused by a bandwidth-sharing app on your device rather than a VPN you deliberately chose), it now tells you that directly, instead of giving you the same VPN-focused message. It only affects the model-choice notice that appears next to the model list in the CLI and Desktop app. You'll just see a clearer, more accurate explanation of why some models are hidden, with no action needed on your part.

89abfa4a12586730d5ac44f74b877173a6d2ea56.title: Model compaction recovers reply-text handoffs and ships a completion
89abfa4a12586730d5ac44f74b877173a6d2ea56.summary: Context compaction now accepts a model handoff written as reply text when the model skips the `complete_compaction` tool call, so those runs are sized and installed instead of being discarded. The installed summary may run up to `SUMMARY_OVERRUN_TOLERANCE` (2) times its requested budget as long as the compacted context still lands under `targetTokens`, which keeps oversized but usable handoffs from collapsing into the mechanical fallback. `compactWithModelOrFallback` emits the new `MODEL_COMPACTION_COMPLETED_EVENT` to Axiom with content-free sizes and labels, so a successful model handoff is observable where the runtime is otherwise silent. Two tests covering the agent-runtime package were added to lock the recovery, overrun and reporting behavior.
89abfa4a12586730d5ac44f74b877173a6d2ea56.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts`, `compactWithModel` now recovers a model handoff written as reply text (via `summaryFromReplyText`) instead of only reading the `complete_compaction` tool call, installs summaries that run up to `SUMMARY_OVERRUN_TOLERANCE` (2) times the requested budget as long as the result stays under `targetTokens`, and returns `summarySource`, `summaryTokens`, `summaryBudget`, and sections. In `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`, the new `MODEL_COMPACTION_COMPLETED_EVENT` constant and `MODEL_COMPACTION_COMPLETED_FIELDS` schema (model, agent_run_id, trigger_reason, summary_source, summary_tokens, summary_budget, sections, pre_tokens, post_tokens) were added to the `AxiomOnlyLogEvent` type union and wired into `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent`.
89abfa4a12586730d5ac44f74b877173a6d2ea56.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes `summarySource`/`summaryTokens`/`summaryBudget`/`sections` from the compaction result beyond the new log emission.

changes.what: compactWithModel now recovers a handoff from reply text via summaryFromReplyText, tolerates summaries up to SUMMARY_OVERRUN_TOLERANCE times the budget when the result stays under targetTokens, and returns summarySource, summaryTokens, summaryBudget and sections; compactWithModelOrFallback emits.

Added the MODEL_COMPACTION_COMPLETED_EVENT constant and MODEL_COMPACTION_COMPLETED_FIELDS allowlist (model, agent_run_id, trigger_reason, summary_source, summary_tokens, summary_budget, sections, pre_tokens, post_tokens), added it to the AxiomOnlyLogEvent union, and handled it.

227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.title: Steering messages are framed as mid-turn so models keep the running
227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.summary: Steering messages a user sends while a run is in progress are now wrapped with the user_message_sent_while_working tag and a note, via frameSteeringContent in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts, because a bare message read as the whole new request and models dropped the task they were doing. The CLI computes steersRun in cli/src/hooks/use-chat-streaming.ts as (isStreaming || isChainInProgress) && !sponsoredHoldsQueue and passes it to useQueueUi, which now shows an 'Add to the current task' placeholder instead of the ordinary prompt. formatPrompt in packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts recovers the user's original words with unwrapSteeringText so placeholder injection still works for framed input. Five files changed across CLI and agent-runtime.
227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/util/messages.ts adds STEERING_TAG, STEERING_OPEN, STEERING_CLOSE, STEERING_NOTE, frameSteeringText, unwrapSteeringText, and frameSteeringContent; run-agent-step.ts wraps drained steering messages via frameSteeringContent; templates/strings.ts unwraps them via unwrapSteeringText; use-chat-streaming.ts computes steersRun and passes it to useQueueUi, which renders an 'Add to the current task' placeholder.
227e3fdb0d096fd532844dddbfc0fae41cd4b9d6.unknowns: How the host populates the drainSteeringMessages hook and when steersRun flips mid-stream are not shown in the diff.

changes.what: useChatStreaming derives steersRun from streaming/chain state minus sponsored holds and passes it to useQueueUi.
useQueueUi gains a steersRun parameter that swaps the input placeholder to 'Add to the current task' when a run is in progress and no messages are queued.

fa6729bf4c2f8809a3d8afb07f6e976176db09bc.title: Fix streak bonus copy for east-of-Pacific readers
fa6729bf4c2f8809a3d8afb07f6e976176db09bc.summary: The credited-branch copy in getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus drops the "today's ... is in your wallet" wording, which misled east-of-Pacific users whose credit landed on their previous local day and was spent before reading. The new copy says +${bonus} credited · next +${bonus} with your first message after ${when}, describing the credit's state and the next due moment without claiming it sits in the wallet. The unused-day branch likewise softens from "for today's +${bonus}" to "to earn +${bonus}". The function docstring and inline comment now state the credit is "already credited" rather than "already in the wallet", matching the new wording and the server-driven award rules the comment already cited.
fa6729bf4c2f8809a3d8afb07f6e976176db09bc.evidence: common/src/util/freebuff-streak-line.ts: getFreebuffStreakBonusStatus rewrites its credited branch from Today's +${bonus} is in your wallet · next after ${when} to +${bonus} credited · next +${bonus} with your first message after ${when}, and the not-yet-used branch from Send a message before ${when} for today's +${bonus} to Send a message before ${when} to earn +${bonus}; the function docstring is updated from "already in the wallet" to "already credited". The diff hunks are sourced from the provided source file content and do not include test files.
fa6729bf4c2f8809a3d8afb07f6e976176db09bc.migration: If you render Freebucks streak bonus status, update any copy matching the removed "today's ... is in your wallet" and "for today's" patterns to the new credited/after phrasing.
